text: Virginia Montes. Prosecutors added details to their accusation against Sean Diddy Combs on Thursday, saying the hip-hop star, whose trial is set for May, is accused of sex trafficking at least three women and of dangling someone from a hotel balcony during a two-decade-long organized crime conspiracy. The revised indictment was presented in the Manhattan federal court. Combs' lawyer, Marc Agnifilo, noted that the superseding indictment does not contain new charges. Combs, 55, pleaded not guilty to the sex trafficking charges brought against him after his arrest in September. He remains jailed without bail, awaiting a May 5 trial. In the formal superseding indictment, prosecutors added four years to the duration of the alleged organized crime conspiracy, claiming it lasted from approximately 2004 to 2024. The original indictment stated that the conspiracy began in 2008. The indictment specified that there are at least three female victims, listed only as Victim1, Victim2, and Victim3. Prosecutors said that Combs used his power and prestige as a music mogul to intimidate, threaten, and draw women into his orbit, often under the pretext of a romantic relationship. The indictment says that he then used force, threats, and coercion to compel the victims, including the three women, to participate in commercial sex acts. He allegedly subjected his victims to violence, threats of violence, threats of financial harm and to their reputation, and verbal abuse. On multiple occasions, Combs threw objects and people, in addition to hitting, dragging, choking, and pushing others, he said. On one occasion, Combs hung a victim over the balcony of an apartment. Prosecutors did not provide further information about that accusation. Agnifilo, in a statement, said that Combs remains committed to fighting the charges. The government added the ridiculous theory that two of Mr. Combs' former girlfriends were not girlfriends at all, but prostitutes. At the beginning of this month, the defense attorneys asserted in court documents that the charges described in the indictment were a sexist and puritanical reaction by the prosecutors to consensual sex acts between adults.

In Guatire, the Scientific, Penal and Criminal Investigations Body detained a pedophile who operated through social media. The investigations of the Property Crimes Coordination of the Guarenas Municipal Delegation allowed for the location and capture of Douglas Daniel Bravo Cabeza (32 years old), after it was determined that through social media he was dedicating himself to capturing girls and boys to obtain pornographic material. Through a complaint filed by the mother of one of the affected individuals who detected that this man had contacted her daughter, and through the investigations carried out, it was possible to know that he manipulated children and girls between 11 and 13 years old through the social networks Instagram and Tik Tok, to send them photographs without clothing, as well as to perform video calls to engage in sexting and thus satisfy his improper desires. The arrest took place in the Las Rosas Urbanization, Guatire Parish, Zamora Municipality, Miranda State, where three cellphones and three computers were found to be used as a means of commission. The Cicpc urges parents and guardians to be vigilant about what their children do through social media, to create spaces for family bonding that allow for the prevention of children from being victims of individuals who act outside the law and harm the innocence of our children.

On Friday, January 31, more than a hundred people attending the invitation of the Latin American and Caribbean Ecclesiastical Network on Migration, Displacement, Refuge, and Human Trafficking (Clamor), connected through the Zoom platform to participate in the conversation "Scenarios and Challenges before Trump's Migration Policies," a space that served to analyze the recent measures adopted by the government of the United States and their impact on the migrant population. The event, moderated by Gerardo Cruz, coordinator of the Formation Commission of the Clamor Network, allowed, thanks to the support of specialists, to reflect on the harsh measures of the U.S. migration policy, which includes abuse, massive detentions, and denial of asylum. Restrictions and messages of fear The measures imposed by the Trump government leave concerning restrictions in the area of migration. According to Dylan Corbett, director of the Hope Border Institute, these measures would eliminate the possibility of asylum at the border, increase the number of deportations, lead to more detentions, reduce lawful immigration channels, and eliminate external aid. The director warns that these policies aim to sow fear in the migrant population and leave hundreds of people in a state of vulnerability. He adds that the closure of protection programs and the end of the sensitive locations policy would facilitate raids in places such as hospitals, schools, and churches, which were once considered safe. Photo ADN Celam A looming economic and social crisis Moreover, he highlights the severe economic and social consequences that a massive deportation would bring to the country. When mentioning that 11 million deportees would generate a crisis in the agriculture and construction sectors, as migrants provide the workforce, a crisis that he warns would also extend to countries such as Mexico and Central America, where remittances are a vital part, Corbett proposes the three L rule: legality, logistics, and leadership. He highlights the possibility of challenging these policies in court, budgetary limits for their implementation, and the importance of civil society and the church in defending the rights of migrants. A call to hope and solidarity with migrants.The second to intervene in the conversation was Bishop Mark Seitz of El Paso, Texas, who emphasized the importance of ecumenical collaboration beyond borders to address the migrant crisis. He thanked the Clamor Network for the invitation and recognized the leadership of Cardinal Ramazzini and Bishop Lira, with whom he said he has initiated regular meetings to strengthen pastoral care and the defense of the human rights of those seeking asylum. The prelate pointed out that, although the political scenario is not easy, we must maintain hope. He expressed his concern about dehumanizing policies and influence trafficking because they trample the most vulnerable. He cited theologian Dietrich Bonhoeffer to emphasize that Christian faith must focus on concrete service to the most needy and reaffirmed that Christ is present in migrants. He called on pastoral agents not to fall into cynicism or despair, but to strengthen their commitment to justice and solidarity. CNN Action and Denunciation of False Narratives The bishop of El Paso urged the Church in the United States not to be afraid, but instead, he called on them to protect migrant families through pastoral accompaniment and the provision of legal resources. On the other hand, he denounced the criminalization of migrants, calling it one of the most cruel lies promoted by those in power. He reaffirmed the need to counter this narrative and promote the truth about the positive contributions of migrants to their communities of destination. In addition, he spoke out against the militarization of borders and indiscriminate deportations, considering them incompatible with moral law. Bishop Seitz emphasized the importance of the Regional Pastoral Letter "Lo vio, se acercÃ³ y lo cuidÃ³" (He saw, approached, and cared for it), signed by bishops from Central America, the Caribbean, Mexico, and Canada. He reaffirmed that pastoral work with migrants should not be limited to shelters, but rather extend to places where they suffer exploitation and violence. He also called for caring for pastoral agents who work with migrants and combating corruption that affects those who transit through migration routes. Finally, he urged the Church to study and apply the Pastoral Letter in local contexts, promoting concrete initiatives for the protection and defense of the human rights of migrants.The Migrant Crisis and its Implications On the other hand, Bishop Eugenio Lira of Matamoros and president of the Pastoral of Human Mobility of Mexico, mentioned that all restrictive measures being taken by the administration of the United States violate the fundamental rights of migrants. This situation affects not only those who come in search of a good opportunity, but also touches the stability of families, communities, and destabilizes the economy of this country as well as the countries of origin. In the face of this somber panorama, the religious leader emphasized the importance of analyzing this reality in the light of the Gospel, to avoid falling into despair, anguish, or polarization. Jesus teaches us discernment as a key tool to understand reality and act with faith, hope, and love, he asserted. He called on the community to listen attentively to avoid falling into generalizations, with the purpose of understanding and acting with charity in the face of this migrant crisis. Likewise, he highlighted the need for unity among various actors, such as the Church, government authorities, and civil society, to address the problem in an integrated and just manner. The Commitment to Migrants and a Glimmer of Hope He also highlighted and thanked the efforts of various organizations, ecclesiastical networks, and pastoral agents in favor of migrants. He urged them to continue their service and to keep promoting their integration in society. Additionally, he called on the community to recognize and respect the dignity of each migrant. Far from being a threat, migration can become a development engine if managed with justice and balance, he affirmed. Bishop Lira concluded his intervention by recalling that, although the situation is challenging, it is possible to find solutions from unity and cooperation. He invited the community not to lose hope and to continue working on promoting just policies, social awareness, and the strengthening of support structures for migrants. Citing Jesus, she recalled that in the midst of difficulties, we must maintain our faith and commitment to those who need it most, as only through love and justice can we build a future with greater opportunities for all. Following January 21, the number of migrants leaving through this border has been minimal, with only a few individuals being released from detention centers. This highlights the impact of restrictive policies and uncertainty in the asylum and regulation process for migrants. The nun recognized the tireless work being carried out by the United States Episcopal Conference, reaffirming her commitment to defending the dignity of human beings, to which migrants have rights. She pointed out how the Church has sought dialogue paths with the government in search of fair and compassionate solutions to avoid the continued application of that law. Through the Migration Commission, in which Sister Leticia participates, actions of awareness have been strengthened with priests and the faithful, as well as strategic meetings with local authorities and civil organizations to mitigate the impact of restrictive policies. She mentioned that Hope Border has been key in the formation and accompaniment of migrant and refugee communities. The Church, in turn, remains a beacon of hope and solidarity in the midst of this humanitarian crisis. Hate Speech by Milei Mobilizes Movilh to Argentine Embassy in Santiago The Movement for Homosexual Integration and Liberation (Movilh), protested on Saturday, February 1, in front of the Argentine Embassy in Santiago. Activists left a letter at the site to express their concern about the human rights of LGBTIQ individuals following the hate speech by Argentine President Javier Milei, which they assume to be based on a prejudiced and discriminatory appreciation. The situation is very concerning, as it comes from Argentina's highest authority, who promotes and influences disdain for social diversity, with the corresponding withdrawal of favorable norms or public policies for LGBTIQ rights, the signed letter by the organization's president, Rolando JimÃ©nez, states, addressed to Argentine Ambassador in Chile, Jorge Faurie. The Movilh criticized the controversial speech that Milei offered on January 23 at the World Economic Forum, held in Davos, Switzerland. Milei's words harm human dignity. On the occasion, the official spoke about gender ideology, qualifying it as child abuse and pedophilia, and accused LGBTIQ people of being victimizers and experimenting with children, girls, and adolescents. According to the group, his words harm human dignity due to sexual orientation, gender expression, and gender identity, going so far as to qualify respecting human rights as an imposition. In the letter, it was delivered in the framework of the Antifascist and Antiracist Pride demonstrations, convened worldwide by LGBTIQ and human rights organizations from Argentina. In the writing, Movilh requested that the Argentine State eradicate and prevent hate speech, and recalled that the embassy has been in the past an active collaborator of LGBTIQ rights in Chile.

In the framework of International Day Against Forced Labour, which is celebrated tomorrow, National Labour Inspectorate Superintendent, Michael Guevara Varela, revealed that Sunafil has executed 216,352 prevention actions nationwide in the areas of child and forced labour. He made these statements within the framework of a technical assistance operation to prevent forced labour aimed at employers and workers in economic activities with a high risk profile in the Gamarra commercial district. In this context, the official will present indicators to detect cases of forced labour and tools. He stated that one of the major challenges is the lack of denunciations due to generalised ignorance about what constitutes forced labour and what are the appropriate channels to report it. That is why we are here today, to provide you with the necessary tools that will allow you to identify and report possible cases of forced labor in your surroundings, highlighted the head of the Sunafil. Finally, he emphasized that SUNAFIL has the Specialized Group for the Inspection of Child and Forced Labor (GEIT), a team of highly trained inspectors who not only investigate these cases, but also work closely with the National Police of Peru, the Public Prosecutor's Office, the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, and the Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations.

San Luis PotosÃ­ Legislative Meeting In a working meeting of the First Justice Commission of the LXIV Legislature, the resolution was approved to reform article 110 in its second paragraph of the San Luis PotosÃ­ Penal Code, with the objective of establishing that the crimes of sexual abuse committed against minors are imprescriptible. The resolution also reformed the State Law on Women's Access to a Life Free of Violence, with the objective of incorporating the concept of interculturality, and patrimonial violence. Diputada MarÃ­a Leticia VÃ¡zquez HernÃ¡ndez, president of the Commission, specified that the resolution that reformed article 110 in its second paragraph of the San Luis PotosÃ­ Penal Code, establishes that the crimes of rape, statutory rape, femicide, qualified homicide, homicide due to family ties, kidnapping, and enforced disappearance of persons, are imprescriptible. Similarly, the crimes of sexual abuse, sexual harassment, sexual harassment, and the illicit dissemination of images will be imprescriptible when the victim is a minor. In the explanatory section, it is established that according to the National Survey on the Dynamics of Relations in Homes ENDIREH 2021 of the INEGI, 49.7% of women aged 15 and over stated that they had suffered some form of sexual violence throughout their lives, and 23.3% in the last 12 months. The survey indicates that 12.6% of women aged 15 and over stated that they had suffered sexual abuse in childhood. Regarding the aggressors, 20.8% were identified as uncles or aunts, 17.4% as cousins or cousins, 8.1% as other relatives, 7.1% as brothers or sisters, 6.5% as stepfathers or stepmothers, 5.2% as fathers, 3.6% as grandparents or grandmothers, 0.6% as mothers, and 15.8% as non-relatives. It is evident that sexual crimes committed against children, girls, and adolescents are one of the worst forms of violence against childhood and adolescence. Despite being a growing problem worldwide, most cases go undetected and unreported. Unlike physical violence, whose diagnosis depends on the possibility of seeing the injuries, the detection of girls, boys, and adolescents who are or have been victims of sexual crimes depends on their testimony to know about it. In most cases, there are no physical injuries that serve as evidence of the aggression, nor are there witnesses, as the perpetrator usually commits the crime without anyone observing. The girls, boys, and adolescents who are victims of sexual violence often keep silent due to fear, guilt, powerlessness, or shame, so that only the passage of time allows them to speak about what happened, about the aggression suffered, as humiliation and the fear of being stigmatized accompany them throughout their lives. Therefore, it is necessary to guarantee the broadest protection of the human rights of girls, boys, and adolescents, in particular, their right of access to justice at any time, without any room for impunity derived from the prescription of the crime. The First Chamber of Justice also approved the report that reforms articles 8 in its XIV fraction, and 30 in its I fraction, and adds articles 3 in its VII Bis fraction, and 4 in its XII Bis fraction of the Law of Access of Women to a Life Free of Violence of the State of San Luis PotosÃ­, to read as follows: Article 3, fraction VII Bis Interculturality The intercultural approach is based on the recognition and respect for existing cultural differences, under the conception that cultures can be different from each other but equally valid, without any superior or inferior cultures existing. It is oriented towards addressing the particularities of indigenous women, Afro-descendant women, and other differentiated ethnic groups and their relationship with the dominant society, beyond the coexistence of cultures.Article 4th, clause XII Bis. Patrimonial Violence. Any act or omission that affects the victim's survival. It manifests in the transformation, removal, destruction, retention, or diversion of personal objects, documents, property, and valuables, patrimonial rights, or economic resources intended to meet their needs and can encompass damage to the victim's common or personal property.Article 8th, clause XIV Access to comprehensive, intercultural, multidisciplinary, transversal, and under the same roof attention in women's justice centers. Article 30, Section I. Train the Investigating Police, prosecutors of the Public Ministry, experts, and all personnel responsible for justice procurement to attend, with a gender perspective, interculturality, with full respect for women's human rights, and in accordance with specialized protocols, cases of violence against women, permanently evaluating their performance. The assessments will be put to consideration of the Full Congress of the State for their analysis and voting.

In a violent incident recorded at the Huamancaca prison in Huancayo, an inmate identified as Royber Husinga Vivanco (40 years old), convicted of sexual assault, was brutally murdered in the morning of Saturday. The alleged perpetrator of the homicide is Alex Huarcaya Laura (23 years old), who is serving a sentence for aggravated robbery. READ MORE Huancayo Detains Shaman Accused of Sexual Abuse During Flower Bath According to initial reports, the crime occurred around 11:30 a.m., following a fight between the two inmates in Pavilion 3, a maximum-security area of the prison facility. During the altercation, Huarcaya Laura allegedly used a sharp object to attack Husinga Vivanco, causing a deep cut in his jugular, resulting in rapid blood loss and his subsequent death. Violent Attack with Sharp Object According to witnesses within the prison, the confrontation between the inmates escalated rapidly and turned into a deadly fight Laura Huarcaya, in a act of extreme violence, allegedly inflicted a fatal wound to the neck of her victim, leaving them severely injured. Despite the efforts of some inmates to alert the prison authorities, Husinga Vivanco bled to death in a few minutes, losing their life on the spot. The agents of the National Penitentiary Institute (INPE) intervened immediately and isolated the suspected murderer, who was placed at the disposal of the authorities for the corresponding investigations. Investigation in progress After the crime, the Peruvian National Police (PNP) and the Public Ministry arrived at the prison to initiate the proceedings and investigate the circumstances of the murder. It is worth mentioning that the detention took place in the Azcapotzalco municipality and is part of an ongoing investigation into crimes related to sexual exploitation and human trafficking. Nuvia N The Venezuelan woman was identified as Nuvia N, and is allegedly linked to a case registered in July 2024 in the CuauhtÃ©moc municipality. According to investigations by the Investigation Police of Crimes Related to Human Trafficking, the woman, along with other people of the same nationality, would have been involved in the sexual exploitation of a foreign woman. According to the investigations, the victim was pressured into providing sex services to pay off a debt that she allegedly incurred after seeking help to reach the United States. The victim was rescued during a raid conducted at a property located in the mentioned municipality. The Loitador Case, a malicious Argentine case determined that the alleged case of labor exploitation should be subject to their laws because the fishing vessel was in the islands during the commission of the crime. Lara GraÃ±a E. Thiam, a Senegalese national, boarded the Vigevan fishing vessel Loitador on February 15, 2017. She did so in Cabo Blanco, Mauritania, after flying from her country of origin. According to the proceedings in the case being investigated by the Federal Court of Caleta Olivia, in the Santa Cruz province of Argentina, 14 compatriots were on board as sailors, in addition to a Mauritanian and 11 Indonesians. On June 5, and after four months of forced labor on board, according to the accusation of the Public Ministry, she was evacuated by a helicopter from the Argentine Naval Prefecture with a severe chest pain, loss of vision, and difficulty breathing. It was the doctor who treated the 35-year-old crew member at the time, who filed a complaint that led to an arrest warrant against the captain of the fishing vessel, a 56-year-old Spanish national, who was executed last December. However, the reason why the country's justice system has persisted in these complex proceedings does not stem from the fact that the evacuation took place within its 200 nautical miles of jurisdictional waters. Here, a patriotic issue has been determinant. Almost three months after E. Thiam's evacuation, the federal prosecutor of Caleta Olivia, Lucas Colla, ruled that it corresponds to the application of Argentine penal law to investigate a case of possible human trafficking for labor exploitation on board the Loitador. The reason lies in the Malvinas (or Falklands, which is the denomination adopted by the territory itself), which are claimed as Argentine property in its Constitution. In particular, Colla explained that the Falkland Islands, South Georgia, and the South Sandwich Islands are part of Argentine territory over which the Argentine Republic holds sovereign rights, so it is not necessary to highlight that the Argentine legal system applies to these territories. The thread that the prosecutor wove between the Loitador and the Falklands is that the ship, owned by Profesionals Pesqueros SA, arrived in Port Stanley twice during the same 2017, in March and April, a time period in which the alleged crime of the supposed case of human trafficking for labor exploitation would have taken place.Because, indeed, the Vigo trawler entered Argentine waters only to proceed with the evacuation of the sailor and when he was already gravely ill, according to the medical report. The Loitador was outside the 200-mile limit when it requested medical assistance and was authorized to enter Argentine territory to accelerate the rescue operation. That these alleged forced labor jobs are being investigated in Argentina is due to the fact that, in the end, and according to the Caleta Olivia Prosecutor's Office, they were parallel to those two scales carried out in the Malvinas. The company owning the ship has flatly rejected the sailor's accusations, and since the moment when the Argentine justice decided to initiate the investigations under the assumption of a labor exploitation case. It even alluded to a political issue due to the link with the Malvinas. text: Four men who an indictment says espouse neo-Nazi beliefs have been charged with child exploitation in a case in which they allegedly coerced 16 children, including two in San Bernardino County, to create child pornography and other images that harmed themselves, the U.S. Department of Justice said Thursday, Jan. 30. Members of CVLT, pronounced cult and apparently not an acronym, prepared the children to produce degrading images, including exposing the victims to extreme and violent content, a DOJ press release said. CVLT targeted vulnerable victims, such as those with mental health issues or a history of sexual abuse, the Justice Department said. Members of CVLT participated in their child exploitation activities online because they wanted to create an army of sadistic followers, the indictment said. The victims were encouraged to participate in dehumanizing acts, including cutting and consuming their hair, drinking their urine, hitting themselves, calling themselves racial slurs, and using razors to carve the names of CVLT members into their skin, the Department of Justice said. CVLT members coerced victims into attempting to take their own lives during a live video broadcast, according to the statement. CVLT members exposed children to extreme and violent content, including women who were raped and animals that were tortured to death, the federal agency said. When the victims resisted or threatened to tell their parents or authorities, CVLT members would threaten them, and in some cases, they did, distribute compromising photos and videos of the victims to their family and friends. Colin John Thomas Walker, 23, of Bridgeton, New Jersey, and Clint Jordan Lopaka Nahooikaika Borge, 41, of Pahoa, Hawai, were arrested on Thursday and charged with one count of participating in a child exploitation enterprise. The indictment also charges two men currently in custody with participating in a child exploitation enterprise: Rohan Sandeep Rane, 28, of Antibes, France, and Kaleb Christopher Merritt, 24, of Spring, Texas. If found guilty as charged, the defendants in this case could face a minimum of 20 years to life in prison. The San Bernardino County Sheriff's Department and the Los Angeles Police Department were among the agencies that assisted in the investigation. Originally published January 30, 2025 at 5:18 PM PST

All of Hispanic America is experiencing an unprecedented surge in organized crime. Spain, which had for years had under control the phenomenon, has today suffered a relapse like almost all of the Latin American region. Spain faces significant challenges related to narcotics trafficking and human trafficking. In 2023 alone, authorities identified at least 1,466 victims of human trafficking and exploitation crimes, of which 18 were minors. The vast majority of the victims were women from Latin American countries who had been brought under deception or extortion to Europe. Just a few days ago, Spanish authorities dismantled a Chinese organized crime group, known as Tian Xia She, dedicated to trafficking women for prostitution in Spain, Greece, and the United States. The worrying thing is that even the Spanish elites do not fully understand that they are only discovering the tip of the iceberg of a much larger phenomenon, which of course puts back at the center the authoritarian equation that is putting liberal democracies of Western civilization in jeopardy, more accentuated organized crime with migration. The Venezuela led by NicolÃ¡s Maduro is today the main epicenter of transnational crime in Hispanic America. Much has been talked about the Aragua Train in recent times. Its expansion has been so voracious in the region that practically any crime or violent event seems to bear the seal of this group. One of the first measures taken by the newly installed Trump Administration was to designate the Aragua Train as a terrorist organization, a fundamental step in the fight against this structure. Several tentacles of the Aragua Train have been detected in Spain in recent months. The Maduro regime, as is customary, has attempted to shift the blame, accusing me and other leaders of heading a human trafficking network in conjunction with the Aragua Train. An absurd accusation taken out of context that, obviously, no one believes. However, the regime's true objective is to divert attention from its direct relationship with these transnational organized crime groups. How the Aragua Train Emerged Its birth and expansion are directly linked to the power structure and criminal governance in Venezuela. This gang originated in the notorious TocorÃ³n prison, which for years functioned as the operation center of this organization. Despite the regime denying the existence of the Aragua Train for a long time, going so far as to have the Maduro cabinet minister label its existence as a fiction created by the media, last year the dictatorship was forced to acknowledge it after the TocorÃ³n operation. In that operation, images were revealed showing the privileges enjoyed by the prisoners, including discos, pools, children's parks, casinos, restaurants with terraces, bars, liquor stores, ATMs, and even a zoo with jaguars and pumas, all financed with money from criminal activities. Among their activities, they stand out for extortion, kidnapping, human trafficking, drug trafficking, gold trafficking, prostitution networks, border crossing control, homicides, gun sales, and money laundering, among other crimes. The growth of the Aragua Train has been exponential, even surpassing the most dangerous criminal groups in the world. According to various investigations, the Venezuelan megaband would have presence in countries such as Colombia, Brazil, Chile, Argentina, Ecuador, Peru, Costa Rica, Panama, Mexico, the United States, and even Spain, where last year they captured a relative of the leader of the criminal group. A report from the US Department of Homeland Security identifies members of this organization in 16 US states and notes that there are 100 ongoing federal investigations related to the Aragua Train. In a statement published to Ringside News, Grant's legal team asserts that they have obtained previously unseen text and voice messages from McMahon, allegedly showing that he forced her into sexual acts and offered her to other men, including WWE talent. A Graphic Text Message from McMahon Detailed His Fantasy of Seeing Multiple Men Surround Grant and Physically Destroy Her. Another Message Supposedly Showed McMahon Declaring He Had the Power to Organize Grant's Sexual Encounters. McMahon Supposedly Filmed Grant Naked and Sent the Video to John Laurinaitis Without Her Knowledge or Consent. The WWE's 2022 Internal Investigation into McMahon's NDAs Supposedly Never Interviewed Grant, Despite Her Involvement in the Scandal. This case is far from over, and with new incriminating evidence emerging, the legal battle could become even more chaotic. The United States Coast Guard has recently deported 12 Cubans who attempted to enter the country illegally by sea. These Cubans were intercepted in two separate groups while using makeshift boats for their crossing. Once taken aboard Coast Guard vessels, the migrants were returned to Cuba. This situation highlights the zero-tolerance policy implemented by the Trump administration, which aims to prevent illegal entry into the country. Although during the Biden administration, Cubans intercepted at sea were also deported, the chances of success for those attempting this type of crossing have significantly decreased. The Coast Guard has warned that it will increase its presence in the area to prevent maritime migration attempts, especially from countries like Cuba and Haiti. This implies that the chances of success for those attempting to reach the United States are very limited. Even if they manage to set foot on land, the probabilities of being able to regularize their situation are scarce, as it is most likely they will be arrested and deported. In a statement, the Coast Guard reported that the crew of the patrol boat Isaac May repatriated these Cubans after two attempts at irregular maritime immigration. On January 19, a marine air operations crew notified the Key West Watch of a raft with illegal immigrants approximately 21 miles south of Long Key. In another incident, a good Samaritan reported that they had rescued seven foreigners from a damaged vessel 50 miles southwest of Cuba. Lieutenant Commander John B, a public affairs officer for Coast Guard District 7, emphasized that his commitment is to protect the United States by securing maritime borders and preventing illegal entry into the country. The warning has been reiterated not to attempt to cross the sea, as it is an extremely perilous journey. If intercepted, foreign nationals are processed to determine their identity and nationality, and they are provided with food, water, shelter, and basic medical care before being repatriated. It is essential to note that those who attempt to enter the United States by sea in an illegal manner will be repatriated to their country of origin or the country from which they departed. This means that if a Cuban leaves from the Bahamas, for example, they could be returned to the Bahamas before the country attempts to repatriate them to Cuba. The Coast Guard has also requested that mariners and recreational boat users report maritime illicit activities through the VHF marine radio on channel 16. It is recalled that, although the intention may be to help Cuban or Haitian rafters at sea, no assistance can be provided that implies taking them to the United States, as this could be considered human trafficking and entail serious legal consequences.

text: The European Parliament's Committee on Foreign Affairs condemned systematic human rights violations and abuses perpetrated by the Cuban regime, particularly the medical missions. Created January 31, 2025 7:59 am Updated January 31, 2025 12:03 pm The European Parliament's Committee on Foreign Affairs included, for the first time, in its annual report, a condemnation of the Cuban medical brigades, assured MEP Antonio LÃ³pez-IstÃºriz White on social media. That Committee condemned systematic human rights violations and abuses perpetrated by the Cuban regime, particularly the medical missions, present in some European countries, which constitute a form of slavery and forced labor, they added. The amendment to include this topic was approved on Thursday LÃ³pezIstÃºriz White stated that the export conditions of Cuban medical supplies violate Article 5 of the European Union's Charter of Fundamental Rights (EU), which prohibits forced or compulsory labor, as well as Article 4 of the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and the Conventions of the International Labour Organization (ILO). The MEP recalled the work of the organization Prisoners Defenders, which filed a complaint with the International Criminal Court in 2019 for human rights violations, after collecting the testimonies of over 1,200 Cuban doctors. For the first time, Antonio LÃ³pezIstÃºriz White (EPP) EP_ForeignAff, introduced in the annual report that summarizes and conditions European foreign policy, this complaint about the well-known Cuban medical brigades. In previous occasions, several European Parliament members have denounced the exploitation of Cuban doctors. At the end of 2023, a complaint was made by doctors from the island sent to Italy under a communist regime agreement with the president of the Calabria region. In the document, the politicians recalled the multiple reports from organizations such as Human Rights Watch (HRW), Human Rights Foundation (HRF) and several resolutions from the European Parliament, which have denounced the violation of human rights and the work of doctors in the context of similar contracts. These institutions classify Cuban medical missions or brigades as a labor exploitation scheme and a human trafficking operation. More recently, in January 2024, the United Nations accused the states of Cuba, Spain, Italy, and Qatar, as well as the company MSC Cruises, of promoting the so-called Cuban work missions abroad. According to the report revealed by PD, the accusation emphasizes the threats, harassment, and sexual violence suffered by doctors, nurses, and other professionals at the hands of Cuban regime officials. Regarding Italy, they emphasized the forced labor situation driven by Roberto Occhiuto, President of Calabria. In response, the then Vice-President of the European Parliament, Dita CharanzovÃ¡, reacted to the report saying: "This UN accusation brings to light very serious violations from forced labor to contemporary slavery, harassment, sexual violence, and threats, to physical violence. Once again, it is evident that the Cuban regime systematically and unpunishedly violates the human rights of its people. From the European Parliament, we must support this effort by the United Nations and Prisoners Defenders, and closely follow the case. Additionally, calls have been renewed for that country to take the lead in the fight against Cuban medical brigades, denouncing them as a modern system of slavery. Congressman Mark Green and Eric Patterson, executive director of the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation, expressed this in an article published in The Hill. It's time for the nations of the world to tell Cuba that its medical professionals should not be exploited, abused, or threatened, and the United States should spearhead the initiative, they wrote. Cuban healthcare professionals are subjected to abusive working conditions, their passports are confiscated upon arrival in destination countries, they receive minimum wages, and they are under strict surveillance. Moreover, many are forced to provide information to the Cuban regime and manipulate healthcare statistics. By May 2024, the Cuban regime had 54 brigades with a total of more than 22,600 professionals in various countries. Karla PÃ©rez Cuban journalist temporarily residing in Costa Rica, after being expelled from the UCLV, continues her studies at the Universidad Latina. She has collaborated with alternative media outlets such as 14ymedio, Diario de Cuba, Tremenda Nota, and Revista Late.

After the complaint was filed regarding the alleged sexual abuse of seven minors from a municipal preschool in ParanÃ¡, which is being investigated by the Public Prosecutor's Office (MPF), attorneys Sofia Dumon and Lara Linari issued a statement to clarify the current state of the investigation. In an operation, alias Jorge and Ricardo Aguayo were detained, who stored and distributed child abuse material through the Viber platform. The Cybercrime Investigation Directorate, through a joint operation led by the Child Cyber Protection Department (DEPCPI) of the Peruvian National Police (PNP), has successfully dismantled an international and dangerous criminal gang dedicated to distributing child pornography in Callao and the Lima district of Comas. These are people who specialize in exporting and importing child pornography through technological means, phones, and the internet, according to PNP General JosÃ© Zavala. INVESTIGATION UNDERWAY FOR MARINES, NARCOS BAND WHO WERE GOING TO SMUGGLE 251 KILOS OF COCAINE TO BRAZILOn January 30th in the morning, Jorge Armando Ancho ChÃ¡vez (42), alias Jorge, was detained in flagrante delicto at his apartment located on Micaela Bastidas Avenue in Comas. Investigations allowed for his identification as the person responsible for storing and distributing a significant amount of child abuse material on various Viber groups, causing harm to minors who are still being identified. The PNP also apprehended Ricardo Aparicio Sarnaque Cornejo, who used the alias Ricardo Aguayo on Viber for distributing pornographic material. According to the alert from the International Organization for the Protection of Children, the detained individuals' mobile phones are linked to a child abuse network. They are looking for a driver who ran over a child in Callao and covered up the car's license plate in front of a security camera. Ricardo Aparicio Sarnaque Cornejo is linked to a network of child pornography. Now we are seeing the commercialization and possession of this pornographic material. We need to determine if he himself produced it in order to try to identify the victims, the general added.Help lines If you are or know someone who has been affected or involved in cases of domestic or sexual violence, contact the Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations' free Line 100. There is concern among organizations and human rights defenders about unfounded accusations that seek to obstruct access to justice for women and girls in the CDMX. Mexico City, January 31, 2025. Due to the recent unfounded accusations that aim to discredit her and remove her from her position, 30 civil society organizations and 100 human rights defenders support Sayuri Herrera RomÃ¡n, General Coordinator of Gender Crimes Investigation at the Attorney General's Office of the City of Mexico. The women's, feminist, and victims' movement shows concern about the actions against Herrera RomÃ¡n, as the gender-based political violence against her reflects a resistance to change and an attempt to maintain a system that protects aggressors and perpetuates impunity. In a statement, they point out that in recent days, acts of violence and corruption have been made public in cases of violence against women and girls and boys within the family setting, in which the aggressors use their political and economic power to manipulate and corrupt the prosecution and administration of justice system. This situation is considered a strategy to further violate women, denouncing them for other crimes, taking away their daughters and sons, and using institutions to ensure their impunity. This form of operation by the aggressors is not new and is not exclusive to those with political or economic power, as the patriarchy also performs its function against the most vulnerable. In some media outlets, without any basis, there has been an attempt to involve Sayuri Herrera RomÃ¡n in these acts of corruption, without conducting a thorough analysis of what is really happening within the Prosecutor's Office and even within the judiciary of the City of Mexico in these cases where aggressors are favored and access to justice is hindered for women and their daughters and sons. Groundless accusations have been made, as is generally the case with women, to a violence against the family of our colleague Sayuri Herrera RomÃ¡n. In this case, unscrupulous media outlets have disseminated images of a minor and sensitive information about her private life, violating all parameters of protection towards girls and boys. The public statement notes that on March 8, 2020, Sayuri Herrera RomÃ¡n was appointed as the first Special Prosecutor for the Investigation of the Crime of Feminicide in Mexico City, whose candidacy was supported by civil society organizations specialized in access to justice with human rights standards, rural development work, unionized workers and workers' rights organization, as well as defense of the rights of girls and children, as well as the support of numerous women's collectives that accompany victims and family members of victims of gender-based violence against women in this city, the statement notes. Sayuri Herrera RomÃ¡n, a highly distinguished professional, has carried out a solidary and persevering work as a legal advisor to Araceli Osorio, mother of Lesvy BerlÃ­n, murdered on the Ciudad Universitaria campus of UNAM in May 2017. Some of the tangible results of her work as head of the Feminicide Prosecutor's Office are the advancement of investigations, the increase in the number of judicial proceedings, the reclassification and prosecution of long-standing cases that were initially considered as suspected suicides or accidents, as well as the increase in the percentage of violent deaths of women accredited as feminicides. This led her to be appointed as the General Coordinator of Investigation of Gender Crimes and Attention to Victims, in charge of prosecutor's offices for sexual crimes, family violence, human trafficking, and child, adolescent, and girl trafficking, as well as victim assistance centers. The signers call on the authorities, particularly the new attorney general, to ensure the safety of Sayuri Herrera and her family, and to value the results of her work in the Prosecutor's Office. That each of the prosecutor's offices that make up the CoordinaciÃ³n de delitos de gÃ©nero (Gender Crimes Coordination) be strengthened through a deep evaluation of their operational conditions, from their attention spaces, the workload assigned to each staff member, to the professionalization and updating of all their personnel, including the forensic area, and ensuring the respect of labor rights and the guarantee of dignified and reinforced conditions in the face of this work of great impact on those who carry it out, and of priority for society. Additionally, they state that in the cases in which complaints of supposed corruption are presented, corresponding investigations should be carried out to provide legal certainty to all parties, sanctioning the public servants responsible and clarifying the situation when the accusations are unfounded. They demand that measures be taken to prevent these practices in which the Prosecutor's Office is used to fabricate crimes against women who are victims of family violence, including their children, through coordination and control mechanisms, applying a gender perspective and an integral analysis of the context of all parties involved. Finally, they explain that this type of act against Sayuri Herrera RomÃ¡n and other prosecutors clearly falls under political violence against women, recognized in the General Law of Access to a Life Free of Violence for Women.

Illegal mining can produce $12 million in annual profits for this criminal group, the main Colombian narco-trafficking cartel, added SolÃ­s. In the operation, carried out on Thursday and attended by a collaborator of AFP and other local media, seven Panamanians and three Colombians were arrested. The network, in whose dismantling the Colombian army also collaborated, operated at least two illegal mines in the headwaters of the Mangle River, 5 km from the border with Colombia. text: We investigated human trafficking at sea, explains the prosecutor handling the case opened in Argentina against the captain of a Galician fishing vessel PESCA Y MARISQUEO Lucas Colla confirms sufficient indications of labor exploitation when the Loitador offloaded a crew member with advanced malnutrition on February 1, 2025. Updated at 0440 h. The detention in Spain of the captain of the Galician vessel Loitador, from the company Profesionales Pesqueros, caused a stir after being released on bail after making a statement. He is accused of human trafficking for labor exploitation, awaiting a decision on his extradition to Argentina, where the case is being processed. The Voz de Galicia spoke with federal prosecutor Lucas Colla, in charge of the investigation. How the case is proceeding We are waiting for the extradition decision to be resolved in Spain. In what evidence were they based on to request the arrest of the captain of the fishing boat The case begins with the disembarkation of a sailor (Colla clarifies that he will not mention the name of the victim) who was on board the ship The doctor who treated him filed a complaint based on the vulnerability indicators that person had and that's when we intervened to see if there was a situation of human trafficking We took a testimonial interrogation from the person, gathered evidence, had communications with the International Labor Organization that passed on information about the maritime work standards, and together with the Prosecutor's Office for Human Trafficking and Exploitation of Persons, we elaborated what ended up being the request for an investigation and the formulation of charges This was in 2019, but it wasn't until February 2024 that we received a positive reception from the court, and it's there that the person is ordered to be summoned in order to be informed of what is being investigated and to exercise their defense. The ship had a license to navigate in the Falkland Islands and fished beyond the 200-mile limit, that's a fact. I've understood that yes, but we didn't enter into analyzing the issue of licenses, that is, its administrative situation linked to the exploitation of the fishing resource. However, on the fiscal website fiscales.gob.ar, it is cited and it is said why it is valid to apply Argentine law in a case of trafficking on board a ship that docked in the Falkland Islands. Yes, but one thing are the licenses and another is the jurisdictional issue. We analyze the factual situation, and here what is being investigated is a fact in which a person is a victim of a situation of slavery at sea. But if the ship had remained outside the 200-mile limit and had not touched the Falkland Islands, they could have intervened. Yes, due to universal jurisdiction issues. There are situations that are resolved by the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (Convemar), and one of the ways to control a ship is based on whether there are sufficient indications of a situation, for example, of slavery. In this case, we acted because we had access to a victim of an incident that, under Argentine law standards, is equivalent to forced labor or slavery. The company claims that there is a lack of evidence and that it is a political matter, rather than a legal one, because it involves the issue of the Falkland Islands. I am not going to give my opinion, but the political issue is unrelated to this, and I think it is a way to divert and desensitize the situation.We have a person who was recruited in February in Cabo Blanco (Mauritania), and who was part of a crew where the only two people of Spanish origin were the ship's senior officers, the rest were from Indonesia, Mauritania, and Senegal. There were seven Senegalese sailors who were sought out and taken to the port of departure, and made to sign their labor contracts once on board. This person stated that they were not provided with suitable clothing to work in freezing cargo holds, that everything was done without an interpreter, and that the contract was signed in Spanish. There are a multitude of elements that attest to a situation of vulnerability that was exploited for labor exploitation. Thus, the issue of jurisdiction can be discussed in terms of insufficient evidence, we are not condemning anyone, nor are we in a trial instance. Ramadan had begun eight days earlier, and the doctor spoke of advanced malnutrition Sources close to the company denied a lack of food supply on board and even attributed the state of the Muslim sailor to Ramadan. It is suggested that the sailor's health deteriorated due to fasting during Ramadan, not because he was not given food. Yes, but Ramadan had started eight days earlier, and the doctor's report spoke of an advanced state of malnutrition, so if that is going to be the defense's argument, we will see. The same if they have evidence that this person did not want to consume because they were fasting. Precisely, what we are trying to do is bring the accused person to exercise their defense. What do they know about the life of this crew member of the Loitador? The victim was immediately returned to their country of origin through a national rescue program, in accordance with the obligations assumed by the Argentine state in relation to the Convention on Combating the Trafficking of Persons. That program, together with the International Organization for Migration, worked on returning them to their country of origin and accessing a labor reintegration program.

text: After Judge Ariel Lijo's attempts to dismiss the human trafficking charges involving businessman Alejandro Roemmers, the case continues with revealing testimonies that further incriminate the accused. A key testimony I don't know how I feel every time I hear the government insisting on Lijo for the Court.. Roberto Mazzoni (@robermazzoni) Judge who took statements with a fake ID from the accused for HUMAN TRAFFICKING Alejandro Roemmers.. The evidence speaks for itself, this is a crime pic.twitter.com/URL23, 2024 The complaint, which had been filed two years ago by Roberto Mazzoni from Mar del Plata, gained new momentum last July when the Justice ordered the investigation to move forward. Now, the testimonies of those who were lured by Roemmers' entourage are beginning to be known. One of the most compelling testimonies is that of a witness with a reserved identity who recounts how he met Roemmers in 2007 at a dinner in Mar del Plata According to his statement, Roemmers arrived accompanied by his then-partner, a young man known as the Indian, and another minor, nicknamed Coquito, all aboard a Ferrari. Subsequently, the group moved to a casino, where the witness rejected a money offer to play. Later, one of Roemmers' companions proposed spending the night with the businessman in exchange for a sum of money, an offer that was declined. The testimony also mentions that among the young people, there was information circulating that Roemmers offered contracts of $10,000 monthly, as well as gifts and vehicles, to those who accepted being part of his inner circle and maintaining relationships with him. Private trips and parties Days after the encounter in Mar del Plata, the witness participated in a trip to Calamuchita, CÃ³rdoba, along with his friend Abel and other people linked to Roemmers. The trip included a stop at the entrepreneur's residence in San Fernando, province of Buenos Aires, from where they departed on a private plane to CÃ³rdoba. In Calamuchita, a helicopter awaited them, taking them to Roemmers' ranch, a luxurious property that, according to the witness, featured restaurants, a private lake, and a cinema. During the journey, the witness received money in an envelope as a gift from Roemmers, which reinforces the pattern of paying young people to remain in the entrepreneur's circle. He also describes the existence of a staff of young people who were offered these benefits in exchange for sexual favors. In another episode, the witness was invited to a gay party in an exclusive penthouse on Avenida Del Libertador, where prominent entrepreneurs attended. According to his account, Roemmers handed out $10,000 in cash to the young people present to buy clothes and get ready for the occasion. At the party, the witness felt exposed like an object and received advances from various businessmen, including one linked to the Techint group. The next day, at Roemmers' residence pool, one of the businessmen attempted to approach the witness again, who rejected the situation and decided to cut off all contact with the group. Additionally, he mentioned that drugs were a regular part of these gatherings, although he did not participate in their consumption.A structured recruitment network The witness also stated that Roemmers' staff was constantly being replaced, with a waiting list of young people interested in joining Roemmers' circle. SAN ANTONIO A 37-year-old woman, Desiree Hamm of San Diego, California, was found guilty by a jury of being the first violently sex trafficker in Texas. The verdict was delivered on Thursday in Comal County Court. According to reports, in late 2009, 22-year-old Hamm began online relationships with two underage victims. Hamm exploited her victims after spending hundreds of hours on the phone and computer with them. Additionally, after sending the minors secret cell phones, computers, and gifts, Hamm watched them through a web camera. Within months, Hamm coordinated the kidnapping with another adult woman who drove from San Diego to Comal County and transported the minors back to California. During the month the minors were under Hamm's physical control, she committed a series of individual and joint sexual assaults against them. When the minors' families became aware that they were missing, the phone records identified Hamm's phone number and the authorities were able to arrest her. Hamm pleaded guilty on August 4, 2011, and was sentenced to 20 years in prison for 13 counts of child sexual abuse, aggravated kidnapping with intent to violate and sexually abuse, and child molestation.

United States. Raids against undocumented migrants in the United States have resulted in the detention of more than 5,500 people in various cities, according to data from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). It has been reported that during the first two weeks of President Donald Trump's mandate, these operations have intensified in key cities such as New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago. Unlike previous administrations, ICE has opted to disclose daily arrest figures nationwide, even highlighting profiles of detainees. Through the social network X, the agency has highlighted information about 21 people, some with name, photo, and nationality, and others identified only by the crimes they are accused of, ranging from driving under the influence of substances to child sexual abuse. You may be interested in reading Donald Trump resumes border wall reconstruction in Tijuana Authorities have avoided providing a detailed breakdown of the arrests by nationality or exact location, leaving regional offices to decide whether or not to share the data. For example, in Texas, 84 arrests have been confirmed in Dallas, but local media have reported operations in San Antonio, Austin, and Houston. The actions in Chicago and New York have been especially visible due to the presence of Border Czar Tom Homan and Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem. The Trump government has justified these operations by claiming that the detained migrants pose a threat to security, although many of the arrested individuals do not have a criminal record and have reported abuse in the procedures.

What did he say about the whereabouts of minor Loan Danilo PeÃ±a? Something did not go well with (Carlos) PÃ©rez for Loan not to be there. But the final answer is with him. I believe we will have the answer soon. More than seven months have passed since the disappearance of Loan Danilo PeÃ±a, the lawyer for the family is confident that there will be a resolution soon. Regarding the case, there are seven defendants: Carlos PÃ©rez, accused of child abduction and currently being processed with preventive detention, along with MarÃ­a Victoria Caillava, Bernardino Antonio BenÃ­tez, Daniel Oscar RamÃ­rez, MÃ³nica del Carmen Millapi, Laudelina PeÃ±a, and Walter Maciel. According to the lawyer, they are just a minute away from a conviction. Juan Pablo Gallego took the lead of the lawsuit filed by MarÃ­a Noguera and JosÃ© PeÃ±a (the parents of the child) in September last year. There was so much speculation, so many things, that perhaps only now, at this hour, we are seeing the tremendous progress and turnaround of the case. We continue with the objective of finding the truth, I believe we are not far from it, relates, in conversation with Infobae. The first major question is: Where is Loan Gallego, I think he never left his province, after having vanished on June 13 in the Corrientes locality of 9 de Julio. This stance contrasts with the initial versions that pointed to the possibility of being illegally transported to other provinces or even abroad. We have almost certainty that they could not take him out of Corrientes, if they ever tried to do so, which I doubt. Our suspicion, and I have been saying it, revolves around PÃ©rez and Caillava. I have no doubt that they are the ones who took him. According to Gallego, the seven detained individuals, whom he defines as a lumpen gang, represent the final authors of the abduction and kidnapping. There never was a narco trail nor a situation that linked to human trafficking, he reveals. However, he admits that there could have been a sexual abuse. I do not believe in the hypothesis of the sale because, in fact, there was a crossing that initially did not emerge. While they said that Loan had disappeared, Laudelina called Caillava asking when he was returning. This makes it suppose that, in Laudelina's head, the disappearance was temporary. It is something that could have a sexual connotation, but within that group and within that recipient, explains the lawyer. According to his vision, Loan wouldn't have been part of the initial plans of those involved, since he attended lunch at his grandmother's house unexpectedly. It's clear that PÃ©rez took him and that, at the moment when Laudelina invents the story of the disappearance, three people are missing: PÃ©rez and Caillava, who took them, and RamÃ­rez, who handed them over. He also points out two striking facts: Daniel Fierrito RamÃ­rez shows up later at the scene, exhausted, sweating, and disheveled, while PÃ©rez appears several hours later, coincidentally bathed and changed. For the indictment, everything points to the gang's objective being to return Loan, but something would have complicated the process. Rome. RT Sub-Saharan migrants are being detained in Tunisia and sold to Libyan traffickers, a practice driven by the policies of the European Union and Italy, according to the authors of a report presented on Wednesday. The international research group Researchers X denounce that the authorities capture migrants, hold them in detention centers, even in cages, and then sell them for as little as $12 (40 Tunisian dinars) each. When I say sale, I actually refer to a sale, as if we were objects. They sold us as slaves. If we looked up, they hit us, a survivor recounted, specifying that the traffickers sold men, women, and children, all of them. One of my brothers was sold right in front of my eyes, he and his family, along with his one-year-old son, he added. According to the testimonies of thirty people from countries such as Cameroon, Chad, Sudan, Guinea, and CÃ´te d'Ivoire, who reported being sent from Tunisia to Libya between June 2023 and November 2024, migrants are detained in Tunisian cities, transported to special centers near the border with Libya, and sold to Libyan militias. According to the witnesses, women are sold at higher prices, up to $90, due to being exploited as sex slaves. The report also details cases of forced labor, torture, and sexual violence. Since 2016, EU member states, particularly Italy, have implemented a series of measures aimed at blocking migration routes through Libya and the central Mediterranean, notes the report. For example, Rome violated the prohibition on collective expulsions of migrants without individual assessments of their asylum applications. In addition, there is an Italian and European commitment to cooperate with Tunisia to reduce the number of people arriving in Italy from its shores. Since 2023, the North African country has intercepted over 100,000 people, more than 80% of whom came from sub-Saharan Africa, leading to a drastic reduction in arrivals by sea from Tunisia to Italy. The material and diplomatic support of Italy and the EU plays a fundamental role in the development of these policies, explain the authors. Italy has spent almost 75 million euros (78 million dollars) equipping and training Tunisian border guards, they highlight.

The alleged scam begins with job offers published on social media platforms like Facebook and Instagram, or through calls to action. Through a WhatsApp number, they ask the migrant to initiate the registration process, requesting a copy of the birth certificate, proof of their country of origin, and a description of the activity they carry out. Once the documentation is delivered, they leave the migrant on a waiting list. The recruiters demand payments for unnecessary processes, such as a medical examination, in a personal account. Currently, 15 migrants have sought advice from Guanajuato activists after being victims of this scam, but it is estimated that many more families have been affected. However, this process is done without a job offer and certification to grant the H2A visa. On the internet pages of the recruiters, it is stated that the workers are taken to the United States to work, but people who have been in the training camps in Guanajuato denied that trip. In Mexico and the United States, it is illegal to charge for the H2A visa, but within the national territory, fraud is committed by recruiters who charge up to 17,000 pesos to people who enlist to be trained. Subsequently, and in the event that workers are taken to the United States, the recruiters sell Mexican labor, which is highly valued in the United States. Additionally, Judge Guillermo Pereyra sentenced Dalila del Huerto Juarez to four years of effective prison time for finding her responsible for producing CSAM aggravated by a minor under 13 years of age. The case was initiated at the end of the month of May, based on a report from the NGO NCMEC (National Center for Missing and Exploited Children), which alerted that images of apparent child sexual abuse had been detected on the cloud storage service (Google Drive). In view of this and the progress of the investigation, a search warrant was executed at the accused's residence, obtaining a large number of files containing child sexual abuse material (CSAM). From the forensic computer analysis, evidence of the link between both defendants was obtained, where the woman made the images of her minor daughters, including one who was four years old, available to the individual for economic purposes. The accused even incited the minors to send intimate photos in exchange for money in their conversations, and in some cases, proposed sexual encounters that did not come to fruition. Prosecutor Cornejo emphasized that in this case, it was taken into account that the crime for which both were convicted, not only directly affected the victims at the time of the material's production, but its subsequent distribution amplifies the damage, revictimizing minors each time the material is shared, viewed, or consumed. The distribution perpetuates and multiplies the damage, rendering the violation of the minor's dignity indefinite, he noted. Furthermore, the distribution also favors the normalization and trivialization of child abuse in certain sectors of society, increasing the risks to the integrity of more children, girls, and adolescents. Source: Penal Prosecutors.

Alarm over new government measure that relaxes migrant controls on minors A measure from the National Directorate of Migrations exempts transportation companies from verifying the documentation of minors on international trips, generating concern over possible risks of child trafficking. A decision that has generated strong criticism, the national government has relaxed controls on the departure of children, adolescents, and minors from the country. Decree 166, published in the Official Gazette, exempts land, air, and maritime transportation companies from the obligation to verify the documentation of minors under 18 years old who travel with them. The rule leaves the task of fiscalization exclusively in the hands of border controls, eliminating a key filter that has served on numerous occasions to detect cases of human trafficking. The text signed by SebastiÃ¡n Pablo Seoane, head of the National Directorate of Migrations, indicates that international passenger transportation operators will be exempt from requiring additional exit documentation for minors under 18 years old. In other words, it will no longer be a requirement for companies to verify the presentation of travel authorizations or other documents before boarding minors on their units. This disposition contradicts the prevention policy that had been in place until now, which involved multiple instances of control to ensure that children and adolescents leaving the country did so under the appropriate legal conditions. The removal of this filter has raised concern among human rights organizations and child protection specialists, who warn of the risks of relaxing controls in a context where child trafficking remains a serious problem at the international level. Various sectors have recalled previous statements by President Javier Milei, in which, in a theoretical framework on extreme liberalism, he argued that the purchase and sale of people could be considered part of the market. Although the Government has not linked this measure to those statements, the temporal coincidence has generated concern and rejection reactions. From child protection organizations, it has been pointed out that this measure goes against international standards for combating child trafficking. The removal of intermediate controls significantly reduces the early detection of vulnerability situations, explained a source linked to the Juvenile Justice system. On the other hand, the National Directorate of Migrations maintains that the purpose of the provision is to expedite international transit, without implying a reduction in border controls. However, experience shows that additional supervision by transportation companies has been a fundamental tool in preventing the irregular departure of minors. In response to criticism, sectors of the opposition have requested the immediate review of the provision and the reinstatement of previous controls before leaving the country. Meanwhile, human rights organizations are analyzing possible legal measures to halt its application.

Condorcanqui outrage over PJ's acquittal of teacher accused of sexual assault of a schoolgirl Indignation. Utcubamba court acquitted a teacher who was accused of committing abuses over 4 years. Ministries of Women and Education reject judicial decision. Investigating office is investigating. As of now, there are 582 cases of rape in Condorcanqui. The ministries of Women and Education expressed their total rejection and outrage at the resolution of the Utcubamba Penal Collegiate Court, Amazonas, which acquitted teacher Etsam Luis Chigkim Catip, accused of the crime of sexual abuse against a schoolgirl in the indigenous community of Tutino, in Condorcanqui. Prior to this, the Superior Court of Justice of Amazonas coordinated with the Decentralized Office of the Control Authority to have a team of professionals travel to the province to gather information about the evidence, the case files in this case, and to perform a detailed analysis of the factual and legal basis of the issued sentence. On Thursday night, the Ministry of Women expressed its rejection of the decision made by the court that acquitted the accused. It also emphasized that this sentence ignores what is established in Supreme Decree 022005, which recognizes that the victim's statement can be sufficient proof to undermine the presumption of innocence. One cannot question the credibility of the testimony simply because the person is a victim. Decisions like this demotivate victims from reporting, exacerbate the situation of risk, and perpetuate impunity, the Mimp stated in a statement. You can see a Practitioner of the Prosecutor's Office is accused of being part of the gang Los Chamacos that stole vehicles in Lima Sur Protection for Victims On the other hand, the Ministry of Education indicated that, to guarantee safe classrooms, a justice system is required that protects victims and sanctions aggressors. Moreover, it highlighted that actions like this attack the integrity of minors and perpetuate impunity. And adds in a statement also released on Thursday night, that from the Ministry of Education, we join the request of the Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations and demand the Judiciary to investigate with urgency the actions of those responsible for this process, ensuring that there is no impunity. Regarding this, the Judiciary reported that the Decentralized Office of the National Control Authority (ODANC) of Amazonas, under the leadership of the Mg Juan Carlos GuzmÃ¡n Sosa was transferred on January 30 to the Superior Provincial Penal Collegiate Court of the Utcubamba province to carry out an extraordinary judicial visit. The results are still unknown. Impunity Rosamery Pioc, president of the Awajun Wampis Women's Council, mentioned that the minor was sexually assaulted by teacher Etsam Luis Chigkim from the age of 11 to 15 in the Tutino community, in Codorcanqui. Unfortunately, as a result of the rapes, she became pregnant. But that was not all, the abuser physically assaulted her and forced her to have an abortion. The affected person made her testimonial statement, passed through the Gessel camera, and underwent a forensic medical examination, however, despite having clear evidence, it was not enough to prevent the aggressor from being released. Concerned, Pioc denounced at the national level that many of the teachers, such as Chigkim Catip, are still free despite the denunciations and processes against them. This resolution puts other victims at risk. And it makes them lose faith in justice. That's why victims will no longer be encouraged to report, she mentioned.

text: In a joint operation between the National Police and the 2nd Military Police Battalion, Eduardo Guerrero Tapias, known as El GuayacÃ¡n de la DÃ©cima, was captured in the vicinity of the Nuestro AtlÃ¡ntico shopping center, in the El Manantial neighborhood of the municipality of Soledad. Read more A professor from Caucasia, Antioquia, was judicialized for alleged abuse against a minor. The suanero, recognized for his work as a decimero and repentista in the Carnaval de Barranquilla, faces serious accusations of sexual abuse against his granddaughters, who allegedly suffered similar abuses during their childhood. The initial complaint was filed by the parents of one of Guerrero Tapias' granddaughters, who revealed that the man had allegedly subjected the minor to indecent touching after the minor revealed this during a family reunion. After this revelation, other voices from the family came forward, including a second minor and four adult women, some of whom are relatives of the accused, who stated that they had also been victims of similar abuses when they were children. He would touch them while they were asleep and alone, but he would intimidate them. They were afraid of him and the trauma was great. In fact, it took a lot of courage for them to decide that it had to stop, because the accused works in cultural media and has access to children, declared Mildred Salas, the lawyer representing the victims, to Blu Radio. The man used to abuse them at night when most of their family members were asleep. And when he abused them, he would threaten them with divine punishments. Guerrero Tapias did not deny the facts and, on the contrary, stated that he believed these acts had been left in the past. I thought it was already over and forgotten, he expressed. The capture of Guerrero Tapias shook the region, not only due to the gravity of the charges, but also because of the profile of the accused. From the municipality of SuÃ¡n, Guerrero is an iconic figure in the cultural sphere of the Atlantic. His talent as a decimero and improviser led him to be considered a living treasure of local culture, recognition that allowed him to access public funds and consolidate himself as a reference in the Carnaval de Barranquilla. However, his influence in the cultural sector also raised concerns. Lawyer Salas pointed out that, due to his role as a cultural manager, Guerrero has had constant contact with children and adolescents, which could suggest the existence of additional victims. In his role as a cultural manager, he has had contact with many children. We invite the community to attend the hearings and report if there are more victims of his abuses, assured the lawyer. The victims, according to their legal representative, carried the trauma of the abuse for years, silenced by fear and the accused's influence. Authorities have reiterated their commitment to the investigation and urged the community not to remain silent in the face of similar situations.
