text: A man was detained after being accused of raping a 21-year-old woman who was returning home from her job at an ice cream shop in Merlo. A man was detained after being accused of raping a 21-year-old woman who was returning home from her job at an ice cream shop in Merlo. The incident occurred on Route 40, just a few meters from the intersection with President PerÃ³n Highway, on the previous Wednesday at dawn, when the accused was detained hours later based on the description provided by the victim. The young woman reported that she got off the bus and crossed paths with the subject, who approached her with a knife and took her to a nearby stream, where he assaulted her. According to Primer Plano Online, during the struggle to commit the assault, the woman suffered a fracture of the tibia and fibula, while before leaving, the perpetrator stole her cell phone, money she had with her, and a hat. Stay Quiet The officers highlighted that in her statement, the victim remembered that her aggressor told her to stay quiet and walk, that I'm going to rob you, while the blade of a knife was tracing her neck. Later, the young woman recalled that she managed to stand up, arrived at her home, and asked for help from the Police, who immediately took her to a hospital to carry out the protocol of prophylaxis and provide her with containment. Once she felt well enough, she was transferred to the 6th precinct of Mariano Acosta to complete her complaint, which she had already made verbally at the health center with a description of the suspect. On the other hand, prosecutor Patricio Ventricelli, from the 6th office of MorÃ³n, ordered the case to be handled with the protocol of rigor for cases of abuse. He then gave instructions to the personnel of the precinct and the DDI in the area for the search of the suspect, of whom the victim had provided precise details. After the woman's statements, they found the man who turned out to be a neighbor in the area where the sexual assault occurred. Thanks to the victim's resistance and bravery, who despite the horror she had to endure and withstand, was able to locate and identify the perpetrator's whereabouts. Finally, according to sources linked to the case, the officers determined that the perpetrator is Jonathan Gabriel Quiroga, who was arrested on charges of serious injuries due to gender-based violence, double aggravation of sexual abuse with carnal access, and commission with a weapon. He was wearing the victim's hat. We worked throughout the night and finally found him with the information she provided. When he was detained, he was wearing the victim's hat, which she recognized at the police station when she saw him getting off the patrol car and wearing an accessory that belonged to her, a source consulted by Primer Plano Online reported. The perpetrator turned out to be a neighbor from the area where the sexual assault occurred, apparently he had already planned to intercept his victim, among other details that are part of the investigation.

text: The Government of Puebla will reinforce security in the Tlaxcala-Puebla short route, due to human trafficking The head of the Secretariat of Governance (Segob), Samuel Aguilar Pala, stated that security will be reinforced in the short route of the Santa Ana Chiautempan highway in Tlaxcala-Puebla, as in this area, clandestine bars and nightclubs operate where cases of human trafficking for sexual exploitation are registered. In an interview, the state official acknowledged that this problem exists in this area, and some traffickers even travel from Tlaxcala to the city of Puebla to commit crimes. Some data have been registered on this matter, and I personally will pay attention to coordinating with my counterpart in Tlaxcala to establish strategies. We agreed to meet next week to discuss this and other points, he said. On the short route in municipalities such as San Pablo del Monte and Tenancingo, human trafficking gangs operating for sexual exploitation purposes are active. These municipalities border the state of Puebla. Last year, Puebla authorities conducted a raid on the Bora Bora nightlife center in San Pablo del Monte, as it has been reported that criminal gangs operate in this location. Sucesos Security will be reinforced on the short route corridor of Santa Ana Puebla, where strip clubs and bars are located, in several of which there is a record of human trafficking for sexual exploitation purposes, said Samuel Aguilar, head of the Puebla State Government's Secretariat of Security. Santo Domingo. _ The General Directorate of Migration (DGM) reported that a Canadian citizen recently detained in the BÃ¡varo area is in the process of deportation, as he is required by judicial authorities from his country. The agency that regulates and oversees national migration flows explained that Eric Belhumeur has an ongoing judicial process in Canada for sexual abuse against a minor related to his ex-spouse, both of the same nationality. Belhumeur was retained in his country and was released on conditional liberty with the commitment to surrender his passport and not leave the territorial jurisdiction limit, but he violated that agreement and traveled to the Dominican Republic on December 24, 2019, where he has been living illegally. The Tourist Police arrested him in Friusa and sent him to the DGM, where he initially agreed voluntarily to be repatriated, a measure that was going to be executed on January 19, 2025, in accordance with the protocols and regulations of Law 28504, and it was not possible to execute it because his passport was blocked. A court in San CristÃ³bal issued a release order in favor of the Canadian, without considering the elements of evidence or the evidence that makes him a fugitive from justice in his country and the fact that he has been residing illegally in the Dominican Republic for 5 years, a decision that has been the subject of an appeal. The union began charging for job assignments and extorting contractors in exchange for security. They were known as the Aragua Train gang and it was there that they got their name. We were notified through the prosecution of persons of the bulletin that the minor had been missing since December 7, the search began in our municipality and neighboring municipalities, but we did not have a report. A local missing girl was located after being published in local social media and neighborhood groups, said Guadalupe Rivera, commander of the Municipal Police's Gender Unit. CLARIDAD Following her discovery and initial statements, police ruled out that she was a victim of human trafficking, instead confirming that the minor had fled her home due to family violence. To combat the human trafficking network operating in the VÃ­a Corta corridor to Santa Ana Chiautempan, on the borders of Tlaxcala and Puebla, the government of the state of Puebla has announced the reinforcement of security and surveillance in this region, especially in bars and clandestine nightclubs where sex trafficking activities have been identified. The Secretary of Governance of the state of Puebla, Samuel Aguilar Pala, made this announcement this Friday during an interview, following the signing of a collaboration agreement on security matters between the two states. Upon leaving the Tlaxcala Convention Center, Aguilar Pala acknowledged that various establishments in the area have been classified as red hotspots due to their alleged connection to human trafficking networks. In response, he announced that surveillance strategies and joint operations will be intensified with the authorities of the state of Tlaxcala, as well as with the National Guard, the Navy, and the Secretariat of National Defense (Sedena). The problem of human trafficking in the region is one of the most serious in Latin America, and victims are often transported from Tlaxcala to the city of Puebla to be sexually exploited, even reaching states in the United States. Various reports have been filed on this crime, so I will personally be attentive to coordinating efforts with my counterpart in Tlaxcala. We have agreed to hold a meeting next week, in which we will address this issue as a priority, Aguilar Pala stated. Among the municipalities with the highest incidence of this crime are San Pablo del Monte and Tenancingo, both located in Tlaxcala and bordering the city of Puebla. As a precedent, last year, Puebla authorities carried out a raid on the Bora Bora nightlife center in San Pablo del Monte, following complaints about its alleged connection to human trafficking networks and other crimes, including femicides. Government of Puebla to install seven security modules in the state capital As part of the strategy to strengthen security in the state, Samuel Aguilar Pala reported that the Government of Puebla will install, in the first stage, seven security modules in the state capital. In addition, surveillance will be reinforced at the 27 main access points to the entity, which border seven neighboring states, with the aim of halting the mobility of delinquent groups between regions. These modules will allow for more efficient monitoring of criminal activity and an immediate response to any emergency situation. The head of the Secretariat of Governance (Segob) also announced the installation of 10 security towers equipped with cutting-edge technology to improve surveillance at strategic points in the entity. He concluded by saying that the Puebla government seeks to reinforce security and ensure the protection of citizens, combating crimes such as human trafficking and organized crime in the region.

According to the professional, what motivated the start of the sessions in the past was the difficulty in cohabiting with the family unit she maintained with her partner. The drug trade in the Philippines, according to the international organization, remains a complex problem, as the Asian country is both a destination and a transit hub for narcotics trafficking and the geographical distribution of the Philippines, which consists of more than 7,000 islands, poses strong challenges for law enforcement agencies in surveillance and control of drug movement. Methamphetamine, known locally as SabÃº, along with marijuana, are the most trafficked and abused drugs in the Philippines. Recent statistics on drug trafficking indicate that the problem persists, despite the government's efforts under Ferdinand Marcos RomuÃ¡ldez to curb the threat. The situation is further complicated by the participation of various local and international criminal syndicates that exploit the strategic location of the Philippines as a gateway to other Southeast Asian countries. These organizations are deeply entrenched and operate with both traditional practices and a high degree of sophistication, utilizing innovative methods and high-tech technology to carry out their operations. Money laundering, according to the UNODC, is a particularly worrying aspect of the drug trade due to its symbiotic relationship with the multimillion-dollar profits generated by the sale of illicit drugs, which are channeled through the financial system to conceal their illicit origin. Just as in Mexico, where Felipe CalderÃ³n declared war on drugs, the president Ferdinand also declared war on drugs with an aggressive approach, the collateral damage in terms of human rights attracted international attention, and just as in our country, it only served to intensify violence and result in a failure. Among the local organizations in the Philippines are the Bahala Na Gang, Sigue Sigue Commandos, Batang City Jail, and Sputnik. On the other hand, the Philippine judicial system imposes severe penalties for drug trafficking offenses, reflecting the government's firm stance against this illicit activity. The Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act states that the punishment for drug trafficking can range from life imprisonment to the death penalty, depending on the quantity and type of drugs involved, as well as heavy fines, but these measures have not yielded results. Despite these harsh penalties, drug trafficking cases persist in the Philippines, testifying to the lucrative nature of the drug trade and the sophisticated evasion tactics employed by criminal organizations. Consequently, the social impact of drug trafficking is profound and multifaceted. I can swear under oath that POGOs are clean. However, his critics claim that the government has only collected around $100 million in taxes from POGOs since 2016, a mere 10% of what they should have generated. It is in the districts of Makati, Pasay, and ParaÃ±aque, where the largest number of POGO offices are concentrated. Men, women, and children are exploited in rural communities, conflict zones, and disaster areas, as well as in impoverished urban areas and brothels. The Philippines is one of the largest sources of online child sex exploitation, with estimates suggesting that of the 500,000 Filipino children employed as domestic workers in the Philippines, 25% are under the age of 15. In total, it is estimated that between 60,000 and 100,000 Filipino children are affected by labor or sex trafficking. Native Filipinos are often involved in the recruitment stage of human trafficking. Perpetrators are frequently family members or corrupt government officials. Organized crime groups in the Philippines oversee the networks of smuggling and subsequent trafficking. They are connected with the owners of nightclubs or karaoke bars in the destinations where the girls are deployed, who are mostly nationals of the destination country. According to the U.S. Department of State, the Philippines is an important source of sex and labor trafficking. With one of the world's largest immigrant populations, Filipino male migrant workers are often exploited in the fishing, maritime transport, construction, manufacturing, and agriculture sectors, while women are exploited in domestic and hospitality functions. Both boys and girls are subjected to sex and labor trafficking, many of whom have been sold by their own family. There is an emphasis on very close-knit family units in the Philippines, which may mean that children are unlikely to speak up when they are abused or exploited by someone from their own family. The Philippines' labor code allows parents to decide whether their children can work before they turn 15, meaning that sometimes, children start working at the age of 6. This lack of protection contributes to child labor and contract servitude for children who have no one to advocate for them. Child soldier recruitment also occurs in the Philippines, particularly in the southern island of Mindanao, where radical separatist groups operate. Non-state armed groups such as the Maute Group, the Moro National Liberation Front, and the Bangsamoro Islamic Freedom Fighters recruit child soldiers. When it comes to women and girls, as well as children, they are subjected to sexual slavery. The most common method of human trafficking recruitment is through false promises of employment. The traffickers take advantage of the economically disadvantaged, using debt-based coercion or the promise of work to lure their victims. Employers confiscate all travel documents to prevent them from leaving. Online recruitment is another common tactic, particularly in the case of online exploitation of children. One in three internet users in the Philippines was a child in 2020. That increase in children's use of the internet increases their vulnerability to online manipulation and exploitation. Social media in particular is increasingly becoming a common place for recruitment. Traffickers sexually exploit children in live internet transmissions, where foreign clients watch and make international wire transfers for payment. These traffickers are often parents or close relatives who force their children into online sexual exploitation. The majority of viewers of this child sexual abuse material are based in the EU, Australia, Canada, and the UK. Victims of human trafficking in the Philippines are trafficked both nationally and internationally. Bribing immigration personnel, producing fake travel documents, and using student exchange and internship programs are among the main methods used to transport victims. Traffickers use air and maritime routes to transport their victims across borders and evade detection. They take advantage of the lack of immigration personnel at smaller airports in the Philippines to smuggle people into cities such as Bangkok, Hong Kong, and Kuala Lumpur. Despite the illegality of prostitution in the Philippines, many major tourist destinations are critical hotspots for the sex trade, including the exploitation of minors. Generally, it is taxi drivers with knowledge of hidden locations who facilitate the sexual trafficking of children in these urban tourist areas. Thus, amidst the drug trade, corruption, human trafficking, and abuse of the political class, millions of Filipinos have to survive, many of whom end up emigrating to another country, only to become prey to other predators.

text: LONDON The Temporary Foreign Worker Program (TFWP) maintained by Canada facilitates shocking abuses and discriminates against migrant workers, Amnesty International (AI) reported in its latest report. Erika Guevara Rosas, AI's director of research and campaigns, said that the abuses experienced by migrant workers in Canada are extremely concerning, especially considering a country that claims to be a leader in protecting human rights. The report, titled "Canada Has Destroyed Me: Labour Exploitation of Migrant Workers," exposes the impact of the TFWP, which allows employers (both corporations and individuals) to hire migrant workers primarily for low-paying jobs The sectors that most employ this workforce are agriculture, food processing, the care system, construction, and hospitality. The TFWP visas link these people to a single employer entity that controls their immigration status and working conditions. Guevara Rosas said that many migrant people have told us that they came to Canada with the hope of obtaining a better future, but instead, they felt treated like slaves. These workers and women are vital to putting food on the tables of the country and caring for the elderly. They deserve much better, he added. AI based its report on interviews conducted in the provinces of Quebec and Ontario in 2023 and 2024 with 44 people who were TFWP workers, many of whom denounced unpaid wages and excessive working hours. Some contracts viewed by AI specified zero days of rest. Some people also reported that their employers and supervisors used racist language against them and called them derogatory names, such as "burro," "indio," or "mexicano de mierda." One of the cases documented in the report is that of Benedicte, a woman from Cameroon, who suffered racist psychological and sexual abuse at the hands of her employer upon arriving in Canada in 2015, with a two-year work visa to work on a farm. She was forced to work between 70 and 80 hours a week performing agricultural and other tasks, including domestic work, and was significantly underpaid and subjected to constant surveillance. Her employer deceived her, promising to bring her children to Canada, in order to continue exploiting her. Ultimately, she fell ill and was diagnosed with a severe anemia. When she finally left the farm in July 2018, her employer canceled her visa, leaving her in an irregular migratory situation. "I did not expect to be a slave here," she told the interviewers. Many migrant workers under the TFWP regime work and live in remote areas, and therefore their accommodation and access to medical insurance and transportation depend on their employer. If they fall ill, suffer an injury, or are no longer considered fit for work, their contract can be terminated and they can be subject to a rapid repatriation. Some workers and female workers reported that their employer had threatened them with repatriation, and in a handful of cases, they had been taken to the airport against their will. Many workers and female workers do not report the abuses they suffer due to fear of reprisals such as wrongful dismissal, non-renewal of their contract, and repatriation, the report states. Those who do report have to deal with the complex system of law enforcement, which is not designed to protect people with precarious status, and who often do not know how to navigate the bureaucratic systems in either of Canada's official languages, English and French. In 2023, the first countries of origin of Tfwp workers were Mexico, India, the Philippines, Guatemala, and Jamaica, which accounted for almost 70% of work permits issued. Guevara Rosas stated that Canadian authorities are well aware of the abuses committed under the Tfwp and have still implemented very limited measures to address some of them, such as increasing inspections. In particular, AI requires that open work permits be issued, since migrant workers must have the freedom to change jobs and employers, just like Canadians, concluded Guevara Rosas.

Near Hereford, Arizona, U.S. Border Patrol agents from the Brian A. Terry Station intercepted a vehicle. The routine, seemingly normal, took an unexpected turn. Inside the vehicle, two undocumented migrants attempted to escape. The ensuing high-speed pursuit, with details yet to be publicly disclosed, reveals the complexity of the border migration issue. The driver, however, was not a simple facilitator. He is a U.S. citizen with a criminal record, including convictions for serious crimes and a registered sex offender. The individual's identity remains undisclosed for now, but the gravity of his legal situation is undeniable. The U.S. Border Patrol has confirmed that he faces charges for human trafficking, a crime with severe consequences. Our border security is a priority, declared a U.S. Border Patrol spokesperson in a statement to local media. This case, pinpointing the source, highlights the multifaceted problem of human trafficking and the need for interagency collaboration to combat it effectively. The ongoing investigation is raising a range of questions about the criminal networks involved and the possible exploitation of migrants.

text: By Claudia Victoria Arriaga DurÃ¡n. 31URLIt's better to be in prison than to keep getting beaten and forced to sleep with men every day, Ana, a Mayan woman from YucatÃ¡n, a victim of human trafficking, confessed. She has been in preventive detention for over a decade awaiting a sentence. Ana's sisters and nieces want her to be free. She has been incarcerated for 14 years without a sentence, accused of a crime she did not commit. She went from being a victim of human trafficking to being accused of trafficking her own sisters. At 18 years old, Ana was admitted to the Women's Correctional Center (Cereso) in Tekax, YucatÃ¡n, accused of being part of a group of human traffickers known as El clan. You feel like you're worth nothing, that nobody will ever love you, and that you'll never escape the four walls of the room where you're forced to have sex, Ana said, sitting on a concrete bench, her hands covering her face as she gave this interview. Concrete walls over 10 meters high separate her from the outside, surrounding the central courtyard of the women's prison in MÃ©rida. It was there that she was transferred in 2023, along with other Maya women who had their freedom taken away. What separates her module from freedom are nothing but rocks she can't break. In Ana's story, it's not clear what crime she committed. She's been stuck in limbo for over a decade, locked away. According to data obtained through the National Transparency Platform, his case could be part of the four people imprisoned for human trafficking in the form of sexual exploitation or the seven for committing pimping, that is, for commercializing the bodies of their sisters and managing a brothel. It is also not ruled out that he is registered among the 37 people deprived of liberty for committing the crime of corruption of minors and the incapacitated or human trafficking of minors. The truth is that human trafficking in any of its modalities is a crime that is difficult to report. YucatÃ¡n, in relation to the rest of the country, has few cases registered, but it is not exempt. It is ranked 31st according to the official figures of the Executive Secretary of the National Public Security System (SESNSP). Another of its peculiarities is that cases tend to concentrate in the capital, that is, in the city of MÃ©rida. It is not common to find them in the Maya peripheries, as happened with Ana. For a while now, it has been possible to detect trafficking networks in some areas of MÃ©rida. The person victimized by trafficking has lost all their freedom and rights and can be sold up to 20 times in a day, Enrique Puc, representative of the Red Rahamim in YucatÃ¡n, an international organization made up of religious and lay people, who work against human trafficking throughout the country, reported. From victim to trafficker They were military personnel, municipal police, state police, adult men who paid to have sex with me, with a child, Ana declared with courage. In her memories and those of her sisters, there is a map that torments them every day. They were moved to municipalities in the southern cone, traveling to Ticul, Chumayel, Peto, Izamal, and Sinanche. On some occasions, they were also taken to Quintana Roo. Every day, I thought about how to end my life, how to take my own life, she said with a serious voice and tears in her eyes. Ana was interviewed in prison. That day, she wore a blue striped fisherman's sweater, a lilac blouse, and flip-flops. Her hair was tied back, and her face was washed. Her voice would catch at times, showing the number of years it had taken for her to be heard. She thought she had been forgotten. When she was arrested, she was 18 years old, and no one believed her that from the age of 14, she had been prostituted by a couple that had taken away her freedom. At that time, she didn't have the opportunity to defend herself or access a gender perspective defense. She went from being a victim of sex trafficking to being accused of trafficking. They accused her of prostituting her 11- and 13-year-old sisters and her nieces, who, like her, were also prostituted. Today she is no longer alone, her adult sisters, MarÃ­a and Magdalena, have tried several times to request that the charges be dropped. But before that, they wondered every day what they could do if no one listened to them. It was in the Cereso of the municipality of Tekax where they found the answer. There, although it seemed unlikely, the women deprived of their freedom organized to obtain truth and justice. In prison, she also met other women. Some were imprisoned for legitimate self-defense. In a few words, imprisoned for fighting not to be victims of femicide. They told her about a lawyer who was accompanying their case. Ana, with distrust, but already with nothing to lose, contacted him. The majority of the women from that prison shared the desire to be free and to demonstrate their innocence. Their stories are no less important. From Domestic Worker to Modern Slavery Ana, originally from the municipality of Akil, was taken by El clan when she was 14 years old. A couple offered her a job to clean a house in the municipality of Ticul, 32 kilometers away from her community. With the hope of earning money and improving her quality of life, she decided to leave her home, just like many Maya girls and adolescents do. On the day she arrived at her new job, she was received by Carlos and Estela, a married couple she knew nothing about. Once settled, the Patron, Carlos, raped her, warning her that he was training her for her new job. She couldn't defend herself. Soon, they started moving her to different municipalities for prostitution. Ana, sitting on a bench in the female correctional facility's break area, insisted that at the time of her arrest in 2010, the authorities forced her to sign words that never came out of her mouth. In other words, the young woman's initial statements were made under coercion. During the course of this investigation, we had access to the investigation file. The case is being held in storage at the Tekax municipal courts. What can be read in it is a very different version of what the young women claim. Ana's testimony, which was signed under duress, states that she traveled to Ticul because she knew that there were women who received money for sleeping with men. Upon arriving in the town, she asked if there was a brothel and was pointed to a plot of land with a wooden structure and corrugated metal roof. She knocked on the door and it was answered by Carlos. She asked if she could be received and he agreed. She asked if it was a brothel and he replied that it was, and that it charged 20 pesos per room. He did not ask her age, only her name, and from that day on, she began working as a prostitute at that location, according to the young woman's initial statements after her arrest. The case file from the Attorney General's Office of the State of YucatÃ¡n (FGE) details that Ana supposedly charged 120 pesos from clients, gave 20 pesos to Carlos for the rent of the room, and in addition, he asked 10 pesos from each man to let him pass. However, we now know that her traffickers charged between 400 to 600 pesos for sexual services.Further in that same testimony obtained through threats, it is suggested that Ana was in love with her trafficker Carlos, as can be read in her statement of April 4, 2010. Nothing could be further from reality, Ana stated 14 years after these events.Like the rest of the girls, adolescents, and women who were victims of El clan, she was tortured. They would hang her tied with a wooden stick held from the ceiling to beat her. Carlos and Estela Carlos is a man around 40 years old who was married to Estela and lived together in the municipality of Ticul He described himself as Catholic and a believer in the Virgin of Guadalupe. After being arrested, he stated that he earned 400 pesos per week and that he completed the household expenses with the money he made by prostituting Ana, his sisters, and his nieces. In his mind, they were a family. He knew that over time they would get used to it and would come to enjoy that type of life, he testified. When Estela married Carlos, he accepted helping him manage their family business, a brothel. In his statements, he also admitted to the tortures and rapes he committed against Ana, his sisters, and nieces. When they had their period, he would force them to use a sponge, like the ones used in furniture, roll it up and tie a string to it. He formed a kind of makeshift tampon, like the ones sold in stores, and inserted it into their vaginas so the clients wouldn't see that they were on their period. When it was over, she had to pull the thread and remove the sponge to wash it and use it again for the next client, she declared to the authorities. She was in charge of dressing them in what she described as sexy clothing, which was nothing more than lingerie, short skirts, shorts, and tops with straps. She would dye their hair and apply colored contact lenses. The Escape On January 4, 2010, MarÃ­a's life changed. She asked her mother if she could go to work with her sisters, Ana and Magdalena. Her mother allowed it because it represented an additional income for the house and thought she wouldn't be alone. But when she arrived, she found a scene that still terrifies her to this day. When Estela received her, she asked Ana and Magdalena, her sisters, to dress her in a short skirt and a top with straps, at the same time, she yelled that she would have to sleep with many men. MarÃ­a tried to defend herself, but she received a slap. At that moment, Carlos intervened and raped her. The social context of the Mayan communities is a determining factor for girls and adolescents from communities to be caught by human trafficking networks in the mode of sexual exploitation. The Network for Children's Rights in Mexico (REDIM) places the accelerated growth of YucatÃ¡n as a detonator for girls and children who grow up in rural areas to fall into the hands of traffickers, as in many cases they migrate in search of opportunities. Belonging to indigenous peoples, being in a family below the poverty average, are factors that add levels of vulnerability and put Mayan children first in line to be caught by human trafficking networks, REDIM director Tania RamÃ­rez said in an interview for this report. She added that the idea of generating wealth for a few only brings more inequality and risks to the Maya communities. That false idea of development where everything is about generating wealth and, in addition, wealth for a few, without solving the gaps on the floor. YucatÃ¡n has not managed to guarantee equality for the indigenous people, she mentioned.Then, MarÃ­a, with just 11 years old, endured two months of beatings and violations by more than 10 men per day. Fed up and scared, she decided to escape. That opportunity presented itself on February 9, 2010, when Carlos and Estela tried to get her into a sexual relationship with a third client. MarÃ­a fought with all her strength to get out of the room where they locked her. She managed to open the door and confronted them in front of the man, who, enraged by the situation, asked them to return their money. MarÃ­a was punished with beatings and left alone in that same room. The couple was so furious that they did not notice they had left the door unlocked. The little girl ran towards the street and hid in a bush. She spent hours between the thorns until a lady found her. The woman, who, like the rest of the neighbors, suspected what was happening in that house, explained to her how to leave without being caught. I ran towards where the lady told me and saw a house, I approached to ask for help. The woman who opened the door told me that her husband was a police officer, that he was at home and they took me to the Public Ministry in Ticul to report, Maria explained, who is now an adult woman. In the last six years, from 2018 to 2024, the YucatÃ¡n State Attorney General's Office has not received any complaint about the crime of human trafficking in the modality of exploitation. This reflects how complex it is to report, pursue, and dismantle this type of network. There are judicial files with people linked to the process for the crimes of child corruption, child trafficking, and child pornography as mentioned in Article 208 of the Penal Code of the State of YucatÃ¡n. 18 people were charged with child corruption, 4 with child trafficking, and 3 with child pornography. Pending sentencing and justice, Ana was accused of the crime of pimping when she was arrested. Article 214 of the Penal Code of the State of YucatÃ¡n establishes that whoever benefits from the sexual trade of a third party, or facilitates the means to engage in prostitution, commits this offense. Also, whoever runs, administers, or supports brothels commits this offense. The penalty for pimping is one to seven years in prison and 40 to 100 days of fine. However, Ana has been waiting for sentencing for 14 years, that is, she has already served the maximum sentence twice. Data from the YucatÃ¡n Judiciary Council of the Judicial Power, obtained through the National Transparency Platform, shows the sentences of "El clan", to which Ana was accused of belonging. Four people were sentenced, three women and one man (Carlos). Two were sent to Ticul and two to Tekax, and only one concluded with a sentence of 6 years and 2 months in prison. The last one was given to a woman, who, like the others, was a victim of sexual exploitation. As a result of this violence, the woman had a child with Carlos. The minor, the product of this pregnancy, was registered with the surnames of the traffickers' couple and is currently in the custody of Carlos's son, her older brother. Ana's defense attorney, MoisÃ©s VelÃ¡zquez Cuevas, clarified that Ana was accused of rape, statutory rape, and pimping. However, her situation became complicated because her sentence was revoked twice, in 2016 and in 2019. The trafficking couple, on the other hand, reported being victims of torture during their detention and requested to be subjected to the Istanbul Protocol, a mechanism of the United Nations (UN) that provides tools to document torture and ill-treatment. In many cases, it allows victims of this crime to obtain justice. In response, the courtroom of the Superior Justice Court ordered the re-trial of the case. As a result, Ana became one of the forgotten cases of the previous justice system. Ana has seen three governors, three prosecutors pass by, and remains forgotten. It was the exploiters or traffickers, who had private lawyers, who managed to get the re-trial of the case, VelÃ¡zquez Cuevas pointed out. Another reason the case was re-tried is because there were inconsistencies. For example, assigning the same public defender to Ana and the trafficking couple. They all were put under the same public defender. The file states that the kidnapper, to put it that way, the person who forced her to prostitute herself, hit her when they were in court, the lawyer noted. According to the testimonies, Carlos attacked Ana during the hearings. He would step on her foot or pinch her to hurt her in front of the authorities. Despite everything, the young woman continues waiting for the sentence to be read. They tell Ana that they made her do things, she was forced. She shouldn't be in prison, the gentlemen made us all do it. They also mistreated her. When I was there, I saw them beat her with a wooden object, confessed MarÃ­a, Ana's sister. They would hang us and tell us that they would kill us if we escaped and that the first thing they would do would be to look for our family to kill them and then us to kill ourselves. When Ana went to look for us, Estela accompanied her so that she wouldn't be able to escape. It's not fair, the truth. To me, it's not fair what's happening to her. She was a young girl and in her mind, she didn't know how to help herself to save herself, Magdalena said with anguish, sitting in a hammock. Ana tried, in these 14 years of imprisonment, to rebuild her life. She even got married to a person who was deprived of their freedom in the Tekax municipal prison and they had a child. She's not guilty, she's a victim of them. It's not fair that she's there, she should be out enjoying her child. It's not her fault what happened, her aunt commented. From outside, her sisters and nieces, who were also victims of this human trafficking and sexual exploitation network, still have the hope of seeing her in freedom. The 2023-2024 report of the Ciudad de MÃ©xico Citizens Council for Security and Justice's hotline to report human trafficking received 29 assistance requests from the state of YucatÃ¡n. And although it's a crime that's hard to detect, in Mexico, there are anonymous ways to report it. One option is the 800 55 33 000 line, which corresponds to the National Line against Human Trafficking. Another is the Special Prosecutor's Office for Crimes of Violence Against Women and Human Trafficking (FEVIMTRA), whose 01 800 00 854 00 line operates 24 hours a day. Stories like Ana's suggest that, in Mexico, the lack of gender perspective and intercultural perspective leaves victims of crimes like human trafficking defenseless. On the other hand, Ana's support from friends, sisters, and aunts shows that networks can also provide help.

One option is the 800 55 33 000 line, which corresponds to the National Line against Human Trafficking. Another is the Special Prosecutor's Office for Crimes of Violence Against Women and Human Trafficking (FEVIMTRA), whose 01 800 00 854 00 line operates 24 hours a day. On the other hand, Ana's support from friends, sisters, and aunts shows that networks can also provide help.

Lima. The Christian Life Society (SVC), a Peruvian Catholic organization, requested forgiveness on Friday from the minors who were victims of sexual abuse committed by some of its members, which led to the dissolution of the SVC by the Vatican. We want to express (with) deep pain and remorse our request for forgiveness to the victims and all the people affected by the various abuses that occurred in our history, for the wounds that were inflicted and for the entire scandal that this has caused, stated the SVC in a statement. The SVC was an apostolic society, founded in Peru in 1971 by layman Luis Fernando Figari. Since 2011, various complaints from former members of the organization appeared about acts of sexual abuse when they were minors. Currently, Figari is a fugitive from Peruvian justice, investigated for being the presumed leader of a criminal organization dedicated to exploiting minors within the SVC. On the other hand, the organization reaffirmed this Friday the truth about its dissolution ordered by Pope Francis, stating that they accept with docility the decision. The Supreme Pontiff of the Catholic Church ordered the dissolution of SVC on January 18.

The efforts to combat gender-based crimes established in the Peace-Building Coordination Tables and the immediate intervention in response to a citizen's call, allowed elements of the State of Mexico's Secretary of Security (SSEM) to apprehend a man possibly implicated in the crime of sexual abuse. After a citizen's complaint through the national emergency number 911, state police received an alert to attend a residence where a minor had suffered sexual abuse. They arrived at the site in a timely manner. At the location, the officers immediately safeguarded the victim and made contact with a woman, who identified a man present at the scene, pointing him out as the one who had committed an act against the minor's integrity. As part of the actions, the SSEM police officers informed Fredy N, 52 years old, of the constitutive elements of the crime as well as the rights that the law grants him, and presented him at the Women's Justice Center, where his legal situation will be determined.

DOUBLE LOCK The Venezuelan Police detained 33 people for various crimes, according to the director of the Scientific, Penal and Criminal Investigations Corps (CICPC), Douglas Rico, without specifying the period in which the arrests took place. Through social media, Rico detailed on Thursday, January 30, that among the detainees, there are six people who committed trafficking and possession of narcotics, and three for robbery. The rest of the apprehended individuals committed crimes such as sexual abuse, document forgery, or illicit possession of firearms, among others, according to the CICPC director, who did not detail in which regions of the country the detention operations took place. All the individuals were placed at the disposal of the corresponding judicial authorities to continue the process individually, according to the type of crime committed and its aggravations. On Tuesday, Rico said that Venezuela recorded a homicide rate of 4.1 per 100,000 inhabitants in 2024, while highlighting that the country has been consistently reducing this crime. He pointed out that in 2016, the homicide rate was 56 per 100,000 inhabitants, and assured that this average has been decreasing, detailing that in 2022 it was 6.7 per 100,000 inhabitants, and in 2023 it was 5.3. On the other hand, the official reported that last year the CICPC captured 19,434 people who allegedly committed crimes. Also, he continued, 2,004 firearms, 12,783 ammunition, 5,172 vehicles, as well as 5,576 mobile phones were recovered. Of interest, Ecuador declared the Tren de Aragua DOBLE LLAVE gang as terrorist. The Valdivia Court of Appeals rejected a nullity appeal filed by his defense, thus confirming the sentence of the Valdivia Penal Court, which had declared him guilty in November 2022. A crucial conviction after years of struggle The case began in 2022, when complaints were filed that led to an investigation led by prosecutor MÃ³nica Palma. During the trial, it was established that the abuse occurred from 2012, when the victim was 8 years old. The family's complainant lawyer, Daniel Medina, qualified the ruling as very relevant, highlighting that it came to ratify the truthfulness of the facts that were denounced in 2022 and that originated the investigation led by the Public Ministry, headed by Prosecutor MÃ³nica Palma. Sandra Ranz, from the Citizen Network Against Child Sexual Abuse, also highlighted the importance of the verdict. We accompany the long and complex path until the recent ratification of the sentence and the imprisonment of Jaime Matamala. We have been witnesses to the bravery of the victim and her family. We thank them for not being silent and denouncing. We also thank all those who, without a doubt, supported the search for justice and allowed us to break down the barriers of silence and normalization that protect abusers, especially when they wield power or influence.

text: On September 16, 2024, federal agents arrested Sean Combs, also known as Diddy or Puff Daddy, one of the most successful and influential rappers and producers in the industry, at a Manhattan hotel. The main charges include conspiracy to commit crimes in an organized manner and the trafficking of women, in an accusation that outlines that, at least since 2008 to the present, Combs abused, threatened, and coerced women and other individuals, and carried out criminal acts for the trafficking of women, forced labor, kidnappings, arson, bribery, and obstruction of justice, among other crimes. This, in only four of the federal cases currently open (there are more pending). In those other crimes, at least a dozen complaints of sexual aggression, rape, chemical submission, and a history of violence, primarily against women, are included. The Fall of Diddy, a new documentary series by Max, presents up to 30 testimonies from witnesses and victims, several of whom are unprecedented, while the artist remains in preventive detention awaiting trial, and the prosecution continues to expand the charges. The most recent, presented on January 30, 2025, includes the accusation of two new victims who claim to have been coerced into maintaining sexual relationships and an ex-girlfriend's former roommate who accuses him of hanging her from the balcony of his apartment. This is the hidden face of a practically billionaire producer, accustomed to celebrating his birthdays surrounded by friends and celebrities in lavish parties in his mansions worth over 50 million euros. Those White Parties that no one wanted to miss. Parties where the rapper and his guests, including A-list actors, writers, entrepreneurs, millionaires, and a who's who of important people, regardless of their field, dressed in white and enjoyed nights reminiscent of Gatsby, a figure with whom Combs has identified himself more than once. In 1993, for his 29th birthday, he threw a party for a guest list that included Kevin Costner, Muhammad Ali, Sarah Ferguson, or the then-merely entrepreneur Donald Trump. And so year after year, while abuses would have been taking place in hotels, recording studios, and other venues, Diddy was as powerful as wealthy, as famous as gifted with a Midas touch for music, which led him to produce (beyond his own records) artists as varied as Mariah Carey, the late Notorious B.I.G., or Jennifer Lopez's debut (with whom he had a relationship from 1999 to 2001). His record label, Bad Boy Records, can boast of having sold over 500 million albums. Combs has been behind bars in a Brooklyn prison (in the same section where today's inmate, crypto scammer Sam Bankman-Fried, is serving his sentence) without bail. Justified by two judges due to his history of violence, drug abuse, and witness tampering, as well as the risk of flight by a man whose mansions were registered by the FBI a few months ago when he was attempting to board his private jet to the Bahamas. It's not Combs' first run-in with the law in 1999, he and his then-girlfriend Jennifer Lopez were arrested (along with his bodyguard and one of his protÃ©gÃ©s, rapper Shyne) after a chase through New York following a shootout in a Manhattan nightclub. In the car, an illegal firearm was found, and the story was resolved halfway. Shyne was sentenced to nine years in prison for assault and possession of firearms, the bodyguard and Combs were acquitted, Lopez was not charged with anything, and no one was ever convicted of the three gunshot victims in the altercation. One of the gunshot wounds, Natania Reuben, defends and continues to defend today that Combs shot her. To reopen the case, she is willing to have the bullet fragments still inside her skull extracted. Nevertheless, Reuben sued Combs for $130 million in civil court in 2008, and the case was resolved through an extrajudicial settlement. The case was so prominent that it motivated the rapper's first alias change from Puff Daddy to P. Diddy. By then, according to the complaints currently on the table, Combs had accumulated another private record of violence (Lopez stated in 2003 that they broke up because he had been unfaithful to her, but in his recent documentary he also pointed out that in the past they had physically fought and a couple of other unpleasant things had happened during their sentimental relationship, without specifying who) three women have accused Combs of raping, drugging, and assaulting them in that decade. These accusations were possible thanks to the New York law that was approved at the height of the #MeToo movement and the Weinstein case, to temporarily eliminate the statute of limitations for sexual crimes. A temporality that ended in December 2023. Almost coinciding in time with those denunciations, on November 16, 2023, Combs was sued (civilly) by one of his ex-girlfriends, Cassandra Ventura, better known as Cassie, a singer and model, who maintained an intermittent relationship with him from 2005 to 2018. During this time, Combs' record label, Bad Boy Records, which he founded in 1993, released her music. The lawsuit alleges a history of terror, as they met when she was 19 years old and he was 35. Almost from the beginning, he started drugging her and forcing her to have encounters with prostitutes, which Combs would record on video. (It is common in almost all denunciations that Combs would film orgies, rapes, aggressions, and sexual encounters in general.) A power dynamic relationship in which Ventura was forced to participate in wild parties with multiple participants that lasted for several days fueled by drugs, lubricant, and baby oil, in her mansions or hotel rooms, as alleged in the lawsuit. A relationship in which she would have been systematically abused, with beatings, black eyes, bruises, blood, and finally, a rape in 2018 when she wanted to end her relationship. Diddy's lawyer denied all the facts on behalf of his client and described the lawsuit as a series of outrageous lies. This is significant because since that November, the detained individual has denied all accusations against them in the same manner. The case was closed extrajudicially the next day (amicably, according to a statement published by both parties), presumably for a substantial amount of money by Combs, the lawyer for Cassie, had pointed out that before the lawsuit, they had been offered an eight-figure sum and Cassie had sued for $30 million. On December 6, 2023, when five women had already reported him (the previously mentioned ones plus an anonymous victim who reported being drugged, gang-raped, and recorded by Combs and his associates when she was 17 years old), Combs wrote on Instagram (in a post now deleted, like all his Instagram except two photos of his daughters) ENOUGH IS ENOUGH. The past few weeks, I have remained silent watching how they tried to destroy my person, my reputation, and my legacy. Sick people in search of quick money have launched unhealthy accusations against me. Let me be as clear as I can be, I did not do any of the horrible things I'm being accused of. I will fight for my name, my family, and the truth. On May 17, 2024, CNN published a video. By then, I had also been sued by Rodney Jones, Jr., a producer (responsible for a significant part of Diddy's latest album, among others), who in February accused Diddy of forcing him to engage in paid sex with third parties and trying to coerce him into having sex with other men, as well as violently threatening him. A similar pattern of behavior has been reported by another one of his former collaborators, his former assistant Phil Pines, in the documentary by Max. In March, the FBI searched Diddy's mansions in Miami and Los Angeles, where they seized dozens of electronic devices that were handed over to the prosecutors investigating the complaints against Combs to verify the accusations. In other words, the hard drives and recording equipment from Combs' orgies were seized. Also, nearly 1 .000 baby oil bottles, a figure later confirmed by the prosecution, and matching Ventura's description. However, on May 17, 2024, CNN publishes a video shot by the Hotel InterContinental's security cameras in Los Angeles, showing Sean Combs kicking Casandra Ventura on the ground. The next day, Combs posts a video on Instagram It's very difficult to look back at the darkest moments of your life, but sometimes you have to do it. I was messed up, I hit rock bottom, but I can't make excuses, my behavior in that video is inexcusable. I take full responsibility for my actions in that video. It makes me sick. It made me sick when I did it. It makes me sick now. That's not a video of apologies; it doesn't ask for Casandra Ventura's forgiveness. Not even she is named. The only person who appears in that statement is Sean Combs. During the week following the video's release, two more women came forward, including actress and model Crystal McKinney, who accused Combs of drugging and forcing her to perform oral sex in a recording studio. A former student who was a teenager when she met Puff Daddy also filed a complaint, alleging four instances of sexual assault between 1995 and 2000. In July, another lawsuit was made public, this one filed by a former adult film actress who accused Combs of coercing and prostituting her at his lavish parties. In June, a man, Derrick Lee Cardello-Smith, who had been convicted of sex crimes and kidnapping, joined the lawsuit, accusing Combs of drugging and raping him in 1997. The lawsuit had been filed in the year of the alleged incident, but was withdrawn after Combs's immense influence. Combs had even visited him in prison after the lawsuit was filed, but he did not appear at the trial (held on September 10) or even virtually, and was ordered to pay $100 million. The case is currently pending appeal. The day after that sentence, another singer from his label, who would be part of Diddy's own crew, reported the rapper for touching, insults, and labor abuses. Five days later, on September 16, federal agents arrested Combs at a hotel in Manhattan. The wild parties are described by the Prosecution as extremely planned events mainly in hotels where drugs were used as a tool for sexual subjugation, and the recording of orgies as an element of extortion to ensure the silence of attendees. The Prosecution also made a call to action after his detention to all possible victims. That was in September. The response has arrived just a few hours ago. Attorney Tony Buzbee announced in October 2024, at a press conference from Texas, a new wave of over 120 lawsuits against Combs, for sexual abuse and assault. Your law firm, allied with AVA Law Group (famous in the United States for their involvement in large-scale sex abuse cases such as the one that led to the bankruptcy of the Boy Scouts of America, following a compensation agreement of over $2.2 billion for victims), aims to bring the partners and accomplices of Combs under the spotlight as well, with the hope of opening a national dialogue. This type of aggression, abuse, and sexual exploitation should never occur, neither in the United States nor anywhere else. It should never have been allowed to go this far. This behavior has created a multitude of hurt, scarred, and scared people. Buzbee revealed that among the 120 plaintiffs (of the almost 3,300 people who have contacted both firms) there are men and women, and that 25 of their represented were minors when the abuse occurred, in some cases even as young as nine years old, captured by Combs when they were seeking a career in the music world. The lawyer stated that in upcoming dates they will reveal the names of the remaining defendants, which will surprise you. Remembering that the Prosecution, in its accusation, spoke of a criminal network, beyond the main responsible, who did not do this alone. For the moment, and while Buzbee has already presented more than 20 of those complaints, the rapper remains the only accused. Puff Daddy, P. Diddy, Diddy, Love, Sean Combs, one of the most successful and influential rappers in the industry, with more than 30 years of career, a multimillionaire, the man whose birthday parties everyone wanted to attend, now faces a judicial path that could bring him sentences of 15 years to life imprisonment. For the indictment, everything points to the fact that the gang's goal was to return Loan, but something must have complicated the process. It is imperative to ensure that girls, boys, and adolescents are afforded the broadest protection of their human rights, specifically, their right of access to justice at any time, Honorable Deputy. In a working meeting of the First Commission of Justice of the LXIV Legislature, the approved bill that reforms article 110, paragraph two of the Penal Code of the State of San Luis PotosÃ­, with the aim of establishing that crimes of sexual abuse committed against minors of age are imprescriptible and the bill to reform the Law of Access of Women to a Life Free of Violence of the State, with the aim of incorporating the concept of interculturality, and patrimonial violence. Representative MarÃ­a Leticia VÃ¡zquez HernÃ¡ndez, chair of the commission, specified that the resolution that amends Article 110 in its second paragraph of the State of San Luis PotosÃ­ Penal Code establishes that the crimes of rape, statutory rape, femicide, qualified homicide, homicide due to family relationship, kidnapping, and forced disappearance of persons are imprescriptible. Similarly, the crimes of sexual abuse, sexual harassment, sexual harassment, and illicit diffusion of images will be imprescriptible when the victim is a minor. In the explanatory statement, it is established that according to the National Survey on the Dynamics of Relations in Households (ENDIREH) 2021 of the National Institute of Statistics and Geography (INEGI), 49.7% of women aged 15 and over stated that they had suffered some form of sexual violence throughout their lives, and 23.3% in the last 12 months. The survey indicates that 12.6% of women aged 15 and over stated that they had suffered child sexual abuse. Regarding the aggressors, 20.8% were identified as uncles or aunts, 17.4% as cousins or nieces, 8.1% as other relatives, 7.1% as brothers or sisters, 6.5% as stepfathers or stepmothers, 5.2% as fathers, 3.6% as grandparents or grandmothers, 0.6% as mothers, and 15.8% as non-relatives. It is evident that sexual crimes committed against children, girls, and adolescents are one of the worst forms of violence against childhood and adolescence. Despite being a growing problem worldwide, most cases go undetected and unreported. Unlike physical violence, whose diagnosis depends on the possibility of seeing the injuries, the detection of girls, boys, and adolescents who are or have been victims of sexual crimes depends on their testimony to know about these crimes. In most cases, there are no physical injuries that serve as evidence of the aggression, nor are there witnesses, as the perpetrator usually commits the crime without anyone observing. He pointed out that girls, boys, and adolescents who are victims of sexual violence often remain silent due to fear, guilt, powerlessness, or shame, so that only the passage of time in some cases allows them to speak about what happened, about the aggression they suffered, as humiliation and the fear of being stigmatized accompany them throughout their lives. Therefore, it is essential to guarantee girls, boys, and adolescents the broadest protection of their human rights, specifically their right of access to justice at any time, without there being room for impunity derived from the prescription of the crime. The First Commission of Justice also approved the resolution that reforms articles 8, section XIV, and 30, section I, and adds articles 3, section VII Bis, and 4, section XII Bis of the Law of Women's Access to a Life Free of Violence in the State of San Luis PotosÃ­, to remain as follows:Article 3, section VII Bis. InterculturalityThe intercultural approach is based on the recognition and respect of existing cultural differences, under the conception that cultures can be different from each other but equally valid, with no superior or inferior cultures existing. It is aimed at addressing the particularities of women from indigenous peoples, Afro-descendants, and other differentiated ethnic groups and their relationship with the dominant society, beyond the coexistence of cultures.Article 4, section XII Bis. Patrimonial ViolenceIt is any act or omission that affects the survival of the victim. . It manifests itself in the transformation, removal, destruction, retention, or distraction of personal objects, documents, property, and economic resources intended to meet their needs and can encompass damage to common or personal goods of the victim. Article 8, XIV. To access comprehensive, intercultural, multidisciplinary, transversal, and under the same roof care in justice centers for women. Article 30, I. To train the Investigating Police, prosecutors of the Public Ministry, experts, and all personnel responsible for the prosecution of justice to attend to cases of violence against women with a gender perspective, interculturality, and full respect for the human rights of women, and in accordance with specialized protocols, evaluating their performance permanently. The opinions will be put to the consideration of the Plenary Session of the State Congress for analysis and voting.

La Paz, January 31, 2025 (ANF). Vehicle theft, extortion, favoritism towards inmates, sale of arms, and sexual abuse are the scandals that were recorded in the first month of 2025 in which members of the Bolivian Police were involved. The latest case to come to light is this Friday, the governor of the Uyuni prison, Ruddy G.R.R., and five other police officers were implicated in a criminal gang that was dedicated to stealing vehicles in the Oruro department. The uniformed officers are being investigated for dereliction of duty, criminal organization, and other crimes. A case was opened for benefits due to position, dereliction of duty, criminal organization, and other crimes that have led to an arrest. The governor of the Uyuni prison has been apprehended, in total, two people have been apprehended and four have been arrested, explained the district attorney of Oruro, Aldo Morales. According to the Disciplinary Court's report, in 2024, at least 600 uniformed personnel were temporarily and permanently dismissed for violating Law 101 of the Disciplinary Regime. So far this year, 10 police officers were irreversibly severed. In this regard, the Minister of Government, Eduardo Del Castillo, assured that those uniformed personnel involved in different illicit activities will not be allowed to continue tarnishing the image of that institution. He stated that they are conducting a sweep of the bad police officers across the country. So that by the next administration, we will not have bad elements within the Bolivian police. Therefore, we are conducting a sweep across the national territory. We have started in Santa Cruz where we have apprehended them, the same in the PotosÃ­ department and now in La Paz. If there are corrupt police officers, violators, they will not be police officers anymore, they will not continue to stain the institution and they must be in jail, he declared. The CasesOn January 3, Sergeant Brian C. Ch. brutally assaulted his partner after attending a social event in Oruro, was apprehended and prosecuted for family violence. Days later, his permanent dismissal was determined. In the previous administration, this officer received an award from the Ministry of Government for his work in unblocking roads that were blocked by sectors aligned with Evo Morales for over 20 days.On January 21, the second case was reported, when Carlos F. P. filed a complaint against four police officers from the Criminal Analysis and Intelligence Department (DACI) for the theft of $139,000, threats, and extortion. The officers were apprehended this Friday and are being investigated for concussive and passive corrupt practices. The case was registered on December 30, after the victim was robbed by five criminals who wanted to buy dollars, and they went to the police to report the incident. However, the free trader was assaulted and extorted by the police. A day later, the former commander of the Border Police of Chiquitania, Luis Fernando L. G., was apprehended and accused of sexually abusing his ex-partner who has a physical disability. After a hearing on precautionary measures, a judge from Santa Cruz ordered his preventive detention at Palmasola prison. On January 26, at Chonchocoro prison, Brazilian citizen Da Silva Tabaras murdered Nabor LÃ³pez after being attacked with a firearm. The aggressor stated that he bought the device from a policeman for Bs 4,000, who is being processed for complicity. The latest scandal emerged two days later, when a captain identified as Humberto F. C. and three civilians were sent to prison after being accused of leading an armed gang that specialized in hijacking undocumented vehicles, extorting, and kidnapping their victims. According to the investigations, these individuals operated in Comarapa, Mairana and Samaipata, in the department of Santa Cruz. When approaching their victims, they identified themselves as agents of the National Directorate for Prevention of Vehicle Theft (Diprove). Commission On the other hand, Del Castillo stated that there is a commission inside the green olive that is evaluating the different cases to obtain the definitive dismissal of the uniformed personnel who were involved in those illicit acts. There is a commission within the Bolivian Police and, respecting the current regulations, it will achieve the dismissal of all these elements, so that they do not return to the institution as they did in the past, he specified.

text: The last victim of police officer Jhon Choque Valdez is going through a true ordeal. Despite needing support from state institutions, the National Police is investigating her for the alleged crime of drug trafficking. According to Jaime Montalico, the family's lawyer, the Anti-Drug Department summoned the victim's mother to testify about the alleged possession of drugs and human trafficking. Confused by the summons, the mother appeared before the non-commissioned officer who had summoned her, who confirmed that the investigation is against the minor. How is it possible for the victim to be processed, the lawyer emphasized. EMOTIONAL CRISIS Montalico described the difficult situation the minor went through when she was subjected to Officer Jhon Choque. He mentioned that the victim told the Gessel camera that the officer threatened her with a firearm to assault her, and forced her to consume drugs. Due to the sub-officer Jhon Choque Valdez's attacks, the minor received medical, psychological, and psychiatric treatment to restore her health. Nevertheless, the investigation initiated by the Anti-Drugs Department would have affected her mental health again. For the lawyer, this situation would have pushed her to attempt to take her own life by ingesting 30 sleeping pills that the doctors had prescribed for her. It was known that the mother noticed in the morning of this Friday that her daughter was convulsing in her bedroom. The afternoon of the previous day, the hearing for preventive detention against the sub-officer Jhon Choque Valdez had taken place. WOMEN'S EMERGENCY CENTER Another unfavorable aspect for the well-being of the adolescent, According to the lawyer Montalico's report, is a report issued by the Women's Emergency Center to the Special Protection Unit, which indicates that the minor is in a situation of abandonment This situation could have separated her from her mother, had it not been for the good offices of the lawyer to prevent the breakage of said family bond. The family defense detailed that the mother of the family even resigned from her job to provide the necessary care to her daughter.

Prince Andrew, the brother of King Charles III of England, was in contact with the late millionaire Jeffrey Epstein, convicted of child sex trafficking crimes, for a longer period than he had previously admitted, according to emails published by British media outlets. The Duke of York allegedly sent a message to the deceased American financier in which it is evident that their relationship continued. A message sent in February 2011 reads: "I'll be in touch soon and we can play a bit more," as revealed by documents in the possession of the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). In an interview with the BBC Newsnight program, Prince Andrew told journalist Emily Maitlis that he had not seen or spoken to Epstein since visiting the businessman's home in New York in December 2010, a meeting that he himself described as a bad decision, which was captured by photographers. The email questioning the prince's testimony was distributed during a judicial case involving the FCA and banker Jes Staley, who has been barred from leadership positions due to his relationship with Epstein. Staley appealed the FCA in a judicial case in which the evidence presented by that agency on his contacts with the magnate also includes emails related to a member of the royal family, presumably Andrew, and shows the exchanges between the duke and Epstein. In the aforementioned interview with the BBC, the prince was questioned about the magnitude of his association with Epstein and said that his relationship with the magnate had ceased after becoming aware that the latter was being investigated at the end of 2006. The royal said he was not in contact with the financier until 2010, when a photographer captured an image of the prince and Epstein walking in New York. When asked specifically if he saw or spoke to Epstein again after that meeting, AndrÃ©s replied that he did not, which contradicts the recently released legal documents.

In general, girls who experience unwanted pregnancies have no resources, and the state does not recognize any alternatives for them to continue their studies or develop. This complicates the detection of the violence itself and the family environment takes a long time to become aware. text: The SBS reported advances in the care of Lev Tahor community children, following court orders. Meetings have been held to evaluate their situation and they have been offered registration in Integral Care Centers. Authorities from the Social Welfare Secretariat reported that progress has been made in the care of Lev Tahor community children, although the process is complex due to the legal challenges it involves. Marvin Rabanales, head of that department, assured that actions are being carried out in strict compliance with judicial dispositions. Up to this point, two meetings have been held to evaluate the situation of minors and continue dialogue, with the goal of ensuring their integral well-being. As part of the measures, they have been offered the possibility of registering in any of the country's Integral Care Centers (CAI), where they could receive specialized support and follow-up. However, the authorities admit that finding a definitive solution is not an easy task, as the case presents multiple legal and social facets that require a careful approach. In this context, the Public Ministry and the National Civil Police arrested Aaron Teller, 60 years old, and Yosef Rosner, 52, members of the Lev Tahor sect, at a hotel in the capital's zone 1 on January 30. Both are accused of child abuse and human trafficking, specifically for forced marriages. Rosner, close to the founder of the sect, had been detained in 2022 in Mexico for similar crimes but was released due to lack of evidence. According to investigations, he is responsible for performing forced marriages between girls and members of the sect. The MP, together with the PGN and Interpol, carried out raids in search of 11 minors with Alert AlbaKeneth, without success. Currently, 160 children rescued from the sect are under the custody of the PGN. The Lev Tahor sect arrived in Guatemala over a decade ago, fleeing Canada, where they were being investigated for abuses. In November 2024, four minors escaped and reported physical abuse and forced marriages, prompting an operation that resulted in the rescue of 160 children and the discovery of skeletons in boxes. Authorities insist that this case is not an attack on a religion, but rather an action to protect minors and enforce the law. The case remains under investigation. By Andrea Palacios.

On her first day of work at a pizzeria in Tenancingo, Tlaxcala, a 13-year-old girl who had been reported missing since December 7 was located by the municipality's Gender Police. The minor had gone to the establishment in search of a job and was where she was finally rescued. We were notified by the prosecutor's office about people, through a bulletin that the minor was missing since December 7, and the search began in our municipality and neighboring municipalities, but we didn't have a report. In contrast, they confirmed that she had fled her home due to situations of domestic violence. She begins to cry, I tell her not to cry, to calm down, that everything will be okay, that we will notify her family members since she is a minor and cannot walk alone, she cannot take care of herself yet. She comments that she did not want to see her family members, Rivera reported.It may interest you that Sandy was found charred and tied to her bed in Tlaxcala, neighbors attempted to lynch her partner. The police protected the minor found working at a pizzeria. The municipal police took care of the minor and took her statement, while the Specialized Prosecutor's Office for Missing and Unlocated Persons (FEPDNL) will determine if a crime was committed against her.According to the minor's testimony, she decided to leave her home on her own volition, due to the constant mistreatment she received from her grandmother. She left her house on her own because her grandmother was mistreating her. Her grandmother told her that if she didn't like living at her house, she could leave. And that's what she did, she grabbed her things and left, that's what the minor said, the commander detailed. The minor left her home and pays rent with her own resources. The minor's identity is kept confidential for legal reasons. It is known that she is the daughter of absent parents, as her father abandoned her and her sister when they were young, while her mother works in Campeche, so she was under the care of her grandmother, who allegedly mistreated her. During the time she was missing, the minor spent more than a month outside her home. According to police reports, she lived in an apartment in the city of Puebla, where she managed to support herself by paying rent with her own resources. They Find Girl at PizzeriaFinally, her whereabouts were discovered when she returned to Tenancingo and sought employment at a pizzeria located in the Centro neighborhood. The owners of the establishment hired her without knowing her situation, but upon seeing her missing person's notice on social media, they notified the Municipal Police to avoid any legal issues. Upon being rescued, the minor burst into tears and reiterated that she did not want to return to her family. She commented that she did not want to see her relatives because her mother and father were not in the municipality and she was under the protection of her grandmother, Rivera reiterated. The minor was turned over to FEPDNL personnel through the municipal DIF, who will determine the necessary protective measures for her safety and well-being. In Santa Cruz, a 27-year-old man named VÃ­ctor H. S. D. has been sentenced to 18 years in prison for the crimes of child corruption, statutory rape, and child pornography. This sentence was issued after the defendant pleaded guilty in a streamlined procedure hearing. The abuse was perpetrated against three minors aged four, eight, and 12, who are currently under the protection of the Child and Adolescent Defense Office. The sentence was issued this Friday at the Palmasola prison facility. Judicial Process Prosecutor Mijael Cavero reported that the defendant chose to undergo a streamlined procedure hearing, where he acknowledged his guilt in the crimes he was charged with. VÃ­ctor H. S. D. was apprehended on Wednesday at a residence located in the Plan Tres Mil area, after being identified as the perpetrator of the abuses through pornographic videos. These videos showed the three minors, who are relatives of the aggressor. The investigation was initiated ex officio, as records of images and videos of sexual content involving the victims were found from 2021 to the present date. Protection of the victims The departmental prosecutor of Santa Cruz, Alberto Zeballos Flores, emphasized the importance of rescuing and protecting the girls, boys, and adolescents who have been victims of abuse. The minors have already made their statement in the Gesell Chamber of the Prosecutor's Office, under the supervision of psychologists from the Forensic Investigation Institute (IDIF). Zeballos assured that the victims will receive comprehensive attention and protection, in accordance with the current legislation. The justice seeks to guarantee the well-being of the minors affected by this very serious case.
