Convicted of Abusing Nine-Year-Old Granddaughter During Confinement in Alicante The verdict considers proven that the accused got into the bed of the minor while she was sleeping The Provincial Court has sentenced a 71-year-old man to four years and three months in prison for sexually abusing his granddaughter, according to the sentence that this newspaper has had access to. The abuses occurred during confinement at the accused's home in Alicante when she was nine years old. The family was in that house temporarily in those months, where the little girl would stay to sleep at her grandfather's house. The sentence, issued by a Third Section court, considers proven that, on the morning of April 16, 2020, the accused took advantage of the fact that the girl had gone to his residence to spend a night to enter the room where she was sleeping next to a 13-year-old cousin, to pick her up in her arms without her waking up and take her to another room. There the sexual abuse took place. The girl told her cousin what had happened, who in turn told her mother, the victim's aunt. Finally, the victim's father filed a complaint. The accused denied the allegations during his testimony in court, claiming that he had only accompanied her at night to the bathroom and left her alone there. However, the court gave credibility to the victim's version based on her testimony and the account given by her cousin and aunt. The minor reported that she was sleeping and found her grandmother licking her when she woke up at night. The verdict notes that no ulterior motives have been detected that would have motivated a false complaint against the defendant, nor that they would try to avenge or benefit at the expense of the accused. The court considers the testimony consistent and without any contradiction. The experts also evaluated the credibility of her testimony in the most relevant aspects. The testimony has been maintained throughout the trial with detail, without any signs of fabrication or exaggeration against the accused, he stated. In this line, the victim herself said that she would be willing to forgive the accused and that she understood that he was not aware of what he had done, but that she would be afraid to stay with him alone. Without DNA evidence The minor was subjected to an emergency examination at the hospital after the report of sexual abuse, but the DNA tests were unable to find anything determinative. Nonetheless, the court's own ruling admits that due to the time elapsed, these biological remains could have fortuitously dissipated. A circumstance that, for the judges, does not generate any doubts about the victim's testimony. The ruling ensures that the accused took advantage of his position of superiority, given the age difference between him and his victim and the existing family relationship, as well as the circumstance of the events occurring in the accused's own home, in the secrecy of the night, and taking advantage of the fact that the minor was sleeping. In addition to the penalty of deprivation of liberty, the judicial resolution establishes the measure of separation at a minimum distance of 500 meters from the victim for a period of nine years, as well as eight years of supervised liberty, and the payment of a compensation of 15,000 euros to the minor in consideration of the moral damages suffered. The magistrates estimate that the facts affected the normal psychological development of the minor. The sentence is not final and is appealable in appeal before the Superior Court of Justice of the Valencian Community (TSJCV) within a period of ten days from its notification. text: INVESTIGATION PelÃ¡ez Case The testimony of the therapeutic team of the complainant could favor the San Juan surgeon The case of the San Juan surgeon FabiÃ¡n PelÃ¡ez added a new chapter with the declaration of two mental health professionals who treated his ex-partner, the young woman who denounced him for having drugged and forced her into prostitution. A psychologist and a psychiatrist provided details on the consumption of drugs and the participation in sexual parties of the complainant, information that could favor the San Juan doctor in the accusation of human trafficking. Both professionals were interrogated as witnesses by Judge MarÃ­a Eugenia Capuchetti, while they await the young woman's recovery and can do so in CÃ¡mara Gesell. These declarations were published by Infobae and in them there are details of how the consumption of drugs and the sexual parties that the surgeon and his girlfriend organized. The psychologist stated that the surgeon's girlfriend has been undergoing therapy on a discontinuous basis for the past two years. The lack of a consistent pattern is due to her mental state, which does not always allow her to attend, according to the professional. What motivated the start of the sessions, the psychologist replied, was the difficulty in cohabiting with the assembled family that she maintains with her partner. The woman lives alone in a house that PelÃ¡ez has rented for six months, since they stopped living together due to a violent episode that cost her a perimeter restriction on one of the surgeon's children. According to what the patient herself stated during the sessions, the sexual practices she carried out with the doctor (threesomes) were not against her will and always had her consent. However, she did conflict with the choice of the third person who got involved in the couple. Due to jealousy, the couple would look at the other person more, she pointed out. The psychologist noted that the consumption of substances (mainly cocaine and ecstasy) on weekends destabilized her a lot. He denied, at the same time, that PelÃ¡ez forced her to consume. She consumed with him by choice, he detailed, and revealed that the woman always felt like doing it before a party. He emphasized that the consumption always went hand in hand with the threesomes they carried out. She carried out what she wanted, he put it into action, he underscored. It was something mutual, it was proactive between both. It responded to the logic of her partner, he expanded. However, this consumption had consequences for her mood. It did not collaborate at all in her emotional fluctuations, especially after consumption, which generated difficulties for her to connect in her family dynamics, in her studies. She was more irritable and unstable. She couldn't continue with her activities, he mentioned. No, never, she said firmly when asked if she had ever mentioned that her partner prostituted her or put her in a situation of subjugation of her autonomy. At the request of the Prosecution, she was asked if the patient had ever mentioned that the accused put her in a position of subjugation that definitively eroded her autonomy. Never, she assured. On the other hand, she reported that the last time she saw her, she noticed that she was disoriented from her studies, from her sports. When the woman began treatment, the psychologist noticed that she was self-medicating, so he insisted that she initiate psychiatric treatment. The patient agreed. Her first consultation with her current psychiatrist was in October 2024. She reported feeling very anxious and more irritable. Since then, she has attended the clinic four times. Although time was not enough to diagnose the patient, the doctor suspected, in a short time, that she suffered from a mood disorder, so she prescribed lithium, quetiapine, and paroxetine to stabilize her. She was aware that, in addition, she was taking clonazepam. The treatment takes time. There was no total response until I saw her (NdR in January), we could not say that the treatment was being totally effective, emphasized the psychiatrist, who also denied that the woman had mentioned to her that her partner had forced her to consume drugs. The doctor also pointed out that the weekend consumption referred to by the patient could affect the treatment. It affects the evolution, the result, it is not a good combination, the psychopharmaceuticals with the substances, always suggested that when a treatment begins, neither alcohol nor any other substance should be consumed, she specified. In the case of the protected identity witness, she stated that after consuming mainly cocaine and ecstasy, she felt anxious and distressed. Another important point she referred to in her statement is her willingness to travel to Buenos Aires. The psychiatrist assured that the patient had told her that she was going on vacation. She also denied having mentioned having experienced any situation of sexual subjugation.

text: Amnesty International Denounces Abuses Against Temporary Workers in Canada Erika Guevara Rosas, AI's Director of Research and Campaigns, has made statements Temporary migrant workers harvesting fruits in a farm in Quebec. Amnesty International denounces that Canada's Temporary Foreign Workers Program is vulnerable to abuses such as discriminatory treatment, excessive working hours, and subjection to a single employer. Image Maggie MacPherson/URL/CBC The Temporary Foreign Workers Program (TFWP) that Canada maintains facilitates shocking abuses and the discrimination of migrant workers, Amnesty International (AI) human rights organization reported in its latest report Erika Guevara Rosas, director of research and campaigns at AI, said that the abuses experienced by migrant workers in Canada are extremely concerning, especially considering a country that claims to be a leader in protecting human rights. The report, titled "Canada Has Destroyed Me: Exploitation of Migrant Workers," exposes the impact of the TFWP, which allows employers (both corporations and individuals) to hire migrant workers primarily for low-paying jobs. The sectors that most employ this workforce are agriculture, food processing, the care system, construction, and hospitality. TFWP visas tie these individuals to a single employer who controls their immigration status and working conditions. Guevara Rosas stated that many migrant people have told us that they arrived in Canada with the hope of obtaining a better future, but instead, they felt treated like slaves. These workers and workers are vital in putting food on the tables of the country and caring for the elderly. They deserve much better, he added.AI based its report on interviews conducted in 2023 and 2024 in the provinces of Quebec and Ontario with 44 people who were former workers under the TFWP program, many of whom reported unpaid wages and excessive working hours. Some contracts viewed by AI stipulated zero days of rest. Additionally, some people reported that their employers and supervisors used racist language towards them and insulted them by calling them donkey, Indian, or Mexican shit. One of the cases documented in the report is that of Benedicte, a woman from Cameroon, who suffered racist psychological and sexual abuse by her employer as soon as she arrived in Canada in 2015, with a two-year tied visa to work on a farm. She was forced to work between 70 and 80 hours a week performing agricultural and other tasks, including domestic work, and was significantly underpaid and subjected to constant control. Her employer deceived her, promising to bring her children to Canada, in order to continue exploiting her. Finally, she fell ill and was diagnosed with a severe anemia. When she finally left the farm in July 2018, her employer cancelled her visa, leaving her in an irregular migratory situation. She told the interviewers, "I didn't expect to be a slave here." Many migrant workers under the TFWP program live and work in remote areas, and therefore their accommodation and access to medical insurance and transportation depend on their employer. If they fall ill, suffer an injury, or are no longer deemed fit for work, their contract can be terminated and they may be subject to rapid repatriation. Some workers and workers reported that their employer had threatened them with repatriation and, in a few cases, had taken them to the airport against their will. Many workers and workers do not report the abuses they suffer due to fear of retaliation such as wrongful dismissal, non-renewal of their contract, and repatriation, the report states. Those who do report have to deal with the complex law enforcement system that is not designed to protect precarious individuals and those who often do not know how to navigate the bureaucratic systems in either of Canada's official languages, English and French. In 2023, the first countries of origin of Tfwp workers were Mexico, India, the Philippines, Guatemala, and Jamaica, which represented almost 70% of work permits issued. Guevara Rosas said that Canadian authorities are well aware of the abuses committed under the Tfwp framework and have still implemented very limited measures to address some of them, such as increasing inspections. In particular, AI requires work permits to be issued openly, as migrant workers must have the freedom to change jobs and employers, just like Canadians, concluded Guevara Rosas. text: Investigative agents and police were able to apprehend a man who threatened a 10-year-old girl with a knife to conceal his crimes, credit FiscalÃ­a. A 45-year-old man was detained in the municipality of Piedecuesta, in the department of Santander, after being accused of subjecting his stepdaughter, a 10-year-old girl, to repeated sexual abuse. According to a report by the Attorney General's Office, the incidents occurred while the man lived with the girl's mother and took advantage of the moments when the girl was under his care to commit the crimes. The arrest was carried out by agents of the Technical Investigation Body (CTI) in collaboration with the National Police, in an operation conducted in the JunÃ­n neighborhood of Piedecuesta. Now you can follow us on Facebook and our WhatsApp Channel. According to the investigations, the accused not only abused the minor, but also threatened her with a knife to prevent her from reporting the incidents. The District Attorney detailed that the man subjected the girl to all kinds of sexual humiliations during the time she lived with her mother in a residence in the municipality. The situation came to light when the victim's family decided to file a criminal complaint, which allowed the authorities to initiate the corresponding investigations and gather evidence against the alleged perpetrator. A family decided to face their fear and denounce, initiating an investigation that ended with the arrest of a man in the JunÃ­n neighborhood.The accused was presented before the First Penal Municipal Court with Mixed Functions of Piedecuesta, where the charges of acts of a sexual nature with a minor under 14 years old in concurrence with violent carnal access were imputed. Although the man did not accept the charges, the judge ordered his detention in a penitentiary center while the judicial process advances against him. The subject will be transferred to a prison in the department of Santander. The authorities also highlighted the gravity of the threats that the man exercised over the minor. According to reports, the accused used a knife to intimidate her and ensure her silence, which prolonged the time in which the abuses remained hidden. However, the complaint presented by the family members allowed the facts to be investigated and the capture of the alleged aggressor to be achieved. Lieutenant Colonel Claudia SuÃ¡rez, head of Childhood and Adolescence of the National Police, pointed out that minors between the ages of 6 and 12 are the most affected by cases of sexual abuse in the country. This case in Piedecuesta is added to a worrying statistic that reflects the vulnerability of children in family and close environments. According to the authorities, the trust deposited in figures such as stepfathers or caregivers is, in many cases, taken advantage of to commit this type of crime.

Following the serious incidents that occurred, the Police deployed Special Services personnel to evacuate the suspected perpetrator from their residence to prevent a lynching. The events took place at the beginning of this Saturday in a residence located on Patagonia Street 400, between Cambaceres and Islas de los Estados streets (Chacra II neighborhood). The suspected perpetrator was identified as Horacio Miranda, a 38-year-old man, who is known in the area because he is often seen under the influence of drugs, according to eyewitnesses. According to the complaint, a grandmother of the child reported that Miranda allegedly molested her grandson, stating that he hugged and attempted to kiss him, clarifying that it appeared he was intoxicated or under the influence of a substance. This generated a reaction from other relatives who were participating in a social gathering, who went to the residence of the alleged abuser with the intention of assaulting him and taking justice into their own hands. Alerted to the situation, police personnel arrived at the scene to dissuade the protesters, but seeing themselves outnumbered, they requested the presence of reinforcements, so the presence of Special Services was ordered. In this way, the anti-riot unit proceeded to clear the street to allow Miranda to leave the house to be transported to a safe location. It is worth noting that during the violent incidents, the father of the minor was identified breaking down the gate of the residence of Miranda's family, so a formal penal complaint was made for damages. In addition, at the Women's and Family Police Station, the mother of the minor filed a formal complaint, initiating an investigation into alleged sexual abuse, charging Horacio Miranda, who was known in the area for having a history of sexual abuse and making advances to minors in public. Regarding the violent incidents that occurred at Miranda's residence, the case was handed over to the Investigating Court, presided over by Judge RaÃºl Sahade, who ordered measures to be taken to ensure the safety of the family of the alleged abuser.

Charges 5, 6, 7: Aggravated criminal sexual contact (third-degree crime). Charge 8: Criminal sexual contact (fourth-degree crime). Charge 9: Endangering the welfare of a minor (third-degree crime). A woman who lived in a nursing home was allegedly abused by a man who was related to the retiree. The incident occurred on Wednesday night, when a complaint was filed against a suspect in a suspected case of sexual abuse perpetrated against a woman who lives in a nursing home in the city of Tandil. Judicial proceedings began to be carried out last Friday, at the institution located on Chacabuco street at 200, and a response from the provincial government is expected. According to local media, the man was removed from the site and an order was issued for a restraining order to approach the geriatric until his guilt or innocence can be proven in the case. Additionally, they mentioned that the complaint was filed by a man resident of the establishment, who allegedly managed to provide some film evidence. On the other hand, the supposed victim, being in a critical health situation and bedridden, after the case was reported, was transferred to the Hospital Santamarina to be evaluated. The complaint was handed over to UFI 16, led by Dr. Marcos Eguzquiza, who ordered a series of measures, including a home search, a measure granted by the Guarantee Court, which was carried out on Friday afternoon.

31 women victims of human trafficking form thanks to scholarships from the Madrid City Council Participants have received training in two areas: commerce and surface and furniture cleaning in establishments and buildings A total of 31 women victims of human trafficking have completed a training itinerary promoted and subsidized by the Madrid City Council, which aims to facilitate their social and labor inclusion. Specifically, this program, which already has several promotions, is aimed at women who have managed to leave situations of prostitution or are in the process of doing so. Participants have received training in two areas: commerce and surface and furniture cleaning in establishments and buildings. In addition to facilitating these women's economic autonomy through employment, this project also allows for the strengthening of their self-esteem and providing them with support in building a new life, leaving behind the situation of violence they suffered, as indicated by the City Council. The courses were held in the last quarter of 2024 at Mercamadrid and Educarte facilities, and each consisted of 480 hours of academic load, including theoretical content, digital skills acquisition, and job search and non-employment practices skills. The Delegate of Social Policies, Family, and Equality, JosÃ© FernÃ¡ndez, has handed out diplomas to the participants this week, recognizing that they have successfully completed this training process. You are an example of self-empowerment and determination, and the diplomas you hold are a testament to your strength in difficult times, the municipal delegate highlighted at the closing ceremony of the course. During the same, FernÃ¡ndez also emphasized that this municipal initiative is an indispensable gateway to economic and personal independence for these women, providing them with the ability to break free from their past and look towards the future, pursuing new goals, new dreams, to continue playing an important role in society.MADRID'S RED MUNICIPAL The Madrid City Council has a comprehensive Municipal Network for Attention to Women Victims of Gender Violence, with specific resources for women who have been abused in the context of a couple or ex-partner, for cases of sexual violence, and situations of sexual trafficking and exploitation. In the specific area of trafficking, the City Council has the ConcepciÃ³n Arenal Comprehensive Care Center, a device that offers psychological and social intervention and legal advice to victims. Within this resource, a mobile unit also operates, whose objective is to approach women victims of trafficking for sexual exploitation and in contexts of prostitution in different areas or spaces of the city of Madrid, facilitating information and directing interested parties to specialized municipal services. Additionally, since December 2021, the Mariana Pineda Emergency Center for Victims of Trafficking has been operational, in which protected housing and comprehensive care are provided to users for a maximum period of three months. Madrid allocates 17 million euros for a new center to help women leave prostitution. To continue the intervention process, if necessary, the City Council also has Casa Pandora, a protected housing facility where women subjected to trafficking and other human rights abuses in prostitution contexts can stay for up to 12 months, and the semi-autonomous apartment Malala, where basic needs are met while women focus on forging an independent life.

The Special Force for Fighting Crime (Felcc) apprehended a 51-year-old man who was being sought for the crime of sexual abuse of a six-year-old girl, an incident that occurred in the municipality of Villa Tunari, a region in the Cochabamba Tropics. The arrest was made after an operation, following knowledge that the suspect had fled the scene of the crime. According to the police report, upon learning that the authorities were on his trail, the alleged perpetrator of the crime sought refuge in another community, where the community leaders went so far as to attempt to settle the crime between the defendant and the relatives of the victim. However, after an intelligence operation, personnel from the Felcc located the exact location where the investigated person was hiding, and with the presence of the Public Ministry and the Defender of the Childhood, they arrived at his residence and proceeded with his apprehension. The 51-year-old man was transported to police cells to give his statement to the corresponding authorities, while the leaders who protected him will also be summoned to declare about the facts. Now the victim is under the protection of the Defender of the Child and the investigated person will appear before the jurisdictional authority of the municipality of Villa Tunari.

In a stunning turn of events in the entertainment world, Daphne Joy, known for her relationship with rapper 50 Cent, has been accused of being a sex worker for Sean Combs, better known as P Diddy. This accusation has arisen in the context of a lawsuit that amounts to a staggering $30 million. The news has caused a stir on social media and has captured the attention of the media, generating speculation about the nature of relationships in the entertainment industry. Daphne Joy, model and actress, has been at the center of attention since she began her relationship with 50 Cent. However, her personal life has taken an unexpected turn following these accusations. The lawsuit, filed by a former employee of Diddy, alleges that Joy was part of an environment that promoted illegal activities and immoral behavior. This type of allegation not only affects Daphne but also puts Diddy's reputation at stake, who has been a prominent figure in the music industry for decades. The lawsuit details impactful situations that, according to the plaintiff, are part of a pattern of behavior involving various celebrities. It is alleged that Diddy used his influence and power to attract young women to his circle, where lavish parties took place and, according to the accusations, sexual activities occurred. Daphne Joy's inclusion in this narrative has been especially contentious given her past with 50 Cent, adding a level of drama to the situation. Joy's lawyers have vigorously denied the accusations, arguing that they are unfounded and that their client has no involvement in the allegations of prostitution or sex trafficking. According to them, these statements are part of a strategy to discredit public figures and obtain financial gains at the expense of their reputation. In a world where social media can make or break careers, the pressure on Joy is palpable. The situation has led to a broader discussion about consent and exploitation in the entertainment industry. Many women have shared their own experiences, opening up a debate about power and vulnerability in relationships where there is a clear status difference. This case could be a catalyst for more people to speak about their own truth, although the personal cost may be high. Meanwhile, P Diddy has remained silent, dodging questions in interviews about the case. His legal team has commented that they are prepared to fight the accusations in court, but the damage to his image has already been done. The celebrity culture is often marred by scandals, and this could be one of the most significant in recent years. In conclusion, the accusation against Daphne Joy and her supposed connection to P Diddy raises disturbing questions about ethics and morality in the entertainment world. As the lawsuit progresses, the public will be attentive to every development, knowing that behind each headline lie complex and often painful human stories. The entertainment industry, with its glamour and glitz, can also be a dark place, where hidden truths are finally exposed.

Due to the large number of attempts at illegal crossing and human trafficking and narcotics smuggling, the state hosts a large number of checkpoints distributed throughout the region. These checkpoints are designed to cover critical areas and prevent people from crossing the border without proper documentation. Most Border Patrol checkpoints in Texas are located along the southern border, from the city of El Paso to the Rio Grande. These points extend into urban, rural, and even desert areas, allowing authorities to maintain constant surveillance of entry and exit routes into the country. In addition to land-based checkpoints, the U.S. Border Patrol in Texas has a significant presence in maritime and airport ports, which are used by both migrants and drug traffickers. The Venezuelan in Colombia Thousands of Venezuelans in the United States and Mexico face serious difficulties returning to their country due to the impossibility of obtaining safe passage documents. The suspension of the digital request system and the restrictions imposed by the authorities have left many stranded, without clear options to return. The lack of response from the Venezuelan Foreign Ministry and the bureaucratic requirements have generated protests and distress calls from those affected. Meanwhile, human rights organizations have pointed out that the refusal to issue these documents could infringe on citizens' right to return to their nation. System failures and lack of official response Since late 2022, the process of requesting safe passage documents, which was previously done in person at the Venezuelan Embassy in Mexico, had migrated to a digital system accessible from the United States However, the problems on the platform have left many migrants with no options. A Venezuelan mother in Georgia reported that her daughter has failed to obtain the document, as the embassy does not respond to emails or messages. When she went to the Foreign Ministry in Venezuela, she was informed that the only way to process it was from Mexico, which makes the process impossible for those with expired passports and cannot leave the US. Migrants stranded in Mexico without options to return In Mexico, the situation is similar. A group of Venezuelans held a protest in front of the Embassy in Mexico City demanding the activation of the safe-conducts. Among them, a woman identified as Marian reported that, despite her need to return, the document was denied, and instead, she was asked to process a new passport for $320. The closure of the CBP One platform on January 20 left many migrants without the possibility of seeking asylum in the US. Forcing them to seek alternatives to return to Venezuela. However, the lack of documentation has made their return almost impossible. Those who can obtain the safe conduct permit Venezuelans to travel to their country in case of loss, theft, or expiration of their passport. The issuance of this document costs $60, although certain groups are exempt from payment, such as minors, repatriates, detainees with deportation orders, and victims of human trafficking. As of October 2, 2024, certain Venezuelans with expired passports no longer need this document to return, such as those with dual nationality or legal residency in another country. However, no explanations have been given as to why some require the safe conduct permit and others do not. Vulnerable rights and demands of those affected Many Venezuelans cite Article 50 of the Constitution, which establishes that every citizen has the right to enter their country without the need for authorization. Human rights organizations have pointed out that the lack of response from the Venezuelan government and the barriers imposed violate this fundamental right. Migrants stranded in the US and Mexico continue to demand immediate solutions to return to their country without bureaucratic obstacles and without the need to pay high sums for documents that should be expedited. The Venezuelan migratory crisis continues to generate difficulties for thousands of citizens who want to return to their country. Bureaucratic tasks, the lack of response from authorities, and digital system problems have left many in a state of uncertainty. While those affected continue to demand solutions, it remains in the hands of the Venezuelan government to ensure that its citizens can exercise their right to return without unjustifiable impediments.

Traumatizados by the process of surrender. They pounded on bathroom doors to ensure no one was hiding inside. And most importantly (...) they did all this without presenting a single name with a single judicial order, she denounced. The Trump administration had warned the previous Tuesday, through the Department of Homeland Security, that criminals would no longer be able to hide in US schools and churches to avoid arrest. This policy, implemented since 2011, prevented immigration agents from arresting people in sensitive locations such as schools, churches, and hospitals. In the first days of Trump's presidency, 538 immigrants have been detained, according to ICE. The President told journalists on Friday that deportations are going well. We're getting rid of the bad ones, the toughest criminals. These are people who have been as bad as anyone you've ever seen. We're getting rid of them first. The criteria presented by Trump to combat illegal immigration are that undocumented individuals have committed some crime. This is just a small preview of the work being done by the Trump administration to protect the borders of our nation, said the White House. The deportation of undocumented migrants in the United States can be expedited for those who entered the country without going through a checkpoint or a court hearing in an immigration court. The president invokes the Alien Enemies Act of 1798 to eliminate the presence of all gangs, such as the Venezuelan Aragua Train. A foreigner can be deported from the United States if they entered the country illegally, committed a crime, broke immigration laws, or is involved in criminal acts that threaten public safety, according to official data. The process generally begins with a local or federal arrest by the police before being transferred to Immigration and Customs Enforcement, asserts New Frontier Immigration Law, a law firm on its website. The powerful American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) reminds that, in general, the migrant should show immigration documents, if they have them, and in the absence of them, remain silent or consult a lawyer. If detained, say they want to remain silent and request a lawyer immediately. Do not provide any explanation, it says. If arrested by the police, they have the right to make a local call, and if arrested by ICE, they have the right to communicate with their consulate, explains ACLU. The detained migrant may remain in a detention center until the trial in an immigration court or until they are deported, according to US legislation. Those who have not passed through a border control upon entering the country may be deported quickly, known as expedited removal, without going through an immigration court. Others go through a court, which prolongs the process. The judge examines the case. Sometimes the foreigner may request asylum, a status adjustment, or seek the cancellation of removal. Occasionally, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) may release a foreigner upon payment of a bond, while the immigration process continues. If deportation is ordered, the migrant has the possibility of leaving the country on their own (voluntary departure). However, the eligibility criteria are very strict for voluntary departures, according to New Frontier Immigration Law. Some deportation orders can be appealed. They can appeal to the Immigration Board, although in some cases, they can also appeal to the Supreme Court. However, while all this happens, which can take months, the accused will be incarcerated, even those who have the option of bail, notes the immigration law firm on its portal. In many cases, if the accused are from Mexico, they are transported to the nearest border, notes New Frontier Immigration Law. According to government information, most people are deported by plane and the United States bears the costs. Those who committed non-violent crimes can apply for a program called Rapid REPAT, which allows them to leave prison and return to their countries. It is unknown if Cuba, Venezuela, and Nicaragua are willing to receive their migrants and how many other countries in Latin America will receive them and under what conditions.

As part of their new decisions, the new president of the United States, Donald Trump, announced the tightening of immigration measures for undocumented immigrants (including thousands of Peruvians), even for legal residents, since they can also be expelled despite having a Green Card, or permanent residence card, which grants immigrants in the US the right to live and work legally in that country. On this matter, immigration attorney Elizabeth Uribe, of the Uribe Uribe APLC firm, explained in an interview with CNN that the Green Card should not be considered an absolute right, but a privilege that needs to be protected. In this, Lee Gelernt, director of the Immigrant Rights Project of the ACLU, agrees, warning that it would be an error to suppose that they will be saved if they are here legally. According to the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA), specifically in its section 237, there are various circumstances under which a lawful resident can be deported, even if they hold a Green Card. Among the reasons for which permanent residents may be deported are Facilitating the illegal entry of another person into the United States. Marriage fraud, marrying exclusively for immigration benefits. Aggravated crimes, including drug trafficking, use or sale of firearms, and child pornography. Domestic violence or violation of protection orders. Terrorist activities, sabotage, treason, or sedition. Crimes against minors and human trafficking. Terrorist activities, sabotage, conspiracy, or treason and sedition. According to data from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), between 2014 and 2023, more than 10 million permanent residence cards were issued. The Peruvian Foreign Minister, Elmer Schialer, confirmed that 74 Peruvians are being held at an immigration detention center in San Diego, in the United States. In the United States, it is understood that there are 74 Peruvians being held at this detention center. They will be deported after completing a process, he stated to the press, although no exact date was specified. (Illustrative Image Infobae) A case of international child exploitation came to light after formal charges were brought against four men linked to an online network that promoted neo-Nazism, nihilism, and pedophilia as fundamental principles. According to a report from the U.S. Department of Justice, the accused allegedly used digital platforms to manipulate and coerce minors, forcing them to produce child sexual abuse material and to perform self-harm acts. The crimes allegedly occurred between 2019 and 2022. Among the accused are Colin John Thomas Walker, 23 years old, and resident of Bridgeton, New Jersey Clint Jordan Lopaka Nahooikaika Borge, 41 years old, originally from Hawaii Rohan Sandeep Rane, a 28-year-old French citizen Kaleb Christopher Merritt, 24 years old, from Texas According to the indictment, the four men were members of a group known as CVLT, which operated online and aimed to recruit sadistic followers and manipulate vulnerable minors. As detailed by New York Post, the accused face charges of participating in a child exploitation enterprise, a crime that could carry sentences of 20 years to life in prison. A pattern of systematic abuse and psychological coercion The CVLT group focused on identifying and exploiting minors who faced mental health issues or had been previous victims of sexual abuse. Members of the network used tactics of psychological manipulation to subjugate their victims, forcing them to perform degrading acts such as cutting their hair and eating it, drinking their own urine, self-harming with knives, and recording the names of group members on their skin. In addition, minors were forced to insult themselves with racist terms and to perform explicit sex acts, some of which involved pets, other children, or even hazardous objects such as knives and cacti. The indictment also alleged that the defendants sent their victims videos of extremely violent content, including animal torture and rape, as part of their intimidation strategy. In some cases, CVLT members pressured minors to kill themselves in live broadcasts. When the victims attempted to resist or threatened to report the abuse, the accused extorted them by distributing compromising images that they had already obtained. The Department of Justice identified at least 16 minor victims of the network. (Lamarque, REUTERS) Leadership and Structure of the Criminal Network According to Fox 8, the three men led the group's activities and coordinated efforts to recruit other members and expand their reach. Although it is unclear how the accused men knew each other, authorities have noted that their collaboration enabled the creation of an organized network with an explicit purpose of abuse and exploitation. The Department of Justice detailed that Rane is currently incarcerated in France, where he was arrested in 2022 on unrelated charges of child exploitation. Meanwhile, Merritt is serving a 350-year sentence in a Virginia prison after being found guilty in 2021 of traveling from Texas to sexually abuse a 12-year-old girl he had met online. Both Walker and Borge were arrested last Thursday in their respective states. Global Impact and Identified VictimsAuthorities have identified at least 16 minors from various parts of the world as victims of CVLT, including two residents of Southern California. According to Fox 8, the accused selected their victims based on their emotional vulnerability and history of abuse, making it easier to manipulate them. The minors were forced to produce explicit material, which was then shared among group members, perpetuating a cycle of abuse. The Department of Justice emphasized that, in some cases, the accused carried out their threats to disseminate compromising images when the victims refused to continue participating in group activities. This pattern of coercion and reprisals exacerbated the psychological harm suffered by the minors, who were already in extremely vulnerable situations.

Recent statements by Donald Trump on the mass deportation of immigrants have sparked uncertainty and fear among the migrant community in the United States. The possibility of millions of people being expelled from the country has sounded the alarm, especially among those residing in U.S. territory without a defined legal status. However, not all immigrants are in the same situation. There are certain protected groups under specific laws and programs that could avoid deportation, despite Trump's new measures. For these sectors, current regulations could serve as a shield against the threat of expulsion. According to Valeria Mendoza Talledo for Peru. Which Peruvian immigrants could avoid deportation Despite the hardening of migration policies, certain groups have legal protections that allow them to remain in the United States Although the situation remains uncertain, these exceptions could be crucial for many Peruvians at risk. 1. Permanent Residents (Green Card holders) Immigrants with permanent residence in the US have acquired rights that protect them from deportation. However, they could be expelled if they commit serious crimes or violate certain immigration regulations. According to the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA), residents can be deported for crimes such as fraud, drug trafficking, domestic violence, or terrorist activities. Therefore, maintaining a clean record is essential to avoid legal problems.2. Naturalized Citizens People who have completed the naturalization process and obtained US citizenship cannot be deported, except in exceptional cases. Migratory fraud or document forgery could lead to citizenship revocation, although these cases are rare.3 Beneficiaries of the DACA ProgramThe Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) program protects young immigrant arrivals who entered the country as children. Those who meet the requirements can renew their work permits and avoid deportation. DACA does not guarantee permanent status, but it does offer some stability to thousands of young immigrants, explained sources from the Department of Homeland Security. However, Trump has threatened to eliminate this program, which has generated concern in the migrant community.4. Asylum SeekersPeople who have sought asylum in the United States while fleeing persecution in their countries of origin have temporary protection. While their cases are being processed, they cannot be deported. Nevertheless, the waiting times for resolving asylum cases can extend for years, generating uncertainty for thousands of Peruvians who find themselves in this situation. Victims of violence or human trafficking Immigrants who have been victims of domestic violence or human trafficking can obtain special visas, such as the U visa or the T visa, which allow them to stay in the US and, eventually, request residency. Victims of serious crimes can receive migratory protection if they cooperate with authorities in the investigation of these cases, explained immigration lawyers. TPS an option for thousands of immigrants The Temporary Protected Status (TPS) has been a fundamental resource for immigrants from countries affected by natural disasters, armed conflicts, or humanitarian crises. Those who qualify for this benefit can live and work legally in the US without fear of deportation. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) recently extended TPS for 800,000 immigrants, providing stability to thousands of people. However, this status does not automatically lead to permanent residence, meaning that beneficiaries must be aware of any changes in government policies. Permanent residents can be deported Although permanent legal residents enjoy certain rights, they are not exempt from deportation if they violate immigration laws. According to Section 237 of the Immigration and Nationality Act, there are multiple reasons for which a resident can be expelled from the country, including Facilitating the illegal entry of other people into the US. Marriage fraud for immigration purposes. Committing serious crimes, such as drug trafficking, domestic violence, crimes against minors, or human trafficking. Involvement in terrorist activities or conspiracy. Due to the measures proposed by Trump, it is expected that there will be an increase in background checks for immigrants with Green Cards, which makes it crucial for permanent residents to avoid any activity that could put their status at risk. 74 Peruvians detained in San Diego will be deported. The Foreign Minister Elmer Schialer confirmed that 74 Peruvian citizens are currently detained in a migration center in San Diego, California, awaiting deportation. These Peruvians will be expelled once their migratory process is finalized, although there is no exact date for their departure, stated the official. The case of these compatriots reflects the severity with which the US government is applying immigration laws. In light of this situation, Peruvian consulates have activated hotline services to provide legal advice to migrants at risk of deportation. The Peruvian consulates provide support to immigrants Amidst this migration crisis, the Peruvian government has reiterated its commitment to assisting its citizens in the US. Consulates in various cities have enabled legal guidance and advisory services for those at risk of deportation. Consular services include: Legal assistance to review immigration options. Document management for those who need to regularize their status. Intervention in deportation cases to ensure a fair process. The Peruvian government has advised its citizens in the US to inform themselves about their rights and avoid scams by fake immigration advisors who promise quick solutions. What can Peruvians at risk of deportation do In light of the hardening of immigration policies, experts recommend: Consulting with an immigration lawyer to evaluate legal options. Not signing documents without legal advice, especially in detention centers. Stay informed about updates on immigration policies. Avoid migrant scams and do not trust people who promise magical solutions. Trump's announced measures have generated a climate of tension, but there are still legal channels to protect yourself from deportation. Being informed and seeking professional advice can make a difference in the future of many Peruvians in the US.

In collaboration with the Te Protejo MÃ©xico platform, the entity has access to a free virtual hotline to report safely and anonymously material related to sexual abuse and exploitation, cyberstalking, cyberbullying, and grooming. Access to a full and peaceful life, free from fears, is the only way we can make our goal of ensuring the rights of all people a reality, with a focus on our girls, boys, and adolescents. Preserving the safety, well-being, and secure environments of childhood and youth is a priority for the State. Upon receiving a report, the platform will trigger collaboration protocols with Interpol and technology companies such as Google, Facebook, X, and Microsoft, to ensure that the material ceases to circulate on the network. Experts point out that while technological development has been positive in multiple sectors, it has also brought new and endless forms of exploitation and abuse. However, only 10% is reported and a mere 1% receives a condemnatory sentence. Mexico ranks first globally in child abuse. In the country, 23,000 adolescents between 12 and 17 years old suffered some form of sexual aggression, he added. On this matter, Eduardo Cruz, from FundaciÃ³n Pas, highlighted that Mexico is the 46th member of INHOPE, the world's leading network in the fight against online child sexual abuse. Through the "Te Protejo" application, we need all Mexican children and schools to have this application and know that if they made a mistake, any photo or video can be reported anonymously, he referred to. Te Protejo Mexico is a virtual line that is part of the INHOPE International Association of Internet Hotlines, which works in constant cooperation and information exchange with Interpol and the major technology companies. With the Te Protejo Mexico platform, you can report any material of child abuse or exploitation anonymously, if the child is under 18 years old. Your voice matters, join us to protect girls, boys, and teenagers in the digital world, shared the area on social media. In coordination with different countries, we eliminate child sexual abuse material in the shortest time possible to end revictimization. These elements help authorities in each country to prosecute perpetrators and rescue victims of this crime. It is worth noting that in its first year of operation in various entities of the country, Te Protejo MÃ©xico identified that 52 percent of sexual content on inappropriate sites was self-generated by girls, boys, and teenagers, either through grooming or sexting. Grooming consists of sexual harassment of minors through digital means, consisting of actions deployed generally by adult individuals. And sexting, self-produced material that involves sexual content that can be shared with countless people without the victim's authorization later on. The most vulnerable are, according to statistics, girls and boys between 4 and 13 years old. The United States, the Netherlands, Russia, Latvia, and Belize are the countries with the largest number of reported child sexual abuse material in Mexico. There are over 46 million images or videos of child sexual abuse online and nearly 750,000 perpetrators searching for contact with a child, adolescent, or teenager through the internet, with sexual purposes. To prevent such situations, it is recommended that mothers, fathers, and caregivers know and talk about the risks on the internet, stay involved in their digital world, know who they are connecting with, use security and privacy controls, and in addition, set age limits for access to platforms and social media, block and report if violence has already occurred, and eradicate revictimization. On the other hand, educational agents should work on training and sensitizing mothers, fathers, and caregivers to recognize the different forms of violence in the digital environment, promote digital civility with values of respect, empathy, and digital responsibility, avoiding cyberbullying and the dissemination of sexual content, and promote digital literacy and updating on topics facing the future.

text: Puerto Galera, Philippines. In front of a webcam, a naked girl performs sexual acts following instructions from a man thousands of miles away. The scene occurs in the intimacy of her home and under the coercion of her own mother in the Philippines, one of the world's centers for child pornography on the internet, according to denouncements from politicians, police agencies, and activists. This is one of the many graphic proofs used to condemn Bouhalem Bouchiba in France to 25 years in prison for having requested hundreds of sexual videos over nearly a decade. The authorities in the Philippines, the world's epicenter of online child sex, labeled the case last December as a significant legal victory against the exploitation of minors. But a question still haunts activists, politicians, and authorities in the Philippines: how can the exploitation be addressed when the perpetrators who force minors to perform sexual acts in front of a camera are often their own family members? Breaking the silence.  Most of this happens within the family, and silence must be broken, said EFE's Reynaldo Arevalo, a guardian of street children from Manila, at the headquarters of the Stairway Foundation in Puerto Galera, a city on the island of Mindoro, which is known for being one of the best places in the Philippines for scuba diving, but whose hidden child prostitution in the 1990s prompted Danish Lars C. Jorgensen to co-found Stairway. Sevilla, February 1 (EUROPA PRESS) The Supreme Court (TS) has dismissed an appeal for cassation of a male defendant, against a judgment of the High Court of Justice of Andalusia (TSJA) that confirms the 27-year-and-a-half prison sentence imposed by the Court of Seville, for sexual crimes against four minors and for possession of child pornography. In a judgment issued on January 16 and recorded by Europa Press, the Supreme Court addresses this appeal for cassation, against the resolution of the TSJA that confirms the initial condemnatory judgment of the Third Section of the Court of Seville, which declared proven that in March 2021, the defendant, S.I.B., initiated actions aimed at gaining the trust of five minors aged 16, whom he knew by finding them in a bakery in a block where they all resided. The accused, according to the Audiencia, gained the trust of all of them and by offering them gifts, managed to have the minors come and agree to go to his home, where he created a friendly and trusting atmosphere, through invitations to refreshments, as well as food, and where afterwards, he practiced touching on their genitals, masturbated, and performed oral sex on four of these minors, in addition to one of them, on one occasion, consenting to be anally penetrated by the accused, who then followed by the minor anally penetrating the accused. Additionally, the Third Section of the Audiencia considered it proven that the accused achieved his purpose through the offer of small amounts of money, between 20 and 70 euros, as well as other gifts, and that in order not to tell what they did with him, he told them that they would get into a very big problem, which generated a clear fear in those involved. Similarly, the sentence states that in a police record of the accused's residence, computer supports were found to contain numerous videos and images depicting minors in sexual and pornographic activities and behaviors that the accused possessed for his own use. MORE THAN 27 YEARS IN PRISON Given the case, the court imposed 18 years in prison for three sex crimes against minors under 16, nine years more in prison for a similar crime but continued, and an additional six months of deprivation of liberty for an additional crime of child pornography, totaling 27 and a half years in prison. He imposed on him, in addition, a penalty of prohibition of approach and communication with each of the minor victims for a period of four years, as well as the measure of supervised liberty for another four years, and in concept of civil liability, the obligation was established to charge the accused to indemnify each of the minors with 5,000 euros. Although the defendant appealed this sentence before the TSJA, the High Andalusian Court dismissed his appeal and confirmed the initial sentence of the Third Section of the Court, for which S.I.B. decided to appeal in cassation before the Supreme Court. Addressing this cassation appeal, the Supreme Court explains that the appeal is aimed at questioning the credibility and probative value of the statements of minor victims, considering that they all lie in their statements. However, the appellate court found that the probative evaluation of the statements of minors made by the Audiencia was solid, rational, and sufficient, ultimately supporting the conviction.THE CASSATION APPEAL According to the Supreme Court, the appellant fails to challenge with the slightest foundation the subjective credibility of the minors. It appears to attribute the responsibility to minor Vicente, who is presented as the instigator and precursor of what happened, and what the rest of the minors later declare, but as the Superior Court points out, no basis is observed or alleged to suspect that the minors constructed their testimonies prompted or induced by third parties due to motives of ill will, interest in illegally harming the accused or another spurious motive. On the contrary, it is unimaginable that everyone conspired to invent a story about touching, masturbation, and oral sex on their persons for no reason, but rather the absence of reasons to doubt their credibility and the plurality of coinciding testimonies in the same direction lead to reputing the content of the testimonies as truthful and convincing. The Supreme Court, citing the High Court of Justice, emphasizes that even if one of the minors in some way collaborated with the accused to contact the others, this in no way exempts him from his responsibility. Additionally, the Supreme Court notes that it is especially significant that the defendant admits to meeting alone and on several occasions with minors in his home with a purpose and circumstances that he has not fully clarified, as well as having in his possession videos or images of minors of a sexual and pornographic nature, thereby dismissing his appeal.

The accused, according to the Audiencia, gained the trust of all of them and by offering them gifts, managed to have the minors come and agree to go to his home, where he created a friendly and trusting atmosphere, through invitations to refreshments, as well as food, and where afterwards, he practiced touching on their genitals, masturbated, and performed oral sex on four of these minors, in addition to one of them, on one occasion, consenting to be anally penetrated by the accused, who then followed by the minor anally penetrating the accused. Additionally, the Third Section of the Audiencia considered it proven that the accused achieved his purpose through the offer of small amounts of money, between 20 and 70 euros, as well as other gifts, and that in order not to tell what they did with him, he told them that they would get into a very big problem, which generated a clear fear in those involved. Similarly, the sentence states that in a police record of the accused's residence, computer supports were found to contain numerous videos and images depicting minors in sexual and pornographic activities and behaviors that the accused possessed for his own use. MORE THAN 27 YEARS IN PRISON Given the case, the court imposed 18 years in prison for three sex crimes against minors under 16, nine years more in prison for a similar crime but continued, and an additional six months of deprivation of liberty for an additional crime of child pornography, totaling 27 and a half years in prison. He imposed on him, in addition, a penalty of prohibition of approach and communication with each of the minor victims for a period of four years, as well as the measure of supervised liberty for another four years, and in concept of civil liability, the obligation was established to charge the accused to indemnify each of the minors with 5,000 euros. Although the defendant appealed this sentence before the TSJA, the High Andalusian Court dismissed his appeal and confirmed the initial sentence of the Third Section of the Court, for which S.I.B. decided to appeal in cassation before the Supreme Court. Addressing this cassation appeal, the Supreme Court explains that the appeal is aimed at questioning the credibility and probative value of the statements of minor victims, considering that they all lie in their statements. However, the appellate court found that the probative evaluation of the statements of minors made by the Audiencia was solid, rational, and sufficient, ultimately supporting the conviction.THE CASSATION APPEAL According to the Supreme Court, the appellant fails to challenge with the slightest foundation the subjective credibility of the minors. It appears to attribute the responsibility to minor Vicente, who is presented as the instigator and precursor of what happened, and what the rest of the minors later declare, but as the Superior Court points out, no basis is observed or alleged to suspect that the minors constructed their testimonies prompted or induced by third parties due to motives of ill will, interest in illegally harming the accused or another spurious motive. On the contrary, it is unimaginable that everyone conspired to invent a story about touching, masturbation, and oral sex on their persons for no reason, but rather the absence of reasons to doubt their credibility and the plurality of coinciding testimonies in the same direction lead to reputing the content of the testimonies as truthful and convincing. The Supreme Court, citing the High Court of Justice, emphasizes that even if one of the minors in some way collaborated with the accused to contact the others, this in no way exempts him from his responsibility. Additionally, the Supreme Court notes that it is especially significant that the defendant admits to meeting alone and on several occasions with minors in his home with a purpose and circumstances that he has not fully clarified, as well as having in his possession videos or images of minors of a sexual and pornographic nature, thereby dismissing his appeal.

A complex international investigation coordinated by Europol has dismantled a sophisticated Chinese crime network involved in illegal immigration and human trafficking for sexual exploitation. On December 17, law enforcement agencies carried out raids on 14 properties in Barcelona (4), Madrid (9), and Toledo (1) in Spain, and one property in Zagreb, Croatia. These operations resulted in 30 arrests, including the leaders of the crime network. In addition, â‚¬180,000 in cash, weapons, 70 passports, equipment for forging passports and visas, narcotics, 10 luxury vehicles, and 33 mobile phones were seized. A total of 33 victims, Chinese and Vietnamese nationals, were also protected. This investigation is based on the dismantling of the largest Chinese prostitution ring in Europe in February 2023. The digital evidence seized during that operation has been thoroughly analyzed since then, including a forensic sprint held at Europol's headquarters in March 2023. During this sprint, experts from nine countries extracted dozens of terabytes of data from hundreds of mobile phones confiscated. The new intelligence provided unprecedented information on the methods used by Chinese criminal networks in Europe, revealing a sophisticated division of labor and a reliance on actors in the organized crime as a service. Two cells, a human trafficking chain, the criminal organization, composed mainly of Chinese citizens, obtained significant profits from the sexual exploitation of vulnerable women. To maximize profits, the group became involved in additional criminal activities, including document forgery, money laundering, and facilitation of illegal immigration. The victims were lured into prostitution in Europe under the promise of earning high incomes in a short period of time. However, upon arrival, they were subjected to severe debt bondage and trapped in a cycle of exploitation from which they could not escape due to their vulnerabilities and dependence on the traffickers. The organization operated in two interconnected cells: the recruitment cell and the smuggling cell. The victims were recruited in China through travel agencies where they were disguised from exploitation by presenting opportunities for prostitution as legitimate employment abroad. Using the Western Balkan corridor, the smuggling cell coordinated with local facilitators and drivers to illegally transport the victims to the EU. Safe houses were maintained along the route, with logistics managed through instant messaging applications. Human Trafficking Cell Once in Europe, the victims were initially exploited in entry countries. Subsequently, they were transferred to Spain and other member states, where they were forced to work in brothels or short-stay facilities. The victims were rotated between cities and crossed borders to evade detection and meet the growing demand for sex services. The organization maintained strict control over all aspects of the victims' lives, taking 50% of their earnings even after their debts were paid. A highly organized and resilient network The smuggling operations were meticulously coordinated through instant messaging apps, with facilitators managing safe houses along the route and providing instructions on the transportation of the victims. Upon their arrival, the victims were initially exploited in countries of entry before being transferred to Spain and other EU member states, where their exploitation continued under the strict control of the criminal group. The victims trafficked by the group were identified in exploitation networks in multiple EU countries, highlighting the scale and resilience of this criminal network. International cooperation led to success. The operation was led by the National Police of Spain in close collaboration with the National Police of Croatia and Europol. The Agency supported national authorities by facilitating the exchange of critical intelligence and providing expert analytical support. On the day of the action, Europol deployed two experts to Madrid and Barcelona, where they worked alongside investigators, verifying operational data in real-time, assisting in field operations, and conducting forensic extractions from the mobile phones used by the suspects. This investigation is part of a wide-ranging Europol operational group dedicated to combating Chinese human trafficking networks. Involving 11 countries, the operational group focuses on dismantling these criminal groups operating throughout Europe.

Washington, D.C. Just 10 days into Donald Trump's second term in the United States, more than 5,500 migrants have been detained in raids carried out by the new government. According to international media, the detentions, conducted by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents, have taken place in over a dozen cities, including so-called sanctuaries like New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago. The ICE has been releasing the daily number of migrant detentions nationwide, even highlighting the profiles of some individuals, this week indicating that the goal is to detain between 1,200 and 1,500 migrants daily. In total, ICE reports the arrest of 5,537 people in operations in over a dozen cities. Through their account on X, the agency has highlighted the profile of 21 detainees, some of whom have a name, surname, and photo, while others only have their nationality and the charges they face, which range from being under the influence of substances to sexual abuse of minors. Except for a profile of a person from Afghanistan, all the cases highlighted by ICE are of people of Latin American origin. Many of the arrests have been shared on social media, especially those participated in by border czar Tom Homan and Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem. Migrant detention should be the last resort UN The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights reminded US President Donald Trump this Friday that the detention of migrants, even if they are in an irregular situation, should be considered the last resort and a completely exceptional measure. The raids for the detention of undocumented migrants in the United States began on January 23, 2025. Photo Sec_Noem Migrants have human rights, and these must be respected wherever they are. The detention of immigrants can only be used as a last resort and in exceptional circumstances, stated Jeremy Laurence, spokesperson for the agency, to the press. Questioned about Trump's order to use the detention center at the US naval base in Guantanamo for migrants before their deportation, Laurence emphasized that dignity and the rights of all must be protected, regardless of their migratory status. It is also the responsibility of the states where migrants are found to ensure they are treated in accordance with international norms of human rights, he added.

text: The prosecutors in New York have expanded their case against rapper Sean Diddy Combs, accusing him of coercing two additional women into commercial sex acts and dangling a person over a high-rise balcony. Combs has been in jail since September after an initial indictment charged him with extortion, forced sex trafficking, and transporting someone for prostitution. On Thursday, the indictment was updated to add two more victims, although no new charges were added to the case. The 55-year-old musician has vigorously denied all charges against him, including the federal criminal case and more than 30 separate civil lawsuits. In response to the amended indictment, his lawyer, Marc Agnifilo, stated that the prosecution's case remains flawed. The government has added the ridiculous theory that two of Mr. Combs's former girlfriends were not girlfriends at all, but rather prostitutes. The updated indictment includes allegations that Combs used his position and influence to coerce women into commercial sex acts, with some victims allegedly being lured into his orbit with promises of fame, wealth, and other benefits. Lionel Combs is as committed as ever to fighting these charges and winning in court. The original indictment identified only one victim, referred to in court documents as Victim 1, whose allegations closely aligned with those of Cassandra Ventura, the singer who sued the Peines for rape and sex trafficking in 2023. In the new indictment, prosecutors claim that the Peines used force, threats of force, and coercion to cause the victims, including, among others, three female victims, to participate in commercial sex acts. That alleged violence was vividly illustrated in a video of the musician kicking, dragging, and throwing a vase at Mrs. Ventura in a Los Angeles hotel in 2016. In the new indictment, prosecutors assert that the Peines, with the help of several close associates, paid the hotel's security staff $100,000 (Â£80,000) for the footage. However, the footage leaked last year Later, Combs said he was disturbed by the images and had sought professional help after the incident. Mrs. Ventura said the violence I experienced broke me with someone I never thought I would have become. A footnote in the document notes that their investigation is ongoing and that additional updates will be presented as soon as possible before the trial. Among the new developments, prosecutors have moved the supposed start date of Combs's sex trafficking crimes to 2004, four years before what was previously said. They have also expanded the list of narcotics Combs is alleged to have used to keep his victims obedient and silent, adding methamphetamine and psychedelic mushrooms to the previously cited cocaine, oxycodone, and ketamine. The accusation that the lashes were hung from a woman's balcony reflects a claim made in a civil lawsuit filed by fashion designer Bryana Bana Bongolan last December. Prosecutors also added an allegation that Combs had not only abused women but also his employees, witnesses to his abuse, and others. text: Most modern slavery cases occur in rural areas, but are increasingly common in urban contexts. Numerous businessmen and politicians were identified in a report by the Ministry of Labor published this week on the labor conditions akin to slavery in South America's largest country. In the last three decades, more than 65,500 people have been rescued from this situation. Only in 2024, 1,035 inspections were carried out, resulting in 2,004 people rescued, once again exposing the local weakness in human rights. According to the Ministry of Labor, around 8,400 control operations since 1995 have led to these liberations. It was only then that Brazil officially recognized the existence of contemporary forms of slavery. Since 2003, around $26.4 million has been spent compensating the victims. Before 2003, there was no precise record, as that year the Worker Rescue Unemployment Insurance (SDTR) was implemented, which consists of three payments equivalent to the minimum wage, it was explained. According to the Brazilian Penal Code, forced labor is analogous to slavery, with grueling shifts, degrading conditions, or where restrictions on mobility are applied due to debts contracted with the employer. In 2023, more than 3,100 people were rescued from their subjugation, detected mainly in construction, coffee cultivation, agriculture, and horticulture. Although forced labor is primarily found in rural areas, it is also widespread in major cities, where it is mainly detected in the textile sector, which employs a larger number of women. Brazilian authorities created the so-called "dirty list" of slave labor in 2004, which includes individuals and companies that imposed those conditions on others, as a warning to potential victims. The United Nations (UN) considered that initiative a key tool in the fight against modern slavery. Being included in the dirty list is not a judicial sanction, but a transparency tool so that society knows which companies and individuals have been identified as people exploiters in degrading conditions, it was explained.

The trickle of weekly cases of sexual assaults continues in the Cantabrian courts. The First and Third Sections of the Provincial Court of Cantabria will be the scene next week of three trials for different sexual crimes, including child corruption, sexual assault, and sexual abuse with penetration. The first will be on Tuesday in the First Section of the Provincial Court of Cantabria, for child corruption. According to the prosecutor's qualification document, the events occurred on a street in Reinosa, where the accused, knowing that the victim was under sixteen years old, approached an eleven-year-old girl and offered her 20 euros to be with him for a while, with the intention of obtaining a sexual encounter. The prosecutor will request a three-year prison sentence, a four-year ban on communicating or approaching the minor, six years of disqualification from working with minors, and one year of supervised freedom after release from prison. Additionally, a compensation of 1,000 euros will be requested for the minor for the moral damages caused. The other two trials confirm the most common trend, that the attacks come from the closest environments. So, on Wednesday, the First Section will have a trial for sexual aggression in a residence, in which a man faces charges for sexual aggression in a residence where both, the accused and the victim, were admitted. According to the prosecution, the accused, after smoking a cigarette with two companions in the bathroom, assaulted one of them when the other left the place. The written classification details that the man, driven by an evident intention of sexual satisfaction, grabbed the victim by the chin to kiss her, to which she refused. Subsequently, he made intimate touching. The woman managed to break free, but the accused grabbed her by the neck when trying to flee. The victim's screams alerted other residents, who came to her aid. The defendant, who suffers from multiple drug dependence syndrome and cognitive disorders, faces a petition for five years in prison, five years of prohibition from working with minors, and five years of supervised release. The prosecution will also request a compensation of 3,000 euros for the victim for the moral damages suffered. On Thursday, the Third Section will judge a man for sexual abuse with penetration while a woman slept in his home. According to the prosecution, the accused took advantage of the victim sleeping in a room adjacent to his, after spending the night with his roommate, to enter her bed naked and penetrate her vagina with his penis. She initially thought it was her partner, but upon realizing, she defended herself and managed to get him to leave the home. The prosecutor will classify the facts as a sex crime with penetration and will request five years of imprisonment, eight years of separation and prohibition of communicating with the victim, five years of supervised freedom, and fifteen years of disqualification to work with minors. Additionally, they will ask for a compensation of 5,000 euros for moral damages. On the other hand, the private accusation, exercised by the victim, will raise the demands to eight years of imprisonment, ten years of separation, fifteen years of disqualification, and a compensation of 10,000 euros.

Judicial documents revealed that Inman, who also worked for the Visit Orlando organization, allegedly received and stored several explicit videos showing adults sexually abusing minors.
