In a shocking incident in San Vicente, a 16-year-old boy was transferred to Coronda prison after being accused of repeated qualified sexual abuse and corruption of minors. The decision was made on Tuesday during a crucial hearing at the Juvenile Court in Rafaela, where Judge Laura Lencioni, along with the Juvenile Defender, the Prosecution, and the Juvenile Advisor, decided on the young defendant's judicial future. The minor will remain incarcerated in Coronda prison until reaching the age of majority, that is, until he turns 18. During this period, the Judiciary will determine his responsibility for the alleged crimes. If found guilty, it will be evaluated whether he will continue serving the sentence as an adult. The case, dating back to December 28, 2024, was initially classified as Simple Sexual Abuse. However, within the framework of the investigation, the First Instance Court for Minors of Second Nominations reclassified the charges, increasing the gravity of the accusation. This modification led the Justice to order a raid on the defendant's home, where a cellular phone was seized and will be subjected to expert analysis to clarify the facts. During the procedure, the minor was detained under the modality of communicated detention, respecting judicial dispositions. The operation was carried out with the objective of collecting evidence that will allow advancing in the investigation and determining the accused's culpability. The case remains under investigation, and it is expected that in the coming months, the Justice will define the judicial future of the adolescent. Meanwhile, the community of San Vicente remains attentive to the developments of a case that has generated a profound social impact and highlights the complexity of sexual crimes in the juvenile justice system.

Twenty-eight women were victims of gender violence in Argentina from January 1 to 31, 2025, which translates to one femicide every 26 hours, according to a new report from the Observatory of Femicides in Argentina, directed by Adriana Marisel Zambrano of La Casa del Encuentro. The most relevant data are that 27 daughters were left without a mother, 49% are minors, and 60% of the aggressors were partners or ex-partners. As each report demonstrates, the most insecure place for a woman in a situation of violence continues to be her home or the home shared with the aggressor, as 70% were killed in their own home. Buenos Aires remains the province with the most cases, followed by Santa Fe, Mendoza, and CABA. The Casa del Encuentro has been tracking cases of femicide since 2008 and for many years was the only Observatory providing statistics on the murders of women, girls, and diverse individuals across the country, which were used to develop public policies and laws for prevention and protection of women and diverse individuals.Five victims had filed a complaint. Two perpetrators had been issued a preventive measure. Four perpetrators were current or former members of law enforcement. One victim had a suspected history of sexual abuse. Two victims were migrants. Four perpetrators took their own lives. Two victims were in the context of narco-crime. One femicide was linked to an adult male.

Gender-based violence in Argentina continues to claim victims at a chilling rate. In January 2025, 28 women were murdered, equivalent to one femicide every 26 hours, according to the data from the Argentine Observatory of Femicides Adriana Marisel Zambrano of La Casa del Encuentro. The numbers reveal an alarming reality as the national Government advances in its agenda to eliminate the legal figure of femicide. The report, released on Monday, also exposed the social impact of these crimes: 27 children were left without a mother, and 49% of them are minors. The majority of the victims were murdered by partners or ex-partners, who represent 60% of the aggressors. Moreover, 70% of the femicides occurred in the victim's home, confirming once again that the domestic space remains the most dangerous place for a woman in a situation of violence. The survey also notes that, of the total number of victims, five had previously filed complaints against their aggressors. However, that was not enough to prevent the fatal outcome. Two femicides had active restraining orders and four were members or ex-members of security forces, reflecting the system's failure to protect women from structural violence. Other data collected by the Observatory includes that one victim showed signs of sexual abuse, two were migrants, four femicides took their own lives after committing the crime and two women were killed in the context of narcocriminality. Additionally, a femicide of an adult male was registered, that is, a man who was killed for trying to protect a woman from her aggressor. As for the geographical distribution of cases, the province of Buenos Aires leads the numbers of femicides, followed by Santa Fe, Mendoza and the City of Buenos Aires. An official agenda that ignores the numbers While the data reveal a crisis of gender violence, the government of Javier Milei is advancing in its intention to eliminate the legal figure of femicide from the Penal Code. From the Executive, they assure that the current concept violates the equality before the law and promote its derogation under the premise that no life is worth more than another. The Minister of Justice, Mario Cuneo Libarona, reaffirmed this stance and assured that his management will advance in the elimination of the category of femicide. However, the measure could benefit convicted murderers under that legal figure, which generated strong criticisms from feminist organizations and opposition political sectors. Despite the warnings from experts in penal law and the questioning from different sectors, the officialdom maintains its stance and dismisses social protests. According to reports, at the Casa Rosada, they consider that the feminist protests will have no impact on the government's final decision.

By Tom Lawrence Published 2022, February 3, 2025 Updated 2038, February 3, 2025 Keir Starmer and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni have agreed on a deal to allow police forces from both countries to launch a crackdown on migrant boats in a mafia-style operation. A working group of government officials will use methods the Italian police use to take down mafia leaders, reported the Mirror. The UK and Italy will share intelligence on money linked to criminal gangs involved in people smuggling. Both countries will also work together to seize the money and assets of the gangs. Last month, Giorgia Meloni said she was in sync with the British Prime Minister on many issues, particularly addressing illegal immigration. Starmer met Meloni in September to discuss the issue, Downing Street said the Prime Minister wanted to learn from Italy, which has reduced numbers crossing the Mediterranean from 118,000 to 44,500 in the last year, a 62 percent drop. Mrs Meloni had previously proposed a major overhaul of Europol or for the organisation to receive a special mission to combat people smugglers. The previous Italian Prime Minister had a close working relationship with former PM Rishi Sunak in efforts to take strong action against illegal migration. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer shake hands at a press conference in September Meloni and Starmer are working together to launch a mafia-style crackdown on migrant boats Mrs Meloni has now secured the support of Sir Keir since she replaced her Tory predecessor in Downing Street last year The Telegraph reported that Sir Keir expressed his backing for Meloni's plan for a review of Europol during their meeting at the European Political Community Summit. He then also proposed the idea of British police officers and their Europol counterparts carrying out joint operations. Before taking power, Sir Keir and Yvette Cooper, now Secretary of State for the Home Department, visited Europol's headquarters in The Hague for talks. The Labour couple used the visit in September last year to describe their plans for closer cooperation with the EU to tackle the disaster of small boats coming to Britain. Sir Keir has focused his efforts on combating illegal migration using counter-terrorism tactics to crush gangs bringing people across the Channel. He also wants to deepen intelligence ties with Brussels as part of a proposed post-Brexit security pact. Last month, the government published its border security, asylum, and immigration bill. It was claimed that Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is joining Sir Keir Starmer to address illegal immigration. Critics accused them of turning the UK into Europe's soft touch after reversing border laws designed to make it nearly impossible for illegal migrants to become UK citizens. According to the proposed law, migrants who avoid rescues in the channel until they reach UK waters face up to five years in prison. And those who sell and handle suspected boat parts used in migrant crossings face up to 14 years in prison under the legislation. However, the power to detain children and the prohibition on migrants who claim that modern slavery protections will remain in place despite Labour's opposition before the elections. The bill will largely repeal the Conservative's Illegal Migration Act, which only passed through Parliament in 2023. In anticipation of the trial against Puff Daddy Sean Combs, a new lawsuit was filed against him, allegedly for drugging a music hopeful. In September 2024, 55-year-old Puff Daddy Sean Combs was arrested in New York, USA, following an investigation into serious sex crimes. Over the past months, a series of accusations and lawsuits have surfaced against Puff Daddy Sean Combs for rape and sexual assault. To these allegations, a music hopeful added his account of how Puff Daddy Sean Combs allegedly drugged him at a party and sexually assaulted him while he was unconscious. This complaint joins the 300 other accusations that have come to light against Puff Daddy Sean Combs, according to attorney Tony Buzbee. Currently, Puff Daddy Sean Combs is being held at Brooklyn prison while awaiting trial in May for charges of sex trafficking and extortion. However, Variety reported on a new lawsuit against Puff Daddy Sean Combs. According to the publication, it comes from an aspiring musician who accuses Puff Daddy Sean Combs of drugging and sexually assaulting him. Attorney Tony Buzbee, who represents the victims of Puff Daddy Sean Combs, allegedly filed this lawsuit in New York on behalf of a John Doe. The plaintiff, a John Doe who would be an aspiring singer and rapper, claimed that in 2015, he was scheduled to perform as an opening act for a popular musical artist at a series of nightclubs in Los Angeles. The plaintiff, who was 23 years old at the time, was notified before his performance at the 20URL of QC that Puff Daddy Sean Combs would be in attendance. If his performance pleased Puff Daddy Sean Combs, John Doe could have received a contract with Bad Boy Records. Later that night, John Doe attended a party in the back of the club, where allegedly other known artists were consuming drugs. In the lawsuit, it is reported that an associate of Puff Daddy Sean Combs approached John Doe and handed him a drink that allegedly had been sent by the producer. Shortly thereafter, John Doe realized that he had been drugged, as he was entering and exiting consciousness. It was at that moment that he witnessed Puff Daddy Sean Combs and his team engaging in group sex with other attendees who appeared to be drugged, unconscious, or as if they were paid escorts. In the lawsuit, John Doe claims that when he regained consciousness, Puff Daddy Sean Combs was touching him and thought that he had performed oral sex on him. After regaining consciousness, he attempted to struggle against Puff Daddy Sean Combs, but they told him that if he did not comply, he would ruin his chances of succeeding in music. Puff Daddy Sean Combs allegedly ordered John Doe to have sex with a woman. John Doe supposedly escaped the location after feigning a need to use the bathroom, as he took advantage of the moment to flee to the parking lot and leave. This is how Puff Daddy Sean Combs' lawyers responded to the new lawsuit against them. After the new lawsuit, Variety reportedly contacted Puff Daddy Sean Combs' lawyers for their opinion. However, the lawyers limited themselves to stating that Puff Daddy Sean Combs cannot respond to every new publicity stunt. Dismissing the accusation, Puff Daddy Sean Combs' lawyers pointed out that they were apparently ridiculous or demonstrably false claims. Furthermore, they expressed confidence in the integrity of the judicial process and stated that the truth would prevail in court. The lawyers for Puff Daddy Sean Combs have pointed out that their client never sexually assaulted or trafficked anyone, whether male or female, adult or minor. Mexico City. Diddy Combs was accused of drugging and sexually assaulting a young man who was starting his career as a singer in 2015, according to a report by TMZ. In a new lawsuit filed in New York by lawyer Tony Buzbee, the plaintiff alleged that the alleged assault occurred when he was 23 years old and was starting to perform as an opening act in nightclubs in Los Angeles. The man, who identified himself as John Doe, claimed that music mogul Combs had considered him for a record deal with his label Bad Boy Records if he performed well at an event where Combs would be present. The promise was broken when John Doe attended a party after the mentioned musical event, where, according to him, both Combs and his companions were consuming drugs. The plaintiff explained in the documents that he was drugged with a drink, during which he became unconscious while watching the famous person and their entourage engaging in group sex. John Doe accused that when he awoke, he noticed Combs touching his intimate parts, leading him to believe that Combs performed oral sex on him. As Doe regained consciousness, he said he attempted to fight Combs to leave the location where the party took place, but Combs threatened to ruin his opportunities in the music industry if he didn't comply. The plaintiff opted to pretend to need the bathroom to escape Combs' intentions. This accusation adds to the multiple charges faced by the singer, including possible charges for sex trafficking and organized crime. In a joint statement to Variety, the defendant's legal team declined to make a statement on the matter, stating that they have confidence that the judicial process will reveal the truth in response to the plaintiffs' allegations. As we have said before, Mr. Combs cannot respond to every new publicity stunt, even in response to allegations that are apparently ridiculous or demonstrably false. Mr. Combs and his legal team have full confidence in the facts and integrity of the judicial process. In court, the truth will prevail that Mr. Combs never sexually assaulted nor trafficked anyone, man or woman, adult or minor.

Colorado 18-3-306 CRS prohibits online harassment of a minor. This is defined as communicating sexual content to a 15-year-old minor (and more than four years younger than you) through electronic means and then attempting to meet that minor for any purpose. The language of section 183306 establishes that (1) An actor commits online harassment of a minor if the actor knows they are communicating via a computer or computer network, telephone network, or data network, or via a text message or instant message to a person the actor knows or believes to be under fifteen years of age, and, in that communication or any subsequent communication via computer, computer network, telephone network, data network, text message, or instant message, describes explicit sexual conduct as defined in section 186403(2)(e), and, in relation to that description, makes a statement persuading or inviting the person to meet the actor for any purpose, and the actor is more than four years older than the person or the age the actor believes the person to be.(2) It shall not be a defense to this section that no meeting occurred (3) Online harassment of a minor is a serious class 5 felony, except that online harassment of a minor is a serious class 4 felony if committed with the intent to meet for the purpose of participating in sexual exploitation as defined in section 18-6-403.5 or sexual contact as defined in section 18-3-401.5.(4) For the purposes of this section, "communication" means communications that promote, advance, promote, or have a continuity of purpose and can occur before, during, or after an invitation to meet. Typical penalties for online harassment of a minor can be as high as 3 years in prison, and a fine of up to $100,000. If the purpose of your communication was to arrange a meeting for the sexual exploitation of a minor or your own sexual gratification, you will be considered a sex offender in Colorado. In addition to his name being added to Colorado's sex offender registry, he will serve up to 6 years in prison and face fines of up to $500,000. A 17-year-old Venezuelan girl was rescued after being kidnapped by the dangerous Los Hijos de Dios (Children of God) crime gang in Moquegua, Peru. The intervention of the Peruvian National Police and the relentless search by her father were key to her release. The nightmare began three weeks ago when a father received an alarming message on his daughter's social media. The young girl, trapped under the control of a criminal organization, managed to send a brief message: "I am being held hostage." The kidnappers operated under the guise of offering deceitful job opportunities. Once captured, the victims were subjected to absolute control and constant abuse, according to El Popular newspaper. Threats were permanent, and the young girls had no access to anything that was not allowed by their captors, including limited use of the phone to report payments and follow instructions. Key actions taken by the father to save his daughter The father, desperate in the situation, began to negotiate with the traffickers through messages while trying to gather the money they demanded. The circumstances led him to confront the criminals directly in a desperate attempt to save his daughter. The Human Trafficking Division, along with Peruvian authorities, carried out a covert operation to liberate the young woman. After locating the Dubai Club, a nightclub where several women were being exploited, the law enforcement forces stormed the location. The authorities arrested several members responsible for the kidnapping and exploitation. This rescue not only saved the young Venezuelan woman but also motivated an investigation into the crimes committed by the faction. Updated 2150 Teleamazonas.com News Report A former teacher from a school in Pallatanga, Chimborazo, has been called to trial for his alleged responsibility in the crime of sexual abuse perpetrated against a 14-year-old student. The prosecution provided details of the incident on Monday, February 3, 2025. The decision was made by a Judge from the Multicompetent Judicial Unit, after analyzing the evidence presented by the prosecution in the evaluation and preparatory hearing. The magistrate also confirmed the precautionary measures of periodic presentation and prohibition of leaving the country against the accused, and ordered the retention of accounts for an amount of $20,000. Read also Prosecution initiated the investigation after a complaint from the rector of the educational institution, who was informed by the father of the teenager about the alleged abuse committed by the accused, who at the time was working as an English teacher. The incidents allegedly occurred on April 24, 2023, while the victim was helping the student enter grades into the system. The change in the student's behavior alerted their parents, who noticed that the teenager appeared more frustrated and sensitive. After consulting with him, the son reported what had happened with the teacher. Sexual abuse is classified as a crime in Article 170 of the Organic Integral Penal Code (COIP) and is punished with imprisonment of three to five years.

The father of Natalia Melmann, the 15-year-old girl who was kidnapped, tortured, and raped by police in the seaside city of Miramar, remembered his daughter 24 years after the femicide, while repudiating the temporary releases enjoyed by one of the convicted officers. In an interview with the Agencia Noticias Argentinas, Gustavo Melmann stated that on February 4, 2001, Natalia went to her friend VerÃ³nica's house and then went out to dance and meet Maximiliano Marolt, a young man she was in love with. She left at night, telling us to stay calm. The day after, I asked if she had returned and my wife replied that she might arrive later, the victim's father pointed out, who had returned from work and upon seeing that his daughter was not at home, he went out desperately to look for her at his friends' homes and hospitals. Since he did not receive any news about the whereabouts of the teenager, Gustavo and Laura Calampuca (mother) went to the Police to file a report for the disappearance. Evidently, they were expecting us and knew what had happened. They ordered us not to speak with the press until 48 hours had passed. The entire town came out to search for her. The Commissioner Grillo told us to look for her in different places since the nursery was being requisitioned by the officers, he stated in relation to the suspicious behavior shown by the authorities. In turn, the necropsy indicated genetic traces of five different people, confirming that she was raped by various men. Natalia's memory was very affectionate, committed, militant, and student leader. We would have breakfast together every morning. She had gone out to sell newspapers to help the household economy and pay for her studies, Gustavo described. He specified that his daughter's project was to become an obstetrician, but she did not want to have children, as she wanted to raise the children who were on the streets and did not have parents. All those projects and dreams were taken away from her, he added in statements to NA. Ricardo Panadero had been acquitted on two occasions due to lack of evidence; however, the Provincial Penal Court of Appeal decided in 2019 to annul the verdict and announced that the fourth police officer of the Bonaerense must be tried for his involvement in the crime. Gustavo Melmann explained that the perpetrators never asked for forgiveness for the murder and that they received were victims of threats, beatings, and insults from them and their families. Human Trafficking The Fact of Sexual Exploitation in a Hypersexualized Society The Web of Rape and Sexual Abductions in the United Kingdom, starring some Pakistani gangs and other immigrants, has generated a heated social, political, and judicial debate in recent years. These cases have shaken the collective conscience of the country, revealing grave failures in child protection systems, the application of the law, and cultural sensitivity in addressing crimes of such magnitude. The Facts Since the 1990s, cities such as Rotherham, Rochdale, Telford, and Newcastle have been the scene of sexual exploitation networks in which underage girls were manipulated, sexually abused, and, in many cases, subjected to situations of sexual slavery. These girls, generally from vulnerable backgrounds, were lured by adult men through gifts, alcohol, drugs, and promises of affection In 2014, an independent report led by Alexis Jay revealed that in Rotherham, approximately 1,400 girls had been victims of sexual abuse between 1997 and 2013. This report exposed the gravity of the crimes and the local authorities' inability to act, despite multiple complaints. Cases of gang rapes, extreme violence, and threats directed at both victims and their families were described. Perpetrator Profiles Most of those convicted in these networks belonged to Pakistani communities, although individuals from other ethnic groups were also involved. This fact has led to complex debates about the cultural and social roots that may be influencing this type of crime. Some experts have pointed out that in certain cultural contexts, there is a degrading view of women, especially those perceived as Western or easy targets. However, warnings have also been raised about the risk of generalizing and stigmatizing entire communities. Many voices, both within and outside Muslim communities, have strongly condemned these acts, emphasizing that the perpetrators represent a minority and that their actions do not reflect the beliefs of the majority. Systemic failures The Rotherham case and similar ones exposed systemic failures in how British institutions handled these crimes. Key problems include: Police inaction In several cases, victims or their families reported the abuse to the police, but authorities failed to act. This was partly attributed to concerns about being perceived as racist when investigating men from ethnic minorities. Negligence on the part of social services Social workers responsible for protecting vulnerable children failed to identify signs of sexual exploitation or deliberately ignored reports due to biases against the victims. Victim stigmatization Many girls were treated as problematic or complicit rather than recognized as victims of sexual abuse. This approach not only perpetuated the harm but also hindered their access to support. Lack of coordination The various agencies involved in child protection failed to work together, allowing abusers to operate undetected for years. Legal consequences Throughout the years, numerous trials have been held against the perpetrators, resulting in significant convictions. However, these processes have also been criticized for being too slow and for not adequately addressing the traumatic impact on the victims. One of the most notable cases was that of Rochdale, where nine men were convicted in 2012 of sexually exploiting minors. In Newcastle, Operation Sanctuary led to the conviction of over 20 people in 2017, including members of a sex trafficking ring that operated for several years. Impact on British society These crimes have had a profound impact on British society. On the one hand, they have generated greater awareness of child sexual exploitation and the need to protect minors more effectively. On the other hand, they have fueled racial tensions and hate speech against immigrant communities, particularly the Pakistani community. Right-wing parties, such as the British National Party (BNP) and the anti-Islamic English Defence League (EDL), have used these cases to justify their agendas, promoting narratives that link sexual abuse with mass immigration and cultural diversity.Government Responses The British government has implemented a series of measures to address this issue. These include:Independent Reviews The Alexis Jay report was one of several commissioned to investigate institutional failures. Staff Training Police officers, social workers, and other professionals have received training to identify and address child sexual exploitation more effectively.Awareness Campaigns Initiatives have been launched to educate the public about child sexual exploitation and encourage reporting of abuse.Tougher Laws Stricter laws have been introduced to punish child sexual exploitation and protect victims. Criticism of the official response Despite these efforts, the criticism persists. Many victims and activists consider the measures taken to be insufficient and that the institutions have not yet fully assumed their responsibility. The willingness to address the cultural and social roots of these crimes without fear of accusations of racism has also been questioned. Final reflection The case of the sex trafficking networks in the United Kingdom is a heart-wrenching reminder of the dangers faced by vulnerable minors and the failures of the institutions tasked with protecting them. As the country continues to grapple with the aftermath of these crimes, it is clear that an integrated approach combining justice, education, and cultural sensitivity is needed to prevent similar tragedies from recurring.

During the official ceremony, Rubio reiterated that this initiative aims to deter irregular migrant transit and combat human trafficking networks. We acknowledge that many people seeking massive migration are victims and are victimized along the way. It's not good for anyone. text: The potential return of Donald Trump to the presidency of the United States could open the door to the release of key information on the case of Jeffrey Epstein, the deceased financier accused of leading an international sex trafficking ring. Epstein's so-called "black book," which supposedly contains the names of individuals linked to his network, remains a mystery, as demands for transparency in the case continue to pile up, according to FOX News. Republican Senator Marsha Blackburn of Tennessee has been one of the most insistent voices in calling for the government to release records related to Epstein. During a Senate confirmation hearing for FBI nominee Kash Patel, Blackburn again pressed the need to reveal the names of those who flew on Epstein's private plane and those who allegedly collaborated in building his sex trafficking network. I have worked on this for years, said Blackburn, who also noted that his previous attempts to obtain this information were blocked by former FBI Director Christopher Wray and Democratic Senator Dick Durbin, then chairman of the committee. Patel, on the other hand, committed to cooperating in this effort if confirmed to the position. Child sex trafficking does not occur in the United States of America, and I will do everything possible to ensure that the American public knows the full weight of what happened in the past, he declared. A case marked by secrecy and controversy The case of Jeffrey Epstein, who died in 2019 in a New York federal prison while awaiting trial on charges of sex trafficking, has been shrouded in questions since its inception. Jeffrey Epstein, a millionaire with properties in the United States Virgin Islands and in several cities across the country, had faced similar accusations more than a decade earlier, but managed to secure a judicial agreement that allowed him to serve only 13 months in prison with daytime work permits. Epstein's black book, supposedly containing the names of prominent figures, including politicians, business leaders, and celebrities, has been the subject of speculation for years. Although a federal court ordered the release of thousands of sealed documents last year, many of the revealed names were not linked to crimes, and the full contents of the book remain unknown. Additionally, a group of 12 women who identified themselves as victims of Epstein filed a lawsuit against the FBI in 2022, accusing the agency of not adequately investigating sexual trafficking allegations dating back to the 1990s. According to the lawsuit, Epstein and his accomplices, including his former partner and collaborator Ghislaine Maxwell, abused young women and minors, some as young as 14. Ghislaine Maxwell, who was convicted for her role in Epstein's sex trafficking ring, is currently serving a sentence in a federal prison in Tallahassee, Florida, and will not be eligible for parole until 2037. Maxwell has appealed her conviction, while another Epstein associate, French modeling agent Jean-Luc Brunel, also accused of sex trafficking, was found dead in his cell under similar circumstances to Epstein. Senator Blackburn has insisted that the FBI must release the evidence it possesses, including surveillance recordings obtained from Epstein's residence in Palm Beach, Florida. We know that the FBI confiscated a large amount of surveillance material from Epstein's house in Palm Beach, where his operation was based, noted Blackburn. Why don't they publish those tapes or flight records that I've been requesting for months. The pursuit of justice The Epstein case has not only generated controversy due to the figures involved, but also due to the devastating impact on the victims. According to court documents, Epstein would recruit young people aged 14 to 16, many of whom were students of a community college in Palm Beach, for massage sessions that ended in sexual encounters. The victims were coerced with violent threats, such as You're going to die or I'm going to break your legs, as stated in the lawsuit filed against the FBI. Senator Blackburn has expressed her optimism about the possibility of getting answers under a new Trump administration. In November, following Patel's nomination as FBI director, Blackburn reiterated her commitment to the cause I hope to work with Kash Patel as the head of the FBI to release the flight records and Epstein's black book, wrote on social media platform X.

On Tuesday night, in a street in Quetta, southwest Pakistan, the police received a report of a shooting. At the scene, they found the body of Hira Anwar, a 14-year-old American citizen, with gunshot wounds. Her father, Anwar ul Haq, initially claimed they had been attacked by strangers. However, after being interrogated, he confessed to being the killer. According to the police, the motive for the crime was the videos the teenager posted on TikTok, an activity her family considered inappropriate and contrary to traditional values. The crime has been classified as a possible honor killing, a practice still widespread in Pakistan, where hundreds of women are killed by their own family members each year due to perceptions of shame. According to the Pakistan Human Rights Commission, at least 588 cases were reported in 2024, an increase from the 490 reported in 2023, The New York Times reported. Hira was born in the United States, where her family lived for 25 years before recently returning to Pakistan. In New York, the teenager led a life similar to that of any young person her age, socializing with friends and sharing content on social media. However, according to The New York Times, within her home, she faced the strict expectations of her family, which demanded that she adhere to dress and behavior norms consistent with her culture of origin. Her father, who holds U.S. citizenship, stated that he began to disapprove of his daughter's behavior while they still lived in the United States, as he considered her presence on social media to be contrary to modesty and the values she should respect. After returning to Pakistan, Hira continued to post videos, which generated a conflict with her family, reported the BBC. Authorities also arrested the brother-in-law of ulHaq, who would have been involved in the murder The police confiscated Hira's mobile phone, although, according to Reuters, they have yet to unlock it. The weight of honor crimes in Pakistan Despite Pakistan implementing reforms to punish honor crimes more severely, they continue to occur frequently. In 2016, following the murder of social media star Qandeel Baloch, Parliament closed a legal loophole that allowed victims' relatives to pardon perpetrators, thus avoiding punishment. However, violence against women continues due to social acceptance and lack of law enforcement, reported the BBC. Similar cases have been registered both in Pakistan and migrant communities. According to The New York Times, in 2022, two Pakistani-origin sisters living in Spain were tricked into traveling to Pakistan, where they were murdered by their relatives for refusing arranged marriages. In Italy, a Pakistani couple was sentenced to life in prison in 2023 for the murder of their 18-year-old daughter, who had rejected a forced marriage. Experts on South Asian diaspora communities say intergenerational tensions are common within migrant communities. In many cases, young people born abroad challenge traditional family norms, leading to conflicts. According to Kavita Mehra, executive director of Sakhi for South Asian Survivors, in an interview with The New York Times, nearly half of South Asians in the US have experienced some form of gender-based violence, not because the community is more violent, but due to the persistence of patriarchal patterns and intergenerational trauma. The Future of the Case and Its International Implications The murder of Hira Anwar has not only sparked outrage within Pakistan, but it could also have implications in the United States, as her father is an American citizen. According to Reuters, it has not been confirmed whether the U.S. embassy has been informed of the case or if U.S. authorities will take any action. If the crime is classified as an honor killing, ulHaq will face mandatory life imprisonment due to changes in the law introduced in 2016. Prior to that reform, many accused individuals avoided legal punishment if they obtained forgiveness from the victim's family, the BBC reported. Authorities continue to investigate the details of the case while activists insist that the fight against honor crimes in Pakistan must be a state priority, without relying on the decision of families to seek justice.

Portugal has held the captain of the fishing vessel Loitador upon his return from Cabo Verde, which occurred last Saturday, but he is now a free man. It will be up to the National Court to decide whether he should be extradited to Argentina on charges of labor exploitation. The Loitador case, opened by the Caleta Olivia Prosecutor's Office (Santa Cruz Province, Argentina) against the captain of the Galician fishing vessel on suspicion of labor exploitation on board, is unusual for multiple reasons. Firstly, because there are no precedents for a judicial action of this kind, in any fishing ground, and least of all with a Spanish-flagged vessel. The complaint originated from the doctor who treated a Senegalese sailor in June 2017, who arrived in a coma after evacuation and recounted a torturous treatment of working 22 hours a day, Monday to Monday, under the responsibility of the highest authority of the trawler. In third place, because Argentina has assumed jurisdiction because the Loitador made a stop twice in the Malvinas during the four months in which these supposed abuses against crew members were prolonged, and Buenos Aires claims that this territory (or Falklands, in its English designation) is theirs. A combination of elements has already resulted in the intervention of the Portuguese police, pending a decision on whether the 56-year-old Galician captain will be extradited. The captain was detained last Saturday in Lisbon upon his arrival from Cabo Verde, to which he traveled precisely on board the Loitador, which is now sailing towards the port of Montevideo. It is common for this type of ship transfer operations to be carried out from MarÃ­n, for example, as in this case, to an intermediate port or the destination port. Sources from the shipowner's legal representation, Profesionales Pesqueros, did not provide details about this police intervention in the Portuguese capital. The captain is already with his family and under provisional freedom awaiting a judicial hearing, which will determine whether he should be extradited to Argentina to give a statement there. The hearing will take place at the National Court, as stipulated in Article 12 of the Passive Extradition Law, his lawyer clarified. In Portugal, there is no procedure, he added. Although the case dates back to June 2017, it was on November 13 that the captain's detention was ordered by the Federal Court of Caleta Olivia, which issued a red notice through Interpol, informed the Public Ministry in a statement. The red notice is a request addressed to law enforcement worldwide to locate and provisionally detain a person pending extradition or delivery. That detention was carried out by the Spanish police on December 18. The captain gave a statement for three hours and was released on provisional liberty. He is accused of a crime of human trafficking for labor exploitation, taking advantage of the vulnerability of evacuee sailor E. Thiam, 35 years old at the time. The shipping company has denied the accusations from the start, considering them unfounded, as well as the supposed multiple victims, which the Argentine Public Prosecutor's Office also affirms. Profesionales Pesqueros has actually alluded to a political issue due to the link between the Loitador, affiliated with the Vigo Shipowners Cooperative (ARVI), and the Malvinas.

The complaint originated from the doctor who treated a Senegalese sailor in June 2017, who arrived in a coma after evacuation and recounted a torturous treatment of working 22 hours a day, Monday to Monday, under the responsibility of the highest authority of the trawler. In third place, because Argentina has assumed jurisdiction because the Loitador made a stop twice in the Malvinas during the four months in which these supposed abuses against crew members were prolonged, and Buenos Aires claims that this territory (or Falklands, in its English designation) is theirs. A combination of elements has already resulted in the intervention of the Portuguese police, pending a decision on whether the 56-year-old Galician captain will be extradited. The captain was detained last Saturday in Lisbon upon his arrival from Cabo Verde, to which he traveled precisely on board the Loitador, which is now sailing towards the port of Montevideo. It is common for this type of ship transfer operations to be carried out from MarÃ­n, for example, as in this case, to an intermediate port or the destination port. Sources from the shipowner's legal representation, Profesionales Pesqueros, did not provide details about this police intervention in the Portuguese capital. The captain is already with his family and under provisional freedom awaiting a judicial hearing, which will determine whether he should be extradited to Argentina to give a statement there. The hearing will take place at the National Court, as stipulated in Article 12 of the Passive Extradition Law, his lawyer clarified. In Portugal, there is no procedure, he added. Although the case dates back to June 2017, it was on November 13 that the captain's detention was ordered by the Federal Court of Caleta Olivia, which issued a red notice through Interpol, informed the Public Ministry in a statement. The red notice is a request addressed to law enforcement worldwide to locate and provisionally detain a person pending extradition or delivery. That detention was carried out by the Spanish police on December 18. The captain gave a statement for three hours and was released on provisional liberty. He is accused of a crime of human trafficking for labor exploitation, taking advantage of the vulnerability of evacuee sailor E. Thiam, 35 years old at the time. The shipping company has denied the accusations from the start, considering them unfounded, as well as the supposed multiple victims, which the Argentine Public Prosecutor's Office also affirms. Profesionales Pesqueros has actually alluded to a political issue due to the link between the Loitador, affiliated with the Vigo Shipowners Cooperative (ARVI), and the Malvinas.

The Indonesian government launched a commission on Monday to define the minimum age required for access to social media, in an attempt to protect children and adolescents from online threats, following the example of countries such as Australia, which already has similar regulations. Communication and Digital Media Minister Meutya Hafid said that along with the Executive, a team of academics, professionals, and representatives of NGOs dedicated to child protection will draft a regulation, which they hope to have ready in two months. We cannot allow children to grow up in a digital environment filled with threats. This team will work to strengthen regulations, increase supervision, and take firm action against hazardous content so that Indonesian children can navigate the internet safely, the minister expressed. In the official note, the Government stated that there are threats that increasingly lurk around minors, such as online gambling, pornography, sexual harassment, and violence, thus seeking to ensure a stricter application of the law against perpetrators and distributors of hazardous content. In this sense, one of the fundamental aspects to be studied will be the minimum age to access social networks, without knowing what age is being considered yet. Likewise, the Government aims to improve digital literacy among children and parents so that they are more aware of the risks in the cyber space. According to government statistics, 89% of children over five years old use the internet only to access social networks in Indonesia, which has the fourth highest rate of child pornography cases worldwide. At the end of 2024, Australia prohibited minors under 16 from accessing social media, a measure that has also been proposed in places such as Spain, Puerto Rico, and New York. Source EFE.

February 3, 2025. Pope Francis called for the protection of undocumented children at the US border and stated they are the first victims of that exodus of desperation in the opening of the summit on children's rights held in the Vatican. In his opening speech for the International Summit on Children's Rights titled "AmÃ©moslos y protejÃ¡moslos" (Let Us Love Them and Protect Them) at the Apostolic Palace in the Vatican, the Pontiff cried out against nationalist interests that kill children under bombs and condemned many of them to die as migrants at sea or due to violence among criminal gangs. He also attacked lethal practices such as abortion and denounced that many minors worldwide succumb to neglect or various forms of exploitation. Abortion suppresses the lives of children and cuts off the source of hope for all society, he cried out. The Holy Father also lamented that just as many die in the desert or on the multiple routes of desperate journeys of hope. Killing the little ones is to deny the future. In some cases, the children themselves are forced to fight under the effects of drugs. Even in countries where there is no war, violence between criminal gangs is just as deadly for children and often leaves them orphans and marginalized, he insisted. He also made it clear that not even the richest world is immune to injustice and noted the existence of other problems related to mental health. To a greater extent than in the past, schools and healthcare services have to deal with children who are already experiencing many difficulties, with young people with anxiety or depression, with adolescents who take the path of aggression or self-harm, he assured. In this way, he denounced the excessive individualism of developed countries and said that children in these contexts are also mistreated or even repressed by those who should protect and raise them. And he added that they are victims of their parents' fights, social or mental anguish, and addictions. Subsequently, Pope Francis urged those present to ask how a child's life can end this way. The Pontiff expressed himself thus in the presence of various personalities such as Jordan's Queen Rania, Italian Senator for Life Liliana Segre, survivor of the Nazi concentration camp Auschwitz, Indian activist Kailash Satyarthi, Nobel Peace Prize winner in 2014, or Al Gore, former US Vice President. It is not acceptable and we must resist habituation. The denied childhood is a silent cry that denounces the injustice of the economic system, the criminality of wars, the lack of medical attention and schooling, he indicated. Thus, he criticized certain media dynamics that tend to make humanity insensitive, causing a hardening of minds in general. We risk losing the most noble part of the human heart, pity, mercy, he lamented as he opened this event organized in the Clementine Hall of the Vatican by the Pontifical Committee for the World Day of the Child. Pope Francis denounces dramatic situations of childhood around the world The Holy Father used his address to give a rundown of the grave situations that children must face in many parts of the world. In this way, he pointed out that more than forty million children are displaced due to conflicts and that nearly a hundred million do not have a home. He also mentioned the drama of child slavery. One hundred and sixty million children are victims of forced labor, trafficking, abuse, and all kinds of exploitation, including forced marriages, he affirmed. On the other hand, he cited the serious phenomenon of the millions of migrant children traveling alone, as well as the problem that they do not have legal documents. Many other minors live in limbo because they were not registered at birth. It is estimated that around 150 million invisible children do not have legal existence, he noted after highlighting the practical consequences such as lack of access to education or healthcare. Moreover, he indicated that, without legal protection, they can easily become victims of abuse or be sold as slaves. He also added that we remember the Rohingya youth, who often struggle to be registered, undocumented children at the border with the United States, the first victims of that exodus of desperation and hope of thousands who rise from the South to the United States, and many others. In the same way, he criticized the logic of disposal in which the human being becomes omnipotent, and unborn life is sacrificed through the murderous practice of abortion. The Vatican hopes that this quote will help build a platform capable of addressing the most pressing issues related to the rights of children, while promoting international cooperation for a safer and more equitable world for children worldwide. ACI PRENSA Bulletin

February 2, 2025. Ambassadors of Hope. Together Against Human Trafficking is the motto of the 11th World Day of Prayer and Reflection Against Human Trafficking 2025, which will take place on February 8, a date instituted by Pope Francis in 2015, on the feast day of Saint Bakhita, an African nun who was a slave and is a symbol in the Church of the fight against this scourge that affects millions. The name Bakhita means fortunate, and she received it at the age of 9 by the will of the human traffickers, while Josefina was given to her 12 years later, when she was baptized. A note from the organizers recalls that, according to the UN, currently there are around 50 million people who are victims of human trafficking, with 79% being women and girls. In this context, around 1.2 billion people are forced to migrate due to wars, poverty, or natural disasters, situations that put them at risk of being victims of human trafficking. The organizers highlight that there will be various activities in different parts of the world over the next week, with a special agenda in Rome, which will center around a meeting with Pope Francis. This Sunday, February 2, activities began with the participation of some members of the Global Network against Human Trafficking in the Angelus with the Holy Father. On Monday, February 3, delegations of young people from the aforementioned network will make a pilgrimage to three Holy Doors, using the Walking in Dignity (Walking with dignity) application. On February 4 at 4:30 PM (local time), there will be a flashmob against human trafficking in Santa Maria in Trastevere Square, followed at 5:30 PM by an Ecumenical Vigil of Prayer in English and Italian at the Basilica of Santa Maria in Trastevere. On Wednesday, February 5, activities on the topic will continue. On Thursday, February 6, there will be a pilgrimage of young people, and in the afternoon, from 4:00 to 7:00 PM, at the Pontifical University of Saint Thomas Aquinas, the event "Call to Hope and Healing" will take place, with testimonies from some survivors of human trafficking, activists, and the presentation of artists such as the Gen Verde group. On Friday, February 7, in the morning, Pope Francis will meet with the delegation of young ambassadors, survivors, and representatives of the network of organizations promoting the Journey. Following this, there will be an online pilgrimage of prayer and reflection against human trafficking worldwide, which will be broadcast in 5 languages (English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, and Italian) and can be followed on [URL]. On Saturday, February 8, the young ambassadors will meet for a full day of dialogue and work to make a new global call for concrete actions against human trafficking. On the occasion of the Church's Jubilee, in light of this year's World Day of Prayer and Reflection, as pilgrims of hope, we make an appeal to all to act against human trafficking, said Sister Abby Avelino, coordinator of the Journey. All these initiatives are coordinated by Talitha Kum, the international network against human trafficking, with over 6,000 sisters, friends, and collaborators. The organizers invite you to dedicate a tweet on February 7 and 8 using the hashtags #PrayAgainstTrafficking and #iubilaeum2025. More information at URL ACI PRENSA Newsletter

The Dominican Republic received 213 citizens as deportees from the United States and Puerto Rico in January, amidst a change in administration and the tightening of policies against undocumented immigrants carried out by Donald Trump and his cabinet. Of the Dominicans deported from these two countries last month, 125 were returned for having entered US territory illegally, a figure representing nearly 60% of the total repatriations, according to data shared by the General Directorate of Migration (DGM) in a request for information. The United States deported 197 Dominicans, and 16 nationals arrived from Puerto Rico. A year ago, deportations from the two countries in January totaled 190, with 186 and four, respectively. The rest of the deportees entered the country after committing drug-related crimes (38), theft (10), robbery (11), illegal possession of firearms (8), homicide (6), violence (5), sexual abuse or offense (5), and human trafficking (2) while abroad. Three Dominicans were returned due to fraud, money laundering, and false documents, one for each category of crime.US media report that the Trump Administration has sent only eight military planes carrying migrants to three Latin American countries, with four arriving in Guatemala and two headed to Colombia. However, President Gustavo Petro prohibited their landing, using Colombian Air Force planes to locate their deportees. The remaining planes arrived in Honduras on Friday. Two civilian planes also arrived in Honduras, carrying a hundred deportees each, with Hondurans on these planes part of the latest deportations by the Biden Administration, while those on military planes are from those captured in Texas and other border points, in compliance with the new measures by President Trump, being applied to all countries. So far, there has been no report of military planes entering Dominican territory. Rubio to speak about migrants in visit The Dominican Republic will be the last destination of the first foreign trip of the US Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, who started a tour of Latin America on Saturday to attend several allied countries with the migratory issue as the main objective of his visit. The Secretary Rubio's participation with high-ranking officials and business leaders will promote regional cooperation in our essential and common interests to stop large-scale illegal migration, fight against the scourge of transnational criminal organizations and narco-traffickers, counter China and deepen economic alliances to improve prosperity in our hemisphere, the State Department said on Friday about the agenda of the US top diplomat. Rubio began his trip in Panama, then will travel to El Salvador, Costa Rica, and Guatemala, from where he will depart for the Dominican Republic on next Wednesday, February 5, just as five months since the visit of his predecessor Antony Blinken, who made in September last year his first and last trip to the island of Hispaniola as Secretary of State.

SOCIETY The Fall of Diddy MAX Released a Documentary About the Rapper Arrested for Multiple Abuses More than 130 accusations in three decades. Since November 2023, over 130 people have accused rapper Sean Combs, known as Diddy or Puff Daddy, of sexual crimes, violence, and extortion. Incidents spanning from the 1990s to the present. Combs is currently in prison without bail, charged with multiple counts, including human trafficking. The rapper was arrested in September 2024 at a Manhattan hotel under charges of conspiracy to commit organized crimes and human trafficking. The accusations indicate that Combs abused, threatened, and coerced women and other individuals since 2008, committing crimes such as kidnapping, bribery, and obstruction of justice. Among the crimes are sexual assaults, rapes, chemical submission, and a history of violence against women. The documentary "The Fall of Diddy" on Max features up to 30 testimonies from victims and witnesses, while the prosecution continues to expand the charges. Combs has a history of violence and scandals that are not unfamiliar to legal problems. In 1999, he was arrested along with Jennifer Lopez after a shooting at a Manhattan club. Although he was acquitted, one of the victims, Natania Reuben, claims that Combs shot her and is willing to undergo testing to reopen the case.Over the years, several women have accused him of rape, drugs, and aggression, taking advantage of a temporary law that eliminated the statute of limitations for sex crimes in New York. The complaint that initiated the current wave of accusations is from November 2023, presented by Casandra Ventura, known as Cassie, who had a relationship with Combs between 2005 and 2018. Ventura alleged that Combs drugged her, coerced her into having sex with third parties, and recorded these encounters. The complaint was resolved extrajudicially the next day, presumably for a multimillion-dollar sum. Incriminating evidence and arrest On May 17, 2024, CNN published a video showing Combs physically assaulting Cassie at a Los Angeles hotel. Although Combs published a video assuming responsibility for his actions in that recording, he did not apologize to the victim or mention her name. Following the publication of the video, new complaints emerged, including allegations of drug addiction and sexual assaults by former collaborators and other victims. In June, a man also accused Combs of sexual abuse in 1997. Combs' failure to appear in court resulted in a $100 million conviction. Combs was arrested in September 2024 by federal agents at a Manhattan hotel. The District Attorney described those parties as planned events where drugs were used for sexual submission and recordings were used to extort participants. Legal and social consequencesAttorney Tony Buzbee announced lawsuits of over 120 people against Combs, including men, women, and minors. These lawsuits also aim to hold Combs' accomplices accountable. Meanwhile, Combs remains the only accused, facing sentences that could range from 15 years to life imprisonment.The documentary about Diddy on Max The 1st of February premiered Fall of an Icon P. Diddy, a documentary that explores in detail Diddy's life and career, presenting statements from people close to the musician, who claimed to have witnessed the questioned behaviors. The production gathered over 30 interviews, including accusers, former friends, colleagues, and employees Additionally, several people publicly shared their experiences with the music mogul for the first time, according to information. This is part of four episodes in collaboration with Rolling Stone Films and Sony Pictures Television.

The US Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, said on Monday in Panama that the US border, to a certain extent, does not start in Texas and Mexico, but rather much earlier, after witnessing a deportation flight of migrants paid for by the US. So, to a certain extent, our border does not start in Texas and Mexico, it starts much earlier, Rubio said at the Albrook International Airport, on the outskirts of Panama City and on the banks of the Canal. He added that the best thing the US government can do is create all the incentives for people not to carry out that type of journey. Rubio was present at the deportation process of 43 Colombian migrants on a flight paid for by the US as part of an agreement with Panama. According to Panamanian authorities, the migrants, 32 men and 7 women, have crimes such as human trafficking, sexual assault, drug-related crimes, and most of them, evasion of border control checkpoints. This (agreement) is evidence of the great alliance that exists between the U.S. and Panama, a friendly and brotherly country with which we have many links and cooperation. What has happened in this hemisphere with massive immigration is very lamentable, a tragedy, added the U.S. Secretary of State. Thus, he said, that migrants in many cases are victims of an irregular route that has created problems for many countries in the region and that they intend to arrive in the United States. Today we have seen part of a cooperation program that helps not only to limit illegal migration, but also to prevent people with criminal backgrounds, of which there were 6 or 7 in this group, from moving forward and creating problems not only in Panama, but also in other countries, said Rubio. That would be impossible without the cooperation of the United States with the Government of Panama, as both have worked very hard, strongly, and together, and we will continue to do so as part of many things. The flight is part of the understanding memorandum between the U.S. and Panama signed on July 1, the same day of the inauguration of Panamanian President JosÃ© RaÃºl Mulino, to reduce the migratory flow through the DariÃ©n, the border jungle with Colombia used daily by migrants who dream of reaching the United States in search of better living conditions. Since the agreement was put into operation on August 20, the United States has funded almost $2.7 million in flights and tickets for the return of migrants to their countries of origin, according to information from the U.S. Government. In particular, 42 charter flights have been made to more than 14 countries, including Colombia, Ecuador, India, and Vietnam, in addition to the repatriation of nationals from countries such as Russia, Afghanistan, Pakistan, Ghana, and Turkey via commercial flights, with a total of 1,729 migrants, according to official information shared by US authorities. To date, due to the lack of a bilateral agreement, deportation flights have not been made to Venezuela, the main nationality of migrants crossing the jungle. The flow of irregular migrants entering through the DariÃ©n jungle, a hazardous route, marked a historic drop in January, with 2,158 migrants registered, compared to the 34,839 who made the journey in the same period last year, according to official data released over the weekend by the National Migration Service of Panama. Rubio arrived in Panama on Saturday night, amidst tensions over Donald Trump's threats to reclaim the Canal due to the alleged presence of China, as part of a tour that will also take him to El Salvador, where he will depart on Monday, Costa Rica, Guatemala, and the Dominican Republic.

Pallatanga (Chimborazo), February 3, 2025. Juan Enrique T. L., a former teacher at an educational unit in Pallatanga, was called to trial for his alleged responsibility in the crime of sexual abuse perpetrated against a 14-year-old student. The decision was made by a Judge of the Multijurisdictional Judicial Unit, after analyzing the elements of conviction presented by the Prosecution in the evaluation and preparatory hearing. The Magistrate also ratified the preventive measures of periodic presentation and prohibition of leaving the country against the defendant, and ordered the retention of accounts for an amount of $20,000. The Prosecution initiated the investigation after a complaint from the rector of the educational institution, who was informed by the victim's father about the alleged abuse committed by Juan Enrique T. L., an English teacher. The facts allegedly occurred on April 24, 2023, while the victim was helping him enter grades into the system. The student's change in behavior alerted his parents, who noticed that the young man was becoming more frustrated and sensitive. After consulting with him, the son recounted what had happened with the teacher. In the proceedings, the prosecutor in charge of the case issued the accusatory opinion based on the elements of conviction gathered during the fiscal instruction phase, including the testimonies of the adolescent's parents, the teachers of the educational unit, and the psychological, medical-legal, and social environment assessments. Legal information The crime of sexual abuse is defined in Article 170 of the Organic Integral Penal Code (COIP) and is punishable by imprisonment of three to five years. (FGE)

Latin American Summary, February 3, 2025. While the government questions the legal figure of femicide and threatens to eliminate it from the Penal Code, a survey conducted in the first month of 2025 found that in the country, there was a death due to gender violence every 26 hours. The report also revealed that 60% of the aggressors were partners or ex-partners of the victims and that 70% of the women were murdered in their homes. While the Government of Javier Milei evaluates eliminating the figure of femicide from the Penal Code and asserts that feminism is a distortion of the concept of equality, the reality in Argentina throws chilling numbers according to the Femicide Observatory Adriana Marisel Zambrano, which is directed by La Casa del Encuentro, 28 women were killed by gender violence in the country alone in January, which is equivalent to a femicide every 26 hours. Those crimes, according to the report released on Monday, left 27 children without a mother, 49% of whom are under the age of 18. The report also revealed that 60% of the aggressors were partners or ex-partners of the victims and that the most insecure place for a woman in a situation of violence remains her home or the shared home with the aggressor, as 70% were assassinated in their own home. In Argentina, in one month, there were 28 victims of gender violence. From January 1 to December 31, 2025, there were 27 femicides of women and girls and 1 femicide of an adult male linked to them, according to a new report from the Observatory of Femicides in Argentina.Adriana Marisel Zambrano (@Casadelencuentro) February 3, 2025Of the total cases, the observatory described, five victims had filed a complaint, two femicides had a precautionary measure of prevention issued, and four femicides are members or ex-members of a security force. The report also revealed that one victim showed signs of sexual abuse, two victims were migrants, four femicides were suicidal, and two victims were in a context of narco-criminality. Regarding the distribution of cases, the observatory detailed that Buenos Aires remains the province with the most femicides, followed by Santa Fe, Mendoza, and CABA. The Casa del Encuentro tracks femicide cases since 2008 and for many years was the only observatory that provided statistics on the murders of women, girls, and diverse people across the country, which were used to develop public policies and laws for prevention and protection. The Government Against the Figure of Femicide On January 23, amidst all the grievances that President Javier Milei scattered during his speech in Davos, which generated a strong social repudiation that was expressed on the streets this Saturday, during the Federal March of Antifascist and Antiracist Pride, the head of state said that it was wrong to normalize that if one kills a woman, it be called femicide. According to the far-right leader, this would imply a more severe punishment if one kills a woman solely because of the victim's sex, effectively legalizing the fact that a woman's life is worth more than a man's. The Minister of Justice, Mario Cuneo Libarona, then ratified the presidential statements, assuring that he would eliminate the figure of femicide from the Penal Code because this administration defends equality before the law, as enshrined in our National Constitution, and no life is worth more than another. Days later, following the massive backlash generated by Milei's grievances, sources at the Casa Rosada had leaked that they would be recalculating and evaluating going back on the idea because technical officials warned that, in the event of advancing with the elimination of that figure, they could end up freeing hundreds of convicted murderers sentenced for femicides under the most lenient law principle. This Monday, however, according to the News Agency of Argentina, there would be those in the government who consider the march on Saturday to be irrelevant and that it will not affect the executive's plans to advance with the anti-feminist agenda, which seeks to end what the Government calls positive discrimination and will include the elimination of the femicide label contemplated in the Penal Code. Un Incredible Story, the US Justification for Rejecting the Relocation of Formerly Incarcerated Nicaraguan Individuals, February 3, 2025, 8:00 a.m.Inside a dimly lit bus, with windows covered by curtains, a group of 135 inmates wonder about their uncertain future. Hours earlier, they were taken out of their cells, ordered to shower and dress, and handed newly issued passports. Months of hell ended in just a few hours. They suspect they will leave the country, but are unaware of their destination.Kevin O'Reilly, the US Embassy's Economic Officer, arrives and greets them enthusiastically. He presents them with two options: return to their cells in Nicaragua or travel to Guatemala. According to several of the newly released individuals, the initial promise was that the Central American country would be merely a layover on their way to the United States. O'Reilly explains to the now-exiled individuals that they were made to sign a document. Their release was a negotiated and agreed-upon treatment over months between the Sandinista regime and the United States, then under the administration of Democrat Joe Biden. Eric Jacobstein, the Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for Central America at the United States Department of State, during the press conference held on September 5, 2024, reported that these released individuals would have the opportunity to seek legal pathways to rebuild their lives outside of Nicaragua, including in the United States, through the Safe Passage Program. Guatemala's Foreign Minister, Carlos Ramiro MartÃ­nez, during the same event, announced that the Guatemalan Migration Institute granted 90 days to Nicaraguan deportees to regularize their migratory status. According to his words, one possibility was to remain in Guatemala or continue their journey to other countries. La Paz, February 3 (EFE). The Bolivian Public Prosecutor's Office announced on Monday that it will take the necessary precautions to find the alleged victim within the investigation into aggravated human trafficking against former President Evo Morales (2006-2019), in response to the assertions of the former head of state and his entourage that the woman does not exist. We will also take the necessary precautions because it cannot be that they say with such certainty and that is what worries us as the Public Ministry, that they say with such certainty that the victim does not exist, said the departmental prosecutor of Tarija, Sandra GutiÃ©rrez, who is handling the case. GutiÃ©rrez reacted in this way to the repeated statements of the former head of state, his lawyers, and parliamentarians close to him, who claim that there is no victim in this case. Morales reiterated on Sunday during a program on the radio station Kawsachun Coca that if there is no victim, there is no crime, and in this process, there is no victim, so he insisted that the case was opened as part of a persecution to prevent him from becoming a candidate in the general elections scheduled for August. The prosecutor recalled that in a much more serious case in 2023, a 30-year prison sentence without the right to pardon was achieved for a confessed murderer, the maximum penalty in Bolivian legislation, despite not having found the body of the victim. GutiÃ©rrez mentioned an audio, whose authenticity is unknown, in which the victim allegedly declared themselves in hiding. He also indicated that this is why the case of suspected human trafficking is being investigated, in which the victims are the young woman with whom Morales allegedly had a relationship when she was a minor and their daughter, whose whereabouts have been unknown since October 2. We are concerned that they will go out happily to say, not only Evo Morales, but also his lawyers and assembly members, that the victim does not exist. That is left for you (journalists), why they are so certain that the victim does not exist, he insisted and indicated that the young woman has all the guarantees to be part of the case. A court declared Morales in default on January 17, after the politician did not appear in two occasions to a hearing that was supposed to resolve the accusation against him for aggravated human trafficking, citing illness. The Justice also prohibited him from leaving the country, ordered the preventive notation of his assets, the freezing of his bank accounts, and the issuance of a warrant for his apprehension against the also former leader of the governmental Movement to Socialism (MAS). In October, the Prosecutor's Office had already issued a capture order, in response to which Morales' followers blocked roads for 24 days to prevent his detention. In addition to the case in Tarija, there are seven more complaints of alleged abuse against minors against the former president Morales in the central region of Cochabamba. Morales has not left the Cochabamba Tropics since October, his union and political stronghold, where he is being protected by hundreds of coca growers and peasants. The judicial process has exacerbated the relationship between Morales and the President of Bolivia, Luis Arce, who have been distant since the end of 2021 due to differences in the administration of the State and control of the MAS.

The capture was carried out after a hearing on precautionary measures on February 3, 2025. At this hearing, the Prosecution presented evidence that links the sergeant to the crimes that would have been committed at the end of January. Details of the accusation Gonzalo Aparicio, departmental prosecutor, reported that the Public Ministry sustained its accusation with indications that point to the sergeant as the perpetrator of the crimes. The accused had taken on the role of custodian at the rehabilitation center for adolescents with legal problems since January of this year. The Prosecution made several requests in this case. Among them are the psychological reports of the victims, which fully identify their perpetrator. The victims stated that the alleged trafficker threatened them, the prosecutor explained. Additionally, the location where the accused lived with the adolescents was recorded, and other elements were gathered that demonstrate the accused's responsibility. Precautionary measures and the accused's status The judge decided to impose preventive detention on the sergeant while the investigations continue. Mijael Agudo, the prosecutor assigned to this case, mentioned that the accused, in a state of intoxication, would approach the victims during the early morning hours and enter their rooms, where he would touch their intimate areas. This incident was reported by the Director of the Departmental Service for Social Management (Sedeges), who alerted about the situation of the adolescents in the rehabilitation center.

Frederik Landabur, the president of the Chile Diverso Foundation, an organization that promotes the rights of sexual and gender diversity, and a recognized militant of the Socialist Party (PS), was detained for crimes of child sexual abuse and exploitation. The detention occurred after Gianina Figueroa, an employee of the Ex-Prison Cultural Park in ValparaÃ­so, reported to the Investigative Police (PDI) that she had received an email from Landabur on January 31, which included a video with explicit content that showed child sexual abuse. The case of Frederik Landabur not only generates concern, but also the proximity of the detained man to high-profile political figures such as Socialist Party President Paulina Vodanovic and former President Michelle Bachelet, as well as various PS leaders. Following the details of the complaint being made public, the Supreme Court of the Socialist Party decided to immediately suspend Landabur's membership. The investigation, led by the PDI, aims to determine the origin of the audiovisual material and whether there are more victims related to the case. Landabur will remain in preventive detention until the investigation advances and his legal situation is defined.

The Alliance is defined as a platform for Latin American and Caribbean integration, with an emphasis on the social dimension. It consists of Venezuela, Cuba, Bolivia, Nicaragua, Dominica, Antigua and Barbuda, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Grenada, and Saint Lucia, and the invited countries of Syria, Haiti, and Suriname. There are 7.9 million migrants and refugees dispersed worldwide, with the vast majority in Colombia, Peru, Brazil, the United States, and Chile, according to the Interagency Platform coordinated by UNHCR and IOM. One out of every four Venezuelans now lives outside their country, and in many of their destinations, they have found opportunities, but they also face inequality in the labor market, lack of housing, food insecurity, and limited access to health and education, according to UN agencies. Today, 7 million Venezuelans within the country need humanitarian aid, and the economic and political crisis continues to drive that diaspora. Chavismo denies the migrant numbers provided by the records of receiving governments. The head of state asserts, instead, that economic sanctions imposed on his government (in retaliation for human rights violations, attacks on democracy, alleged narcotics trafficking and corruption crimes) have caused the migration of nearly 2.5 million people, of whom more than 1.25 million have returned. The Salta justice system sentenced him to four years and six months in prison for the crime of sexual abuse. Zanchetta was under house arrest and was granted permission to travel to Rome. The Appellate Court decided to ratify the sentence of four years and six months in prison for the simple continued crime of sexual abuse aggravated by being committed by a religious cult minister. The sentence had been imposed by the Trial Court, Chamber II of the District Court of OrÃ¡n. Zanchetta's defense had presented a cassation appeal that was rejected by the Appellate Court. In the Appellate Court, judges Virginia Solorzano and Pablo Arancibia acted. In the case, victims of the religious minister participated, and evidence was presented to confirm his guilt.
