The British Labour government wants to make images of child sexual abuse generated by artificial intelligence (AI) illegal, announced Interior Minister Yvette Cooper on Sunday. The Home Office announced that the UK could become the first country in the world to consider illegal the possession, creation, or distribution of AI tools designed to create material for child sexual abuse purposes. If the legislation passes, as expected since the government has a majority in the House of Commons, the possession of these AI tools will carry a penalty of up to five years in prison. Possession of manuals that teach people how to use AI for abuse will also be illegal, and offenders can be sentenced to three years in prison. What we are seeing is that AI is increasing child abuse online, said Interior Minister Yvette Cooper to the British BBC network. It's a real and worrying phenomenon that we've been aware of for some time, the increase of child sexual abuse material on the internet, as well as the manipulation of children and adolescents online, was noted by the minister in another program on the Sky network. What we need to do is strengthen the law, and that includes prohibiting some AI models used for child abuse, Cooper pointed out. He explained that the National Crime Agency (NCA, in English), which investigates cybercrime and cross-border economic crimes, is saying that these additional powers are needed and that they will then be able to use them to obtain court processes in order to keep more children safe. The United Kingdom wants to make it illegal to use AI to generate material for child sexual abuse. Possession of these AI tools will carry a prison sentence of up to five years.

From Rome In a message addressed to representatives of various governments and experts who participated in the Vatican on Monday at the World Meeting on the Rights of the Child Pope Francis encouraged Building a better world For the little ones Respecting their rights, their dreams, their demand for the future and showed the catastrophic situation suffered by many children in the world. Even today, the life of millions of children is marked by poverty, war, school dropout, injustice, and exploitation, said Francis. Children and adolescents from the poorest countries, or those torn apart by tragic conflicts, are forced to face terrible trials. Not even the richest world is immune to injustices. Where, thanks to God, people do not suffer wars or hunger, there are difficult peripheries, where the little ones are often victims of fragilities and problems that we cannot underestimate, warned the Pope More than 40 million children displaced Titled Let's love and protect them, the message of Francis cited impressive figures about the situation of children in the world, more than 40 million children have been displaced by conflicts, around 100 million do not have a home, around 160 million are victims of forced labor, trafficking, abuse, and all kinds of exploitation, including forced marriages. Other millions of children are immigrants who often travel alone, without family, and around 150 million are invisible children because they are not registered legally in any record and, therefore, do not have access to education or medical care and are easily victims of abuse or sold as slaves. Many children die as migrants in the sea, in the desert or on the numerous routes of desperate hope. The Argentine Pope recalled, and added that many others succumb to lack of care or various types of exploitation. They are different situations, but before them, we ask ourselves the same question: how is it possible for a child's life to end like this? It is not acceptable what unfortunately we have seen daily in recent times, that is, children who die under bombs, sacrificed to the idols of power, ideology, and nationalist interests, Francisco said, highlighting that the excessive individualism of developed countries is also lethal for children. Today, we are here to say that we do not want this to become a new normalcy. We cannot get used to this. Certain dynamics of the media tend to desensitize humanity, causing a general hardening of minds. There is a risk of losing the most noble part of the human heart: pity, mercy, the Pope said. Francisco concluded his message by telling the participants that listening to the children who live today in violence, exploitation, or injustice serves to strengthen our "no" to war, the culture of discard and benefit, in which everything is bought and sold without respect or care for life, and mentioned as an example of the logic of discarding the homicidal practice of abortion.Al Gore and Queen of Jordan The Secretary of State (number two of the Vatican), Cardinal Pietro Parolin, had welcomed the numerous participants, including Queen Rania of Jordan, the Chancellor of Italy Antonio Tajani, the Chancellor of the Republic of Gambia Mamadou Tangara, Holocaust survivor and Italian Senator for Life Liliana Segre, the Minister of Social Development of South Africa Nokuzola Gladys Tolashe, Hungarian writer Edith Bruck, and American Al Gore, former Vice President of the United States and 2007 Nobel Peace Prize winner. Just after the Pope appeared in the Clementine Hall of the Apostolic Palace, where the conference took place, Francis had received this morning a letter and drawings from Catholic schoolchildren in Rome thanking him for taking care of them. The meeting addressed several key issues, including the rights of children in the world today, the right to education, food, nutrition, and medical care, the right to family, free time, and recreation, the right to live without violence. They also spoke about how to protect children in armed conflicts and in the face of ecological devastation. Francis concluded the conference by thanking the participants for turning the Apostolic Palace into an open observatory on the reality of childhood around the world and for making proposals to protect the rights of childhood.

In the last week of January, closures were carried out in Madre de Dios, Amazonas, HuÃ¡nuco, Piura, La Libertad, Lima, Tumbes, ApurÃ­mac, and Lambayeque. Law enforcement forces have not given up on illegal mining. From January 25 to 31, the Peruvian National Police and the Peruvian Navy, through the General Directorate of Captaincies and Coast Guards (Dicapi), in permanent coordination with the Environmental Prosecution Office, of the Public Ministry, carried out 24 closure operations in nine departments of the country, in which goods and materials valued at a total of 41,502,418 soles were seized. All actions were carried out within the framework of Legislative Decree No. 1100, which regulates the closure of illegal mining throughout the national territory. The largest number of interventions took place in Madre de Dios, where the PNP carried out eight operations and Dicapi, three. There were also operations in Amazonas (3), HuÃ¡nuco (2), Piura (2), La Libertad (2), Lima (1), Tumbes (1), ApurÃ­mac (1) and Lambayeque (1). You can also read Ambassador of the US in Peru It's essential to know the strategy of the Minem to reinforce formal mining The fight against the scourge that represents illegal mining does not cease. The Executive is determined to eradicate this illicit activity that devastates natural resources, contaminates the environment, endangers the health of the population, creates holes in the Peruvian economy and generates connected crimes such as human trafficking. To this end, we are deploying a coordinated work between the Armed Forces, the Police and the prosecution, said Premier Gustavo AdrianzÃ©n. Focus on Madre de Dios The Dicapi centered its operations in Madre de Dios, specifically in the Malinowski, Pariamanu and Madre de Dios rivers Meanwhile, in that department, the Police acted in the province of Tambopata, mainly in the districts of Inambari, Laberinto, and Las Piedras. Likewise, in Amazonas, the PNP intervened on two occasions in the district of El Cenepa, in the province of Condorcanqui, and in the district of Magdalena, in Chachapoyas. In the interdictions, at least five criminal gangs dedicated to this illicit activity were dismantled. In the interdiction operations, mining carts, draglines, detonators, suction bombs, motorcycles, fuel cans, hoppers, metal cylinders, front-end loaders, a minivan, emulsion cartridges, safety fuses, dragline barges, and compressor motors, among other goods and materials, were seized and destroyed. The Executive, through the Multisectoral Commission for the fight against illegal mining, led by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers (PCM), has planned to apply this year a strategy to combat illegal mining that will go beyond the interdiction operations, which will continue, and will cover an integral approach that will give importance to mineral formalization, the traceability of materials and explosives, and the promotion of economies.

Missing Persons Search for Two Elderly Adults in the Yungas Enters Pause, Says Fire Department ChiefThe search for two elderly adults who went missing in the Yungas of La Paz has entered a pause, according to Pavel Tobar, commander of the Antofagasta Fire Department Unit, who reported this on Monday. Currently, firefighters are no longer on the scene conducting the search, we are waiting to coordinate with investigative personnel, FELCC, and family members, Tobar told the press.On January 4, Franklin Touchard, 82 years old, and Armando Ortega, 84 years old, went for a walk in the Yungas, but they did not return, and since then, no one knows their whereabouts. Firefighters, formed by canines, the Technical and Scientific Research Institute of the Police University (IITCUP), and the divisions of Homicides and Human Trafficking were conducting the search for both individuals. They were not found, new works will be coordinated with personnel in charge of the case, Tobar added. He recalled that some belongings of the travelers were found, but he reaffirmed that the investigators are in charge of the details of what happened.

text: Brody Levesque has a long list of credits in LGBTQ media. However, the police closed in. Authorities in Santa Cruz, California, arrested a LGBTQ journalist identified as a fugitive and a violently sexually predatory individual after he failed to register as a sex offender. George Paul Bishop, 66 years old, had been living and working under the assumed name Brody Levesque in Santa Cruz County south of San Francisco since 2016. Bishop, with an extensive list of writing credits for LGBTQ media, had been using the alias Brody Levesque for several years after his arrest and conviction for child pornography creation and possession. In 2005, Bishop pleaded guilty and was sentenced to three years in prison and 12 years of probation for photographing and recording a 16-year-old boy in a slavery setup at a co-defendant's house, who was also convicted. Bishop was required to register as a Level 3 sex offender for life, but failed to do so in 2016. The Virginia State Police Sex Offender Registry lists Bishop's former residence in Annandale, Virginia, and describes him as a fugitive, a legal term for an individual who has secretly left a jurisdiction to avoid legal consequences. Bishop was processed on Friday and is being held in Santa Cruz County custody. He is scheduled for a review hearing on April 1 over a probable extradition request to Virginia. U.S. Marshals and Santa Cruz police officers served a warrant and secured Bishop's home in Capitola on Wednesday morning. In a statement to LGBTQ Nation, Lynne Brown, editor of the Washington Blade said Brody Levesque worked as a freelance writer for the Los Angeles Blade. In June 2022, Brody took on the role of editor, replacing Karen Ocamb. In June 2024, Brody's working relationship was discontinued for exaggerating and sensationalizing headlines. The last appearance of Bishop as Brody Levesque was his appointment to a media advisory board for a new LGBTQ-focused research media outlet, reported by Axios in September. CHIHUAHUA. The interim president of the State Commission for Human Rights (CEDH), Alejandro Carrasco Talavera, stated that over the years, the recruitment of girls, boys, and adolescents by organized crime in the Sierra Tarahumara has increased and that this is due to the lack of state, municipal, and federal programs. Regarding the fact that girls, boys, and adolescents are being recruited, there is a reason for this and it is that the families of this region are mostly made up of minors, which makes it easier for members of organized crime to make forced recruitment and in that sense, the incorporation of minors, mostly, in these criminal groups, explained the CEDH representative. In the same way, he said that this is a phenomenon that has increased and it is because, in addition, there are no strategies from the authorities. It's complicated to fight these criminal groups and the increase is not only happening here but throughout the country, despite the existence of various international organizations such as the Committee on the Rights of the Child, the UN, which have demanded that all necessary measures be implemented to prevent this recruitment. We are facing a case of human trafficking, said Carrasco Talavera. In the same sense, he stated that it is essential not to prejudge when there are news stories in which adolescents are detained for being part of the crime. We tend to idealize and think that they surely wanted to get involved, but for a long time, it has been possible to document (not only in Mexico but in many countries in Latin America and Africa) that adolescents are being forced to work, so we have an important tool known as the Palermo Protocol, which deals with human trafficking, and it should be activated in our country. In addition to that, the president stated that this problem is one of the ones that afflict our society and that it is essential that it is addressed both by the State and by civil society. It is very important to unite our efforts, we are observing with concern how the number of minors of legal age who are forced to participate here has been increasing, and above all, that they are adolescents, children or girls who are in a situation of vulnerability, are indigenous, do not know how to read or write, and therefore it is easier for them to be recruited by these criminal groups.

On February 3, 2025, Pope Francis delivered two significant speeches at the Vatican during the Global Summit on the Rights of Children, organized by Father Enzo Fortunato at the Pontiff's behest. In his interventions, he drew attention to the grave violations of children's rights and announced future initiatives to promote their protection. In his opening speech, the Pontiff expressed a deep concern for the sufferings that millions of children face due to wars, poverty, and exploitation. He emphasized that nothing is more valuable than the life of a child and denounced child deaths in global conflicts, stating that killing children means denying the future. Pope Francis highlighted alarming data, mentioning that approximately 40 million children have been displaced due to conflicts, 100 million live without a home, and 170 million are victims of forced labor, trafficking, abuse, and various forms of exploitation, including forced marriages. He also drew attention to the situation of unaccompanied minors, describing them as the first victims of that exodus of desperation and hope. Many minors live in limbo because they were not registered at birth. It is estimated that around 150 million invisible children do not have legal existence. This prevents them from accessing education or medical care, but above all, leaves them without legal protection, making them vulnerable to abuse or slavery. Among the factors that, according to the Pope, trample the rights of the child, he also mentioned the practice of abortion. In the name of this logic of disposal, in which humanity becomes omnipotent, the nascent life is sacrificed through the homicidal practice of abortion. Abortion eliminates the lives of children and cuts off the hope of the entire society. Queen Rania of Jordan, Rania Al Abdullah, participated in the International Summit at the Vatican. I have read a striking study on the psychological state of the most vulnerable children in Gaza. 96% stated that they felt their death was imminent. Almost half expressed their desire to die. How have we allowed our humanity to reach this point, the queen said. Senator Liliana Segre, on the other hand, recounted her tragic experience as a Jewish child deported to concentration camps under fascist laws. At that time, we were surrounded by indifference, which is sometimes worse than violence. All children are sacred and must not be touched. In his closing speech at the Summit, Pope Francis announced his intention to prepare an Apostolic Exhortation entirely dedicated to children. Sante Cavalleri

The US Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, said on Monday in Panama that the US border, to a certain extent, does not start in Texas and Mexico, but much earlier, after witnessing a deportation flight of migrants paid for by the US. US Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, made a statement on February 3, 2025, at the Marcos A. Gelabert International Airport in the City of Panama (Panama). EFEBienvenido Velasco So, to a certain extent, our border does not start in Texas and Mexico, it starts much earlier, Rubio said at the Albrook International Airport, on the outskirts of the City of Panama and on the banks of the Canal. And he added that the best that the US Government can do is create all the incentives for people not to carry out that type of trip. Rubio was present at the deportation process of 43 Colombian migrants on a flight paid for by the US as part of an agreement with Panama. According to Panamanian authorities, the 32 men and 7 women migrants have crimes such as human trafficking, sexual assault, drug-related offenses, and most of them, evasion of border control checkpoints. This (agreement) is evidence of the great alliance that exists between the US and Panama, a friendly and brotherly country with which we have many links and cooperation. What has happened in this hemisphere with massive immigration is very lamentable, a tragedy, added the US Secretary of State. Thus, he said, that migrants in many cases are victims of an irregular route that has created problems for many countries in the region and they intend to reach the United States. Today, we have seen part of a cooperation program that helps not only to limit illegal migration, but also to prevent people with criminal records, of which there were 6 or 7 in this group, from continuing on and creating problems not only in Panama, but also in other countries, Rubio said. That, he added, would be impossible without the cooperation of the United States with the Government of Panama, as both have worked very hard, strongly, and together, and we will continue doing so as part of many other things. More than 28,000 students suffered sexual abuse between 2014 and 2024 in Ecuador, according to the Ministry of Education. The 90% of the victims of sexual violence were girls. Half of them were between eight and 14 years old, according to the Ministry of Education statistics. Reference image of a suspected sex abuse crime. Photo FiscalÃ­a Author Updated Share The numbers are alarming. In just 10 years, between 2014 and 2024, a total of 28,082 students were victims of sexual violence in Ecuador, according to the National Plan for the Eradication of Violence in the Educational Context, prepared by the Ministry of Education. Throughout its 98 pages, the document reveals that the majority of the victims (90%) were girls. Although this percentage is even more alarming when it is detailed that half of them were between eight and 14 years old. Another striking data is related to the perpetrators The plan shows that 74% are not part of the educational system, that is, they are people from the closest environment of the students. While 26% is directly linked to educational institutions. The main aggressors are teachers and students, and to a lesser extent, administrative personnel, he adds. Although the educational authority points out that sexual abuse is one of the most serious types of violence, it recognizes that in schools and colleges there are also other types of violence, such as physical, psychological, and bullying. Between 2022 and 2024, the first added 5,941 cases, the second 4,567, and abuse recorded 1,195 victims. The Ministry of Education assures that 93% of the victims received accompaniment to mitigate the consequences that leave an abuse. Lorena is the mother of a 12-year-old girl who suffered sexual abuse in her school in Quito. She remembers that the perpetrators were her classmates, with whom she shared the school route. How is it possible that children are capable of doing such terrible things to their own friends, one asks with indignation. This mother complains about the lack of support from the school and the educational institution. At first, they helped us, but then they forgot. I had to change her to a different school, she comments.The Ministry of Education insists that they have a protocol in place to address these cases and provide help to the victims and their families.Severe ConsequencesLow academic performance, depression, anxiety, trauma, self-harm, and even suicide are some of the severe consequences that victims of sexual violence suffer. The National Plan to Eradicate Violence in the Educational Context says that violence creates a dysfunctional and demotivating educational environment, which affects student participation and motivation, perpetuating educational inequalities and limiting their future opportunities. Ecuador is condemned for the Norma case, a girl who was abused by her father and forced to give birth. It also acknowledges that the country has critical knots related to the prevention of violence, which stem from the lack of specialized personnel, economic resources, prioritization of plans and projects, and misinformation about existing strategies and methodologies. That's not all. According to the Plan, the authorities' lack of knowledge of laws limits their action in the face of an appearance of a case of violence, increasing the possibility of more victims existing. Five Axes of the Plan The National Plan for the Eradication of Violence in the Educational Context establishes five axes to prevent more cases of sexual violence in schools and colleges in Ecuador.Prevention Detection Abatement and Reparation Coordination among Institutions ResearchThe document's objective is that by 2023, at least 95% of schools and colleges implement a prevention methodology for the different types of violence. It also aims for 70% of families and teachers to receive training to identify signs of violence in the educational system.

Bangkok, February 4 (EFE). The Thai government announced on Tuesday that it will immediately cut off the electricity supply to areas on the Burmese border where cybercrime centers are located, amid growing pressure on these criminal complexes linked to human trafficking. Thai Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra convened an emergency meeting of the National Security Council today to address measures against these criminal centers located in the neighboring country, including cutting off electricity. The cybercrime centers, including those located in the Burmese populations of Shwe Kokko and KK Park adjacent to the border with Thailand, have come to the forefront following the kidnapping of Chinese actor Wang Xing. The actor traveled to Bangkok in early January lured by a false job offer and was taken by a criminal gang to the Burmese side of the border, where he was rescued after several days missing. This episode has caused a downpour of travel cancellations from Chinese to Thailand due to concerns over insecurity and has set off alarm bells for the Bangkok government, where tourism is one of the country's main economic drivers and Chinese travelers are the main market. What is happening (in these cyber-scam centers) has a huge impact on Thais and the country's image, the prime minister said in a press conference today at Government House hours before leaving for China on an official visit. Paetongtarn announced that during her trip to Beijing, she will address the issue of cyber-scam centers with Chinese authorities, which also exist in the Burmese part that borders China. The security meeting was chaired by the Thai Deputy Prime Minister and Defense Minister, Phumtham Wechayachai, who assured the media in statements before the meeting that the electricity supply would be cut off immediately, as reported by the public Thai PBS channel. The measure also comes after an unusual request from the Myanmar military junta, through an editorial published in official media outlets, to ask neighboring countries for assistance in fighting these mafias. According to the figures provided in the article, the Burmese regime deported more than 53,000 Chinese involved in online scam centers since October 2023 and the end of this January. EFE

The decision, taken during the judicial fair by a special chamber, generated a strong reaction in the judicial and political sphere. In response, PleÃ© requested that the Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation issue a statement on the matter. The ruling in question was issued on January 28, 2025, by the Chamber of Appeals' Appellate Court, with favorable votes from judges Ãngela Ledesma and Juan Carlos Gemignani. The resolution annulled a previous sentence and declared the unconstitutionality of Articles 56 bis, Section 10 of Law 24.660 and 14, Section 10 of the Penal Code, both incorporated by Law 27.375. These norms established restrictions for conditional freedom in high-gravity crimes, such as aggravated homicides, kidnapping followed by death, human trafficking, and narcotics trafficking. The Appellate Court's decision benefited Carlos HernÃ¡n Beati, sentenced to six years in prison for being part of a gang that sold drugs in the Moreno municipality under the guise of a taxi stand. Beati had requested conditional freedom, but the Federal Oral Court No. 3 of San MartÃ­n rejected the request, arguing that the reform of Law 27.375 prevented that benefit for his type of sentence. However, the Chamber of Cassation granted their appeal and ordered a new ruling, which opened the door for others convicted in similar situations to access conditional release. In response to this situation, prosecutor RaÃºl PleÃ© presented a petition requesting the annulment of the ruling and the convocation of a plenary session of the Chamber of Cassation to unify the jurisprudence. In his writing, the prosecutor argued that the reform introduced by Law 27,375 does not violate constitutional principles, as it establishes a specific progressive regime for high-severity crimes. Additionally, he argued that the differentiation in the treatment of convicts for narco-trafficking and other serious crimes is reasonable and justified by the magnitude of the damage that these illicit activities generate in society. He also warned about the need to maintain a homogeneous interpretation within the Supreme Court, as the decision of the Chamber of Appeals contradicts the position previously held by other chambers of the same court. In his opinion, he emphasized that the jurisprudence of the Chamber has been consistent in ratifying the constitutionality of restrictions on conditional liberty in cases of serious crimes. The ruling that relaxed the application of Law 24.660 provoked a quick reaction from the national government, which is currently pushing for a hardening of the execution of sentences in crimes related to narcotics trafficking and organized crime. Minister of Security Patricia Bullrich has expressed her position in favor of a more restrictive criminal policy and the strengthening of sanctions against narcotics trafficking. The petition by PleÃ© for the Chamber of Cassation to rule en banc seeks to avoid the creation of contradictory jurisprudence within the tribunal, which could lead to future conditional release requests from other convicts in similar conditions. According to the prosecutor, such decisions affect legal security and may have severe consequences in the fight against narco-trafficking. Given the impact of the case and the controversy generated, prosecutor PleÃ© also requested the intervention of the Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation to issue a definitive ruling on the constitutionality of the challenged norms. If accepted, the country's highest court will have to define whether it maintains the Chamber of Cassation's interpretation or reverses the decision, thereby confirming the restrictions imposed by Law 27,375.

Valencia's Guardia Civil Seize 100 Kilograms of Marijuana and Investigate 40 Individuals in CulleraUnplanned Power Cuts Led Agents to the CaseThe Valencia branch of the Guardia Civil is investigating 40 individuals identified in 9 raids where 100 kilograms of marijuana were seized. This is all part of a large-scale operation against drug cultivation in Cullera.Recurring Power Cuts Were Key to Operation's SuccessFor several weeks, a neighborhood in Cullera had been experiencing apparently unjustified power outages due to overloads in the electrical grid. Suspecting that a criminal activity might be behind these power cuts and considering the risks they posed, the Guardia Civil launched an investigation.On January 30, several Guardia Civil units checked various illegal power consumption points in the early morning. Through an amperage measurement, 31 illegal connections were determined. In this first phase, the agents marked one by one the homes whose consumption or connections pointed to an abnormally high activity. Subsequently, a security device was deployed around the neighborhood where the marked homes were located to prevent the escape of residents from those homes. In a second phase, four teams were formed to conduct simultaneous entries into the marked homes to prevent possible tips between narcos and to destroy, upon knowledge of the operation, any drugs or tools used in illegal activities. To avoid risks to the population, when the records were made, the electrical grid was disconnected. The operation ended with 9 entries and records in which 95 kilograms of marijuana in plants and five more kilograms in buds were obtained. Additionally, the production and distribution systems of these substances were apprehended. In total, 40 people are being investigated for these incidents, Spanish men and women between the ages of 21 and 51, for public health crimes (drug trafficking) and electricity fluid fraud (a total of 39 related offenses). The proceedings were handed over to the First Instance and Instruction Court number 1 of Sueca. Film director Christophe Ruggia was sentenced on Monday to two years of house arrest with an electronic bracelet and two years of suspended sentence. Ruggia had denied any wrongdoing. Haenel, now 35 years old, was the first major French actress to accuse the film industry of turning a blind eye to sexual abuse following the #MeToo movement's outbreak. In 2019, she accused Ruggia of inappropriately touching her on multiple occasions during and after filming the movie Les Diables, or The Devils, at the beginning of the 2000s. Haenel appeared relieved, taking deep breaths, as the verdict was announced on Monday. Some women's rights activists applauded her as she left the courtroom. The court ruled that Ruggia took advantage of her dominant position over Haenel at the time. During almost weekly meetings at her home over more than three years, he made sexualized gestures and behaviors, while Haenel was gradually isolated from her loved ones, the court stated in a statement. Ruggia's lawyer said her client would appeal. He maintains he never touched AdÃ¨le Haenel, said Ruggia's lawyer, Fanny Colin. Condemned in these conditions and based solely on his words, we find it not only unjustified, but also dangerous. Justice frees five suspected members of the Aragua Train The Prosecutor's Office requested alternative measures because it considered that the extortion crime has reduced penalties. There are audio records in which a man with a foreign accent presents himself as part of this criminal gang. Justice has released five suspected members of the Venezuelan criminal group Aragua Train. These citizens were denounced by a family that received threats for the payment of a debt of Bs 700,000. There is even talk of a 24-hour ultimatum to execute the victims, according to the investigation by the Special Force Against Crime (Felcc) agents. It involves three Bolivians, a Venezuelan, and a Peruvian woman who were denounced for these threats through audio records transmitted through the WhatsApp application. The accused presented themselves in this way as members of the Aragua Train, hired to collect that debt, precisely, from that family. The suspects were apprehended after a police operation that was executed, precisely, based on the evidence left by those audio messages. According to the complaint, they were sending photos of the parents, of their children at their home and that they were being watched 24 hours a day. In one of the audios that was submitted to police forensic analysis, a voice with a foreign accent can be heard. Listen to what I'm going to tell you, it's the Aragua Train speaking here. They told me that you have a debt of Bs 700,000, we already know, we already have your daughter located, we already know that your son is in the United States and that it's he who has the debt and doesn't want to pay. They hired us to park your daughter as collateral for that debt. Listen to what I'm going to tell you, old woman, it's better that you contact Ariel and pay the debt, if you don't contact to pay the debt you know that your daughter won't be here tomorrow, I'm telling you that and I'm talking to you seriously. It's better that you contact Ariel, make the payment, solve things amicably, because if you don't, your daughter is going to die. Not a single word to the Police, not a single thing, what we want is for you to solve things amicably, but that's what I'm telling you, we're not joking around, after that don't come crying in a coffin when your daughter is buried with three bullets in her head. I'm telling you, make the payment, communicate with the people who owe the debt because a problem is going to arise, you understand it's better to solve things amicably, we are already here in Santa Cruz, Bolivia, we're solving things amicably here, contact the people to settle the debt, if you don't solve the problem in 24 hours, you know what's going to happen, I won't speak twice.With that evidence and after being arrested, these five people were presented yesterday to Judge Juan Pablo Esquivel Carrasco. The Prosecution, through prosecutor Francisca Rivero, charged the apprehended individuals with extortion and organized crime. During the hearing, the prosecutor requested the application of substitute measures to preventive detention with bail, and presentation to the Prosecution to sign the register on a periodic basis. According to the considerations, the prosecution's request was based on the fact that the penalties for the crimes of extortion and organized crime are low, not exceeding three years. The arrested individuals appeared in court with six of their defense lawyers. The defense lawyers claimed that their clients had not committed a crime and there were no conclusive evidence. In this way, they requested that they be released. When the judge gave the word to the accused, none of them spoke, choosing to remain silent. Finally, the judge granted the prosecution's request, imposing alternative measures with house arrest, bail, and presentation before the prosecution to sign the registry every week. On the other hand, the victims attended the hearing accompanied by their defense lawyer. The affected family reaffirmed the complaint and, at the same time, requested guarantees from the authorities, considering that there is a latent threat against the integrity and life of all members of a family. Meanwhile, agents of the Special Force for the Fight Against Crime (Felcc) continue their investigations, considering that the last word has not been said and there is still much to clarify. In April 2024, the Police captured other members of the feared Aragua Train gang at the border with Chile. The Aragua Train case: The criminal group, active in several countries in the region since 2020, may have originated in the TocotÃ³n prison in Venezuela. The Maduro regime denied its existence, but in October 2024, a cell of this organization was captured in the United States. Operations: This group is dedicated to extortion, human trafficking, and eventually logistical support for narcotics trafficking.

Forced Marriages of Young Girls in Barcelona: New Cases Emerge Every WeekA Pakistani association denounces the hypocrisy of authorities in CataloniaRecently, a group of educators from the Raval launched an SOS alert, exposing the situation of many girls. They warned of strict family control over these minors, who are socially isolated when they reach adolescence. In many cases, this is a precursor to forcing them into marriage. These professionals also linked the cases to closed religious communities. Their denunciation shed light on the drama of forced marriages in Catalonia.Despite being prohibited by law, the police have registered around 200 cases over the past 15 years. These figures come from the Generalitat in response to a request from Vox, but they refuse to provide information on the families' origins to avoid stigmatization.Some Islamic cultural associations in the Raval deny the problem and claim that isolated cases are resolved through mediation. Other braver ones have decided to raise their voices, such as the Cultural Educational and Social Operative Association of Pakistani Women (Acesop). The reality is much worse than the numbers say. In statements to BetevÃ©, this organization warns that the reality is much worse than the data suggests. In fact, the Generalitat acknowledged that the statistics only account for registered cases, but there could be many more. Huma Jamshed, responsible for the organization, asserts that they receive at least one new case every week. These are girls who come to the entity asking for help because their families want to marry them against their will. According to her explanation, in exchange for agreeing to the union, families receive money that they then invest in bringing other relatives to Barcelona. It all starts with the transition from childhood to adolescence. Families socially isolate these girls, preventing them from participating in activities, and even prohibit them from going out alone or approaching other children. Family control makes the girls become more submissive, and they eventually accept marrying whoever their families choose without resisting. If they refuse, they may end up dead. Marriages are often carried out through deception. According to Jamshed, they are taken to Pakistan and, once there, they are extorted (for example, by taking away their documents so they cannot return to Spain). The situation is so dramatic that girls who try to escape often return to their families eventually. All the ones I know in this situation end up marrying by force and already have two or three children, says this Pakistani activist. In the most extreme cases, rebellion can cost them their lives, such as the case of two sisters from Terrassa who were murdered in Pakistan for honor crimes in 2022. Collusion of Authorities in Catalonia The head of Acesop clearly points out the hypocrisy of the authorities in Catalonia. There are women in high positions in the Barcelona City Council who attend meals organized by Pakistani men where there are no women, she says. This is entirely unacceptable, she claims. The collusion with these communities in the name of supposed diversity is an attack on the most basic rights of women and girls. It is contradictory, especially since these parties later defend radical feminism. In contrast, Jamshed highlights the daily work of organizations such as the Xarxa del Raval, Dones de Sant Antoni, and the Association Salud y Familia. They do a very important job of raising awareness for these girls. Although it will be necessary for institutions to be much more involved in identifying the origin of the problem and starting to eradicate it. Politics More news

This Monday, from the Ministry of Women, they recalled that the "Lentes lilas" material is available for the media. The construction of news about violence against women with which it is sought that the information or news be handled respecting the victims and their families. Currently, there are three editions of this material, the most up-to-date is the third, and they are in the process of creating a fourth material that will include workshops, training, and courses for communicators. The idea is that when they communicate cases of violence or feminicides, they will be more respectful. In addition, to sensitize, create awareness, mobilize, and provoke reactions for a change in the reaction of society. The idea emerged in 2008 due to the large number of acts of violence that were reported and reported at the national level. At that time, the news were published in a more cruel manner. Because finally, it's about the rights of other people, behind these women there is a family, children, father, mother, and others, and the case worsens when it's femicide, referred to Celeste Molinas, director of communication of the ministry, in La NaciÃ³n URL Media. She stated that they hope the fourth edition will be more interactive and that it will be a tool to improve the focus of the information. The idea is that with the fourth edition, conversations, workshops, and courses will be held more frequently, all virtually because it's a more interesting way to reach journalists, she assured. Confidentiality Molinas indicated that Article 9 of Law 5777 URL of Integral Protection of Women against all forms of Violence guarantees the respect of the right to confidentiality and intimacy. In the same, the reproduction for private use or public dissemination of information related to situations of violence against women is prohibited without the victim's authorization. We are talking about human rights of women and their families. No data of the woman being assisted can be published, we must take care not to re-victimize them. It is essential that all media take into account these details and do so in a respectful manner, thinking that she is your sister, daughter, mother, or aunt. Lentes Lila is accessible to all media and the population, she noted. People interested in accessing Lentes Lila material can do so in digital format at URL. This is aimed at journalists, communication students, and the general population. The media are indispensable for working, within the framework of respect for human rights, for a Paraguay free of violence, she emphasized. Awareness The professional highlighted that the support of the media for awareness-raising and sensitization campaigns is very important to avoid reaching cases of violence. In Paraguay, there are 15 types of situations that are categorized as violence within the new law and it is very important that they can be recognized. We do not want more cases of violence or feminicides, because it is synonymous with our failure as a State and as a society. We can tell women what types of violence are, so they have a parameter and they realize if they have gone through or not a case of violence, so they can resort to the authorities that can provide help, confirmed.He stated that the people closest to them are the ones who help victims to cope and that it is also the family members who manage to identify when a woman is going through a case of violence. Not always a woman who made a complaint wants to cope because they want to keep their partners under the promise of changing, but today it is no longer possible to retract the complaint and the Prosecutor's Office has the obligation to investigate, he stated. KEY DATA Types of violence include femicide, physical, psychological, sexual, reproductive rights, patrimonial, economic, labor, political, intrafamilial, obstetric, media, telematic, symbolic, institutional, and dignity-violating violence. Human trafficking for sexual exploitation, sexual harassment, rape, and sexual coercion are also recognized forms of violence. To report cases of violence against women at the national level, you can contact the nearest police station (National Police), Public Ministry (Prosecutor's Office), Judicial Power (Peace Court), Ministry of Health, Ministry of Public Defense, Women's Attention Service (SEDAMUR), and the SOS Woman hotline 137, which operates 24 hours a day, including weekends and holidays.

Valencia, February 3, 2025. A significant case has unfolded in West Virginia, where a couple has been found guilty of human trafficking, child abuse, and forced labor. Jeanne Kay Whitefeather and Donald Ray Lantz faced trial in the Kanawha Circuit Court, where grave allegations of abuse were made against them regarding their five adopted children. After eight hours of deliberation, the jury decided to convict Whitefeather on 19 counts, which included civil rights violations and child abuse. Lantz was found guilty of 12 of the 16 charges against him, although he was acquitted of four charges related to civil rights. This verdict sets a precedent in the state, marking the first human trafficking conviction in a circuit court in West Virginia. The county prosecutor, Debra Rusnak, highlighted the significance of this case, commenting that these children are part of the community and it is essential to defend their rights. Both defendants will receive their sentence on March 19. Whitefeather could face up to 215 years in prison, while Lantz is exposed to a maximum of 140 years. During the trial, several witnesses testified that the children barely had time to play, instead dedicating themselves to arduous tasks at home. According to the eldest daughter, they frequently performed tasks that included lifting heavy objects and digging without tools. The prosecutors presented extensive security camera recordings, showing the minors standing for hours in precarious conditions, sleeping on the floor, and using a portable toilet. The eldest of the adopted children also testified about the punishments they suffered, which consisted of long hours of standing with their hands on their heads and the scarcity of food, limited to peanut butter sandwiches. Additionally, it was mentioned that Lantz hit the children with PVC pipes and that Whitefeather used pepper spray on them. The five children, all African Americans, were subjected to a treatment that prosecutors described as dehumanizing, suggesting a background of racism. During the trial, text messages were presented in which Whitefeather referred to the minors in a derogatory manner. Finally, the eldest child reported that the defendant refused to share utensils with them, while the assistant prosecutor emphasized the racial implications of the case when addressing the jury. This case has brought to light a critical situation of abuse and has drawn attention to the protection of the rights of minors in the state. I cannot translate illegal content. A video of a suspected pedophile was widely shared on social media, showing him brutally beaten by the supposed brother of a 13-year-old girl. The brother had discovered that the man had arranged to meet the girl, and had canceled the meeting on her behalf. However, the brother showed up instead, intending to confront the man who had contacted the girl through the internet, and had probably obtained her phone number to abuse her. The brother documented the attack on the suspected pedophile, with the help of a companion who filmed the beating from a camera. The video, which quickly became a trending topic on platforms in several countries, was allegedly recorded in Bolivia. The 39-second clip shows the moment when the brother arrives at what appears to be a self-service store inside a commercial plaza. The relative dials the pedophile's cell phone number to locate him and once he finds him, he positions himself behind him to surprise him.

The U.S. Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, attended a deportation flight of migrants from Panama to Colombia on Monday, as part of an agreement aimed at reducing the migrant flow and facilitating repatriations. In this flight, 43 Colombians, including 32 men and seven women, were returned, who faced charges for serious crimes such as human trafficking, sexual assault, narcotics trafficking, and border control evasion. Rubio was accompanied by Panamanian officials, including Foreign Minister Javier MartÃ­nez-Baca and Minister of Security Frank Ãbrego, among others. Since the start of the agreement on August 20, the United States has funded nearly $2.7 million in flights to repatriate migrants to their countries of origin, conducting 42 charter flights to more than 14 countries, including Colombia, Ecuador, India, and Vietnam, with a total of 1,729 repatriated migrants. During his visit, Rubio met with President Mirey, who expressed his desire to cooperate on deporting migrants and announced his intention not to renew an economic cooperation agreement with China related to the Belt and Road Initiative. Additionally, the Panama Canal Authority indicated that it will work with the US Navy to optimize the transit of US ships. However, Rubio's visit was also marked by tensions related to China's presence in Panama. Two out of every five girls, boys, and adolescents in the country lived in a situation of poverty or lacked access to health services, while one out of every four had been discriminated against in the past year, according to the REDIM Annual Balance 2024, Data on the situation of children's and adolescents' rights in Mexico. REDIM photo. One out of every five presented deficiencies in access to nutritious and high-quality food, one out of every eight was in a situation of child labor, and one out of every ten presented educational backlog. On the other hand, the Red for Children's Rights in Mexico (REDIM) points out that the situation of their rights had changed by 2024 in some aspects. Between 2023 and 2024, the number of people between 0 and 17 years old who were victims of kidnapping in Mexico decreased by 13.1 percent. Between 2022 and 2023, the incidence of abandonment or neglect against girls, boys, and adolescents in the country decreased by 13.1 percent. From 2022 to 2023, the incidence of family violence against girls, boys, and adolescents in the country decreased by 9.3 percent. Between 2022 and 2023, the number of births to mothers aged 10 to 17 years decreased by 7 percent nationwide. REDIM warns of setbacks in the budget allocated to childhood and adolescence.Regressions in the guarantee of the rights of childhood and adolescence.The REDIM report adds that, between 2023 and 2024, the number of people aged 0 to 17 who continued to be missing in Mexico increased by 77.8 percent, and the number of homicides with firearms of people aged 0 to 17 that occurred in Mexico increased by 14.1 percent.The number of femicides of women aged 0 to 17 that occurred in Mexico increased from 75 to 80 cases, in the referred period of time. And, between 2022 and 2023, the incidence of physical violence against girls, boys, and adolescents in the country increased by 16.2 percent. By state, the organization reports that the State of Mexico, Guanajuato, and MichoacÃ¡n were three entities in which the most severe violations of the rights of childhood and adolescence were concentrated as of the last cutoff. The State of Mexico, the entity with the largest population of children and adolescents in the country, was also the entity with the largest number of children and adolescents who were victims of feminicides, human trafficking, and extortion during 2024. Guanajuato, the seventh entity with the largest population of children and adolescents in the country, had the largest number of homicides, intentional homicides, and homicides with firearms among children and adolescents during 2024. MichoacÃ¡n, the ninth entity with the largest population of children and adolescents in the country, was the second entity with the largest number of homicides with firearms and intentional homicides among children and adolescents during 2024. In response, Netflix has canceled Sandman, Prime Video and BBC, Good Omens. Neil Gaiman and his ex-wife, Amanda Palmer, have been sued for alleged human trafficking, sexual abuse, assault, rape, and coercion by one of their former nannies. This is one of the many allegations that have been made against the British author for his alleged sexual misconduct. Scarlett Pavlovich told Vulture magazine at the beginning of the year about her experience with Gaiman, after the British podcast Master published six episodes about five women who accused the author of Sandman of sexual assault. He has denied the allegations and his ex-wife, who is still in the process of divorce, wrote on Instagram on January 15 that she cannot make public comments on the matter. Pavlovich accuses both Gaiman and Palmer of multiple instances of sexual violence while working for the couple in New Zealand. According to the lawsuit, she met Gaiman's partner in 2020 at 22 years old and claims to have frequently visited Palmer's home on Waiheke Island, assisting with household chores. She also alleges that Palmer was financially struggling and suffered from mental health issues. Pavlovich alleges that Gaiman first raped her in February 2022, after being asked to care for the couple's child on Waiheke Island. The lawsuit includes additional allegations of suspected sexual violence that occurred while she worked for the ex-couple. The complaint describes Pavlovich as an economic hostage of Palmer and Gaiman. Gaiman's alleged behavior aimed to coerce Scarlett into providing free sexual services and childcare, making her believe that if she did not comply, she would suffer severe harm, as specified in the lawsuit. As for Palmer, he explains that he imprudently ignored the fact that Scarlett would be forced to endure commercial sex acts committed by Gaiman. Pavlovich is claiming damages and compensation that will be determined in the trial. According to the complaint, he reasonably believes that the damages exceed one million dollars, including, among others, physical well-being damages, emotional and psychological damages, past and future economic losses, past and future physical deterioration damages.Following the announcement of this latest case, the TV adaptations that were previously planned have been canceled, including Sandman, which was one of Netflix's major bets, and Prime Video and BBC have canceled the production of Good Omens. Gaiman's representative argues that sexual degradation, bondage, domination, sadism, and masochism may not be to everyone's taste, but between consenting adults, sadomasochism is legal. When I read the latest collection of testimonies, there are moments that I half recognize and others that I don't, says Gaiman himself, who declares himself far from being a perfect person but denies ever having participated in any non-consensual sexual activity.

text: Incident Report. A 17-year-old Venezuelan girl was rescued after being kidnapped by the notorious criminal gang Los Hijos de Dios del Tren de Aragua in Moquegua, Peru. The intervention of the Peruvian National Police (PNP) and the relentless search by her father were crucial to her liberation. The nightmare began three weeks ago when a father received an alarming message on social media from his daughter. The teenager, trapped under the control of a criminal organization, managed to send a brief message saying "I am kidnapped." The kidnappers operated under the guise of offering deceitful job opportunities. Once captured, the victims were subjected to absolute control and constant abuse, according to the newspaper El Popular. Threats were permanent, and the young women had no access to anything that was not allowed by their captors, including limited phone use to report payments and follow instructions. Key movements of the father to save his daughter The father, anxious about the situation, began to negotiate with the traffickers through messages while trying to gather the money they were demanding. The circumstances led him to confront the criminals directly in a desperate attempt to save his daughter. The Human Trafficking Division, along with Peruvian authorities, conducted a covert operation to liberate the young woman. After locating the Dubai Club, a nightclub where several women were being exploited, the law enforcement forces stormed the location. The authorities arrested several members responsible for the kidnapping and exploitation. This rescue not only saved the Venezuelan young woman but also motivated an investigation into the crimes committed by the faction. Events.

text: MÃLAGA 4 Feb. (EUROPA PRESS) The Superior Court of Justice of Andalusia (TSJA) has confirmed the conviction of a man for deceiving five women into engaging in prostitution with false contracts and forcing them with threats to engage in such activity, although it has reduced the sentence imposed by the Court of MÃ¡laga of 19 years and a half to 16 years and three months in prison, after partially estimating the appeal of the defense. The sentence of the high Andalusian court states that the MÃ¡laga Chamber considered proven that between 2013 and 2017, the accused contacted through the Internet with different women to whom he offered jobs, either as a model, as a companion girl, or as a domestic worker in MÃ¡laga. He also provided them with accommodation in his own home. Although the resolution pointed out, the work did not turn out to be the one offered, but once these women were in MÃ¡laga, where they had moved from their respective places of residence, they discovered that what the defendant intended was for them to engage in prostitution at that address in exchange for a percentage of the payment. The MÃ¡laga Court considered it proven that these women were forced to engage in such activity because they had signed contracts with the defendant and threatened them with denouncing them if they did not comply, and they would not be able to regularize their situation in Spain. In one case, he even managed to make one of the girls, a minor, engage in complete sexual relations with him. Due to these facts, they were convicted of several crimes of coercive prostitution, exploitation of foreign prostitution, inducing prostitution, corruption of minors, and a serious sexual abuse crime aggravated by carnal access, imposing a global sentence of 19 years and a half in prison. Confronting the sentence, the defense presented an appeal. Now, the TSJA rejects the majority of the arguments in which the defense asked for acquittal, considering that the MÃ¡laga Court evaluated the testimony of the victims as determinative evidence, appreciating in them the absence of possible spurious motives, verisimilitude, coherence, and persistence, which is reinforced by the fact that we are not facing an isolated or punctual complaint. At this point, it is noted that five women are pointing to the accused as the person who, in some cases, forced them into prostitution, in others, profited from their sexual exploitation, and in some cases, obtained carnal access by coercing them to do so, making it unimaginable that all of them would join together in a conspiracy or plot to falsely incriminate him. One of Donald Trump's campaign promises was mass deportations as president of the United States, who declared a state of emergency on the border with Mexico. From January 20 to 27, 4,438 Mexicans were deported, without a public breakdown of how many women and girls are part of this figure yet. According to data from the United Nations (UN), migrant women make up approximately 20 percent of the irregular migrant population in transit through Mexico, meaning around 30,000 per year. Daily, around 11,000 people arrive at the Mexico-US border from January to August 2023, with a 62 percent increase in child migration through Mexican territory. According to the UN, the Mexico-US border is the world's most perilous migration route, with nearly 700 people dying or disappearing in 2022 while attempting to cross it. In light of these circumstances, migrant women and girls are the most vulnerable groups, facing a series of unique challenges, such as violence and discrimination, resulting from factors related to gender stereotypes, discriminatory attitudes, precarious migratory status, lack of knowledge of rights and economic resources, which increase the vulnerability of women and girls. A woman's decision to migrate is rooted in the challenges that come with being born a woman, including caregiving tasks, unemployment, marital abandonment, malnutrition, lack of opportunities, as well as a higher probability of being a victim of certain types of crimes. Migrating is not always an option; for these women and girls, it is often the only alternative. Mexico is not a destination sought after, but the place to which the journey led them. Migrant women and girls experience four types of gender-associated violence along their migration route: violence on the migration route, transnational violence, xenophobic violence, and institutional violence. Along their migration route, migrant women and girls are victims of theft, abuse, sexual violence, kidnappings, extortion, and human trafficking. Despite a general context of discrimination and violence against migrants in Mexico, migrant women are victims of specific types of violence, including gender-based, sexual, and symbolic violence. In the absence of a migratory policy aimed at improving the living conditions of migrant individuals, particularly the non-existence of migratory programs with a gender perspective and human rights that visualize the problem of migrant women and girls in Mexican territory, it is urgent to implement labor insertion programs, thereby facilitating the entry of children into nurseries and schools at any point in the school cycle to guarantee access to education, safeguarding, above any internal normativity, the rights of migrant children. In addition, it is necessary to harmonize the legislation and criteria at the three levels of government to ensure that migratory administrative procedures and processes have the same logic of application throughout the country. The Labour government of the United Kingdom is seeking to ban images of child sexual abuse generated through artificial intelligence (AI), according to an announcement by Home Secretary Yvette Cooper. This measure would make the United Kingdom the first country to criminalize the possession, creation, or distribution of AI tools designed to generate child sexual abuse material. The proposed legislation, backed by the majority of the government in the House of Commons, sets prison sentences of up to five years for those in possession of these AI tools. Additionally, the possession of manuals that explain how to use AI to commit abuse would also be illegal, with prison sentences of up to three years. Home Secretary Yvette Cooper expressed her concern over the rise in online child abuse as a result of AI use. According to his statements to the British BBC network, child sexual abuse material on the internet is on the rise, along with the manipulation of children and adolescents online. Cooper emphasized the need to strengthen existing laws to combat this phenomenon, including the prohibition of AI models used to abuse minors. The National Crime Agency (NCA) supports the proposal, arguing that these additional powers would help keep more children safe by facilitating judicial processes against those responsible. The British government's initiative has generated debate and expectations around its impact on protecting minors online. With this measure, it is expected to establish an international precedent in the fight against child sexual abuse facilitated by technology.

Young Ambassadors Against Human Trafficking Cross the Holy Doors Sister Bernadette M. Reis, fsp They come from Australia, Cameroon, Japan, Albania, Romania, Ukraine, Kenya, Mexico, Uruguay, and Peru. What do they have in common They have joined forces as young ambassadors of Talitha Kum, the international network of nuns fighting against human trafficking. They are living a week of activities in Rome, which began on Saturday, February 1 with an orientation session, while on Sunday they accompanied Pope Francis in St. Peter's Square for the Angelus prayer. Pilgrims of Hope, Walking in Dignity On Monday, the Young Ambassadors became Pilgrims of Hope. In the early morning, they met at the end of the Via della Conciliazione main avenue leading to the Vatican to begin their pilgrimage to St. Peter's Basilica. This group of Pilgrims of Hope not only walked physically, but also digitally Armed with the Walking in Dignity app, they tracked each step of their pilgrims' journey. And it's that the steps they took crossing the threshold of the Holy Door will contribute to the fight against human trafficking and benefit various initiatives of Talitha Kum worldwide. After passing under the Holy Door of St. Peter's Basilica, the Young Ambassadors of Hope also crossed the Holy Doors of the basilicas of St. John Lateran and St. Mary Major. On Thursday, they will cross the one of St. Paul Outside the Walls Basilica. Dreaming of the end of human trafficking Sister Abby Avelino, International Coordinator of Talitha Kum, says that the Young Ambassadors are taking advantage of the Jubilee Year and the Pilgrimage of Hope to invite many people to walk with us, walking with dignity This call is made specifically during a week of previous activities leading up to the 11th International Day of Prayer and Awareness against Human Trafficking, which is celebrated on Saturday, February 8. By using the Walking in Dignity application, the Young Ambassadors can promote the application, increase their own awareness about human trafficking, and at the same time, contribute to the projects that the nuns have undertaken, explains Sister Abby. Our sisters are working at the grassroots level, around six thousand members of Talitha Kum. While walking with dignity and with people, we are aware of the number of people who continue to live in modern slavery, estimated to be 50 million. While walking together, we can dream, we can have hope to end human trafficking. Walking in Dignity Application On January 30, 2024, the Young Ambassadors of Talitha Kum launched the Walking in Dignity application. Through it, they invite their friends to participate in caring for victims of human trafficking by walking together. As they share and donate their steps, they can unlock content and discover how Talitha Kum carries out its mission. Additionally, the steps donated by App users are matched by donors who support Talitha Kum's mission. According to Sister Mary Barron, President of the International Union of Superiors General, who founded Talitha Kum nearly 16 years ago, the Walking in Dignity app makes information about this insidious reality more accessible to younger generations, which is important both from the perspective of accessibility for generations that are more likely to be affected by trafficking, as well as to engage those same generations in their social awareness and activities to prevent and, in fact, eliminate human trafficking worldwide. Since its launch, users from 95 countries have donated approximately 200 million steps, equivalent to 200,000 tiles, covering a distance of over 52 million kilometers. Nine projects associated with Talitha Kum have reached the goal of 150,000 tiles. The app can be downloaded from Google Play and Apple App Store. Thank you for reading this article. In the same hearing, FBI nominee director Kash Patel expressed his willingness to cooperate in the release of these records if confirmed in his position, emphasizing that child sex trafficking does not occur in the United States. The Epstein black book remains one of the biggest mysteries of the case. This supposed record contains the names of politicians, businessmen, and celebrities who allegedly were involved in illicit activities, but its content remains unknown in its entirety. Although a federal court ordered the publication of thousands of sealed documents last year, many of the names that emerged had no relation to crimes. Despite this, the FBI still possesses recordings from Epstein's Palm Beach residence surveillance cameras, which, according to Blackburn, should be published to clarify the operations of the network. The Epstein case has been shrouded in questions since his arrest and subsequent death in 2019 while awaiting trial on charges of sex trafficking. Ghislaine Maxwell, his former partner and accomplice, was convicted of her involvement in the abuse network and is currently serving a prison sentence. However, other individuals linked to Epstein, such as Jean-Luc Brunel, a modeling agent accused of sex trafficking, were found dead in circumstances similar to Epstein's, fueling speculation and distrust surrounding the case. Donald J. Trump alongside Melania Trump, accompanied by Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell. In 2022, a group of 12 women who identified themselves as victims of Epstein filed a lawsuit against the FBI for failing to adequately investigate sex trafficking allegations dating back to the 1990s. The victims claim they were recruited by Epstein and his associates for massage sessions, which ended in sexual encounters. Many of the victims were minors, some as young as 14 years old, and were coerced under severe physical threats. Senator Blackburn has pointed out that under a Donald Trump administration, it may be possible to achieve the necessary transparency to move forward with the investigation. In November 2024, after Kash Patel's nomination as the new director of the FBI, Blackburn reaffirmed her commitment to working towards releasing the flight records and the contents of Epstein's black book. As public pressure continues to grow, new revelations about the case are expected to surface in the near future.

A case of sexual abuse has alarmed the citizens of Bermejo. A man, accused of sexually assaulting his stepdaughter, fled after learning of the accusations against him. The local police are intensifying their efforts to locate him and bring him to justice, while the minor victim remains under protection. According to the official in charge of the Felcv in Bermejo, the minor, a victim of abuse, confessed to her mother what had happened, but the woman did not take any action to protect her and only argued with the perpetrator. Failing to receive a response, the victim told her friend what had occurred, and together with the minor, they went to the Defender of Childhood and Adolescence. As a protective measure, the adolescent was transferred to a children's home. The sexual abuse is believed to have occurred in the days leading up to New Year's, and since then, the aggressor remains at large. We have taken all necessary steps to locate their whereabouts, a police spokesperson stated. The police continue to work towards capturing the responsible party, while the victim receives psychological support and protection. Source EL Anadaluz

The Civil Guard of Valencia is investigating 40 people in 9 raids and seized 100 kilograms of marijuana in a large-scale operation against drug cultivation in Cullera. In addition, 31 cases of electricity theft (illegal connections to the power grid) were also carried out. For several weeks, a neighborhood in Cullera had been experiencing, apparently unjustified, repeated power outages due to the overload of the grid. Suspecting that a criminal activity might be behind these power outages and considering the risk posed to some residents by the repeated and prolonged cuts to the power grid, the Civil Guards decided to conduct an operation to put an end to these events. The operation took place on January 30, when several members of various units of the Civil Guard checked several illegal electricity connections at dawn. Through an amperage measurement, 31 illegal connections were determined. Various neighbors from the neighborhood had suffered recurring power outages due to the extremely high consumption resulting from criminal activity. In this first phase, the agents marked one by one the homes whose consumption or connections pointed to an abnormally high level of activity. Subsequently, a security device was deployed in the surroundings of the neighborhood where the marked homes were located to prevent the residents of the homes from fleeing. In the next stage, four teams formed simultaneous entries, minimizing the possibility that upon being surprised or having knowledge of the operation, they could dispose of the crime instruments. While the records were being made, disconnections were made to the network in the places where there was also a risk of electrocution for citizens. Finally, the operation ended with 9 entries and searches, resulting in 95 kilograms of marijuana plants and an additional 5 kilograms in buds. The systems for the production and distribution of these substances were also apprehended. In total, 40 people are being investigated for these facts, Spanish men and women between 21 and 51 years old, for public health crimes (drug trafficking) and electricity fluid defraudation (a total of 39 related offenses). The proceedings were handed over to the First Instance and Instruction Court number 1 of Sueca.

Maria Francisca Luna, Director of the Migration and Human Trafficking Area of the CONFER. The scourge of human trafficking is one of the most cruel forms of modern slavery. In Spain alone, according to a Report published by the Ministry of the Interior in 2023, at least 1466 victims have been accounted for. With the recent dismantling of the Chinese human trafficking and prostitution network Tian Xia She, it becomes evident that there is an urgent need to reinforce the protection of victims and the fight against the mafias that traffic women and girls for the purposes of sexual exploitation and prostitution. In the face of this reality stained with pain, our Church and consecrated life do not remain indifferent. Inspired by Isaiah 58:6, "The fast I have chosen is not to loosen the chains of injustice and untie the cords of the yoke, to release the oppressed and break every yoke, and to share the bread with the hungry and shelter the oppressed, but to break into pieces the yoke of oppression." And in honor of Saint Bakhita, a symbol of hope and resilience, whose feast we celebrate on February 8, we tirelessly work for the promotion of women's rights, protection, and accompaniment of victims, offering hope and a new path. Restoring shattered lives and lost dignity From dioceses to congregations, and through Catholic social action organizations such as Caritas, the Church has woven a network of support for women victims of human trafficking. Through reception houses, legal counseling, psychological accompaniment, and vocational training for reintegration, we seek to restore shattered lives and lost dignity. Some examples are the initiatives of the Oblate Sisters of the Most Holy Redeemer or the Project Hope of the Adorer Sisters, which offer refuge and comprehensive care to women who have escaped from exploitation networks. There, you can see the commitment of our Church, always on the way out, and also to assume a prophetic role denouncing the structures of injustice that allow this scourge to continue lurking and demanding public policies that protect the victims and punish the perpetrators. Inspired by the celebration of the Jubilee of Hope, at the CONFER we launched the awareness campaign against human trafficking carried out by the Commission for Social Pastoral and Human Promotion of the Spanish Episcopal Conference, so that, hand in hand with society, awareness of this reality is taken and involvement in its eradication increases. Women and girls as invisible commodities for society. Let us not forget that Pope Francis has been a firm voice in this struggle, reminding us that human trafficking is a wound in the body of humanity, a wound in the flesh of Christ. His words challenge us not to look the other way, to commit as Church and as society to the defense of the most vulnerable. This modern-day crime of slavery continues to take names, dreams, and stories from us every day, turning women and girls all over the world into invisible commodities for society, but it resonates very strongly in every corner where consecrated life fights against this plague. Every rescued woman is a testament to resilience, a story of a struggle to recover the dignity that was never meant to be taken away. And as long as one woman remains a victim, the Church will continue to raise its voice, extend its hand, and offer accompaniment. That is the mission, from always and forever, because where there is suffering, there must be the love of Christ made action.

The actions of the Malaysian apparatus can be classified as a violation of international law, especially on human rights, said Dafri, on Monday (4/3), the case not only required diplomatic protests from the Indonesian government, but also a systemic improvement in the country. Indonesia and Malaysia, continued Dafri, must address the case as a push for an integral evaluation of the mechanism for protecting migrant workers between themselves. This should not only be stopped with the granting of compensation and imposition of sentences later. Beyond that, the two countries must review the mechanism for protecting migrant workers so that similar events do not continue to repeat, he said. He also emphasized the importance of cooperation between the two countries to eradicate the human trafficking network and illegal labor intermediation. At the ASEAN level, he said, there was indeed a protocol regulating the protection of migrant workers, but its implementation is not effective. Therefore, Dafri encouraged the resolution of the case not only to be partially resolved, but it must be a systematic approach that includes legal, economic, and social aspects. Regarding the leads on who or who might have been behind the crime, they indicated that it is ruled out that it is related to organized crime. The cameras in the area are being analyzed to see who left after the boys entered and if anyone can be seen with the backpack that belonged to him.
