The boy was talking to my niece, who is his friend, and he says to her, "I found two dead people over there." My niece went into the house and told her mom and me what the boy was saying. We ran out and asked the boy, but he couldn't speak. He couldn't say the words. I asked him to calm down and tell me, and he said, "It was a girl and a boy." The boy was tied behind his back, kneeling, and his head was on the ground. The girl couldn't be identified, but she had blonde hair, was also tied, and was all disfigured." Marina said. Meanwhile, a group of neighbors marched towards the neighborhood police station due to the death of the two teenagers. If the National Government had paid us the $700 billion last year, how many patrol cars could have been bought with that money? Ten thousand patrol cars. We have a governor who has 6,000 patrolmen, the provincial police officers have the same salaries as federal forces, each officer has their bulletproof vest, we have invested as never before. Every four hours we patrol 75% of the territory and each mayor, whether from the opposition or sympathetic to one or the other, looks at the patrolmen. There is no liberated zone, he added, in reference to the complaints from residents who claimed that Moreno was a lawless land. He also stated that the Buenos Aires governor, Axel Kicillof, is attentive to every single thing that occurs. (Axel) Kicillof represses the good Argentines who suffer from insecurity, but leaves the delinquents loose. This is Kirchnerism's guaranteeism. We do the opposite, putting criminals in prison and protecting Argentines. There is only one option in the ballot box this year to put an end to this chaos, expressed Minister CÃºneo Libarona in a message posted on his social media account.

Once in Mexico City, he applied to CBP One and got a job in a warehouse, where he's happy because, he says, no one bothers him, it's quiet, there he just organizes and ships merchandise. Occasionally, he talks to his wife about what he'll do and concludes firmly in front of the friends he met at the shelter and shares rice, beans, and tortillas with. I'm not going back to UsulÃ¡n, he suffered a lot to get here. My boss, who's Mexican, tells me that he'll fix papers here and helps me bring my family, says we'll rent something, don't worry, you're a good person, you're not talking nonsense. Suddenly, SaÃºl intervenes in the conversation, knowing about the no-return policy. He's been in Mexico for 10 months as a receptionist at a hotel owned by other Venezuelans with whom he's comfortable, except, he insists, for the salary. If you rent, the 2,100 pesos a week they pay won't be enough. All of them agreed, and he continues in his memoirs that his brother-in-law had a company with 22 employees in Caracas, where he worked until it went bankrupt due to the country's economic situation, and then he returned to his hometown, where he realized he couldn't do anything because the ones in charge there are the Caracas people, the paramilitaries. Helpless, he fled to Colombia, where he did very well as an electrician. He even bought a little house, but the inflation under President Gustavo Petro reduced the purchasing power of his salary, and it no longer made sense for him. He ran away from there towards the American dream that now seems to be slipping away from him. Thanks to God, he had some savings (money) and was able to move quickly to the city, he says the new Chilango prospect. Immigrants agree that during their journey, they whisper to each other that in Mexico City, they won't be bothered, that they won't be bothered with them, especially if they appear to be Mexicans because they blend in if they don't speak much and can thus gain the trust, if they show that they are workers.In another shelter in the capital, Casa Fuentes, a Nicaraguan woman reveals that she gained the trust of a fruit vendor at the street markets. That's how she recently hired the migrant to care for her elderly mother, who needs company. The night became long.In the kitchen of the other shelter, they realize they have to work in a few hours, there's only one sizzling pan of refried beans left on the stove, but everyone has already eaten. They say their goodbyes. Some go to the bedrooms, others step out into the patio, which is a bit cool, but it's not cold. Not bad for a winter.

A woman was detained in Ceuta for using her three daughters to traffic drugs. The detainee had drugs attached to the bodies of her three daughters, aged 17, 8, and 4 years, according to police sources. The National Police arrested a woman in Ceuta who was attempting to board a ship bound for Algeciras (CÃ¡diz) with drugs concealed in the bodies of her three daughters, aged 17, 8, and 4 years. The detainee allegedly attached the narcotic substance to the minors in order to evade security checks. According to a statement issued by the Superior Police Headquarters, the intervention took place last Sunday. During a routine inspection, agents detected irregularities when the woman attempted to cross the documentation control accompanied by her daughters, which raised suspicions. Following a more thorough search, authorities discovered that the minors had the drugs attached to their bodies. The woman was arrested immediately and protective protocols were activated to ensure the safety of the minors while the investigation continued. In total, they were carrying almost 7 kilograms of hashish. The National Police detected suspicious behavior in a woman and her three daughters when they were about to board the 11:30 ferry to Algeciras. According to the agents, the family exchanged nervous glances, which raised suspicions and led the police to transfer them to the port facilities for a more detailed inspection.During the search, the agents found a total of 6 kilograms and 600 grams of hashish hidden on the bodies of the three minors. The drug was distributed in 569 hazelnuts attached to their bodies, while the mother did not have any illicit substance on her body or among her belongings. After the discovery, the woman was arrested along with her 17-year-old eldest daughter, both accused of a presumed public health offense. As the investigation advances, authorities have activated protection protocols for the two younger girls. What penalties could the mother of the minors face? According to the Spanish Penal Code, in its article 368, drug trafficking can result in prison sentences of 3 to 6 years and a fine of triple the value of the drug if it involves substances that cause serious harm to health, such as cocaine or heroin. In the case of hashish, considered a less harmful substance, the base penalty is 1 to 3 years in prison and a fine of double the value of the drug. However, there are aggravating circumstances, such as the use of minors to commit the offense (article 369 of the Penal Code), which could increase the sentence to a range of 6 to 9 years in prison and an even greater fine. Additionally, the mother could face additional charges for corruption of minors or child exploitation, which would further complicate her legal situation.

The prosecutor RaÃºl PleÃ© presented a recourse against the ruling of the Chamber of Cassation that enabled conditional freedom for narcos (Guille Llamos). Prosecutor General RaÃºl PleÃ© presented a recourse of inapplicability of law to the Federal Chamber of Cassation to annul the sentence that declared unconstitutional certain articles of Law 24.660, allowing for conditional freedom of convicted individuals for serious crimes, including narcotics trafficking. The decision, taken during the judicial fair by a special chamber, generated a strong reaction in the judicial and political spheres. In response, PleÃ© requested that the Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation issue a ruling on the matter. The ruling in question was issued on January 28, 2025 by the Chamber of Cassation's Fair Court, with favorable votes from judges Ãngela Ledesma and Juan Carlos Gemignani. The resolution annulled a previous sentence and declared the unconstitutionality of articles 56 bis, inciso 10 of Law 24 Articles 660 and 14, section 10 of the Penal Code, both incorporated by Law 27,375. These norms established restrictions on conditional liberty for crimes considered of high gravity, such as aggravated homicides, kidnapping followed by death, human trafficking, and narco-trafficking. The Chamber of Appeals' decision benefited Carlos HernÃ¡n Beati, sentenced to six years in prison for being part of a gang that sold drugs in the municipality of Moreno under the facade of a remisserie. Beati had requested conditional liberty, but Federal Oral Court 3 in San MartÃ­n rejected the request, arguing that the reform of Law 27,375 prevented that benefit for his type of sentence. However, the Court of Cassation granted his appeal and ordered a new ruling, which opened the door for other convicts in similar situations to access conditional liberty. In response to this situation, prosecutor RaÃºl PleÃ© filed a petition requesting the annulment of the ruling and the convocation of a plenary session of the Chamber of Cassation to unify the jurisprudence. In his written statement, the prosecutor argued that the reform introduced by Law 27,375 does not violate constitutional principles, as it establishes a specific progressive regime for high-gravity crimes. Additionally, he argued that the differentiation in the treatment of those convicted of narcotics trafficking and other serious crimes is reasonable and justified by the magnitude of the damage that these illicit acts generate in society. The resolution considered key articles that limited conditional freedom in serious crimes such as narcotics trafficking to be unconstitutional (EFE) PleÃ© also warned about the need to maintain a homogeneous interpretation within the Chamber of Cassation, as the decision of the Chamber of Appeals contradicts the stance previously held by other chambers of the same court. In his opinion, he emphasized that the Chamber's jurisprudence has been consistent in ratifying the constitutionality of restrictions on conditional liberty in cases of serious crimes. The ruling that relaxed the application of Law 24.660 triggered a quick reaction from the national government, which is currently pushing for a hardening of the execution of penalties in crimes related to narcotics trafficking and organized crime. The Minister of Security, Patricia Bullrich, has expressed her position in favor of a more restrictive criminal policy and the strengthening of sanctions against narcotics trafficking. PleÃ©'s request for the Chamber of Cassation to issue a ruling in plenary session seeks to avoid the generation of contradictory jurisprudence within the court, which could lead to future requests for conditional liberty from other convicts in similar conditions. According to the prosecutor, this type of decision affects legal certainty and can have severe consequences in the fight against narcotics trafficking. Given the impact of the case and the controversy generated, Prosecutor PleÃ© also requested the intervention of the Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation to issue a definitive ruling on the constitutionality of the challenged regulations. If accepted, the country's highest court will have to determine whether to maintain the Chamber of Cassation's interpretation or reverse the decision, confirming the restrictions imposed by Law 27,375.

Rubio highlighted that many of the migrants crossing the Darien jungle and Central America actually have the United States as their destination. The head of U.S. diplomacy attended the takeoff of a deportation flight for 43 Colombian migrants at Albrook Airport. The aircraft is heading directly to the city of MedellÃ­n. Rubio emphasized that migrants are victims living a tragedy and that those who benefit are human trafficking networks. This migration has caused many problems in American countries. A 28-year-old Ghanaian man, who was convicted of sex crimes against a minor, was arrested by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents in Columbus, Ohio. The ICE announced that Joseph Osei Boateng was detained on January 29 at a Columbus prison. According to the ICE, Boateng entered the United States legally from Ghana in 2019. Boateng pleaded guilty on October 7 to two charges of unlawful sex conduct with a minor and was sentenced to three years in prison, minus 178 days, as per documents from the Franklin County Common Pleas Court. At the end of his sentence, Boateng will be required to serve five years of community control. He will remain in ICE custody until his immigration proceedings are resolved. This marks another arrest of an immigrant in Ohio's central region since President Trump issued executive orders to intensify arrests and deportations nationwide. Last week, U.S. marshals arrested a 23-year-old Honduran man in Delaware, accused of severe sex abuse and entering the U.S. illegally. An earlier report on that arrest can be seen in the player above. Trump said his administration is pursuing undocumented immigrants who have committed crimes. On Wednesday, he signed the Laken Riley Act, named after a nursing student killed by an undocumented immigrant.

Vatican City. Pope Francis closed the summit on children's rights held on Monday in the Vatican with words of gratitude for the participants, by turning the Apostolic Palace of the Vatican into an open observatory on the reality of childhood in the world, which is often wounded, exploited, and denied. His presence, experience, and compassion have brought life to an observatory and, above all, a laboratory, with various thematic groups that have developed proposals for the protection of children's rights, considering them not as numbers, but as faces, the pontiff valued, seated beside Queen Rania of Jordan, at the conclusion of the summit. Pope Francis also announced that to continue the fight for children's rights and to promote it throughout the Church, he will prepare an apostolic exhortation for children, a type of official document that the Pope usually uses to communicate his views, teachings, reflections, or guidelines to be taken. Among the attendees at the summit was Indian Kaylash Satyarhi, the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize winner, dedicated to the fight against child abuse. This is the time when we should learn to solve problems through compassion, Satyarhi said in statements to journalists, including EFE, before entering the summit. What happened to the women who practiced prostitution on the Silla Track? The southern entrance to the city of ValÃ¨ncia turned into a highway of terror on the night of October 29th. The median separating the lanes of the V31, known as the Silla Track, briefly halted the progression of the mud tongue towards the Albufera, but the water reached over half a meter, collided with the median causing a massive wave, and the cars and trucks floated out of control. Dozens of people spent the night with their heads submerged in water, many died on that highway, the majority abandoned their cars and like zombies walked towards the city at dawn. This same highway has been a very visible and known prostitution enclave for decades, both on the streets and in brothels. In fact, in 2022, several municipalities launched a municipal campaign to, as they announced, close ranks against the sex workers with police measures in that area. Now a large pile of cars, trash, and household items filled with mud recalls the scene. The pile is a continuous entry and exit of trucks to unload mud, leave household items or take away trash to specialized plants. It smells of humidity and rot and a cloud of red dust floats in the air. On the adjacent sidewalk, two girls share a chair, 100 meters higher there is a large brothel from which men enter and exit, further ahead another woman on another chair and if we continue along the same service road we arrive at a new motel, shiny, that has just been inaugurated. I am a survivor of the scene and I practice prostitution, this is how the audio of an anonymous woman begins. We lived on the ground floor and had to take refuge in a third floor. For days I did not want to leave the house, I could only cry. Months have passed and I'm not sure what will happen, I feel alone in this process, I'm unable to access aid. There are nights I cannot fall asleep, all I can do is move forward, concludes. What happened to these women in the area affected by the dana? Someone has cared for them, Teresa Meana, from the Feminist Assembly of ValÃ¨ncia, alerted the media before the start of the protest on 25N. There are sex workers in the areas devastated by the dana, of which nothing is known because they are neither identified nor reported, maybe their people didn't even know they were there. Dr. Andrea Sixto of MÃ©dicos del Mundo is the president of the autonomous delegation of MÃ©dicos del Mundo, an organization that declares itself abolitionist of prostitution and has been providing support and assistance to women in prostitution and sexual exploitation situations for over two decades. This assistance includes a mobile unit for street work, visits to flats and clubs, as well as a specific center offering psychosocial and medical assistance. Out of the 873 women they assisted in 2023, they estimate that around 30 are from the zona dana area. Initially, MÃ©dicos del Mundo's efforts focused on locating these women and verifying their well-being, or at least ensuring they were safe. However, they acknowledge that this task was not easy due to the women's mobility and the loss of contact with many of them. Of the 30 women, only three remain in the zona dana area, notes Dr. Sixto. Sixto notes that there is a pile-up of circumstances to which we must add those of the barrancada, and that each of these women is a different case with many specifics, the lack of social network for many of them, the administrative irregular situation of some (undocumented migrants), the lack of resources or the lack of registration to be able to request aid. For the women who were leaving prostitution and had been granted the Valencian income of inclusion, it was easier to stop, he tells us, having an income you can try to survive, but those who did not have any type of income had to get money from somewhere. The authorities rescued five potential victims of human trafficking in an operation conducted by the Philippine National Police Maritime Group (PNPMG) in Tawi-Tawi province, according to the police on Tuesday. The PNPMG identified the rescued potential victims of human trafficking as four minors and one minor female. On Friday, the PNPMG spoke with the five rescued potential victims of human trafficking who were on board a passenger boat traveling from Zamboanga City to Bongao, Tawi-Tawi. The rescue was carried out by the 1st Special Operations Unit (SOU) Maritime Law Enforcement Special Team (MLEST), in collaboration with the Tawi-Tawi Maritime Police Station and other associated agencies. The rescued potential victims of human trafficking, who did not have any identification documents, intended to travel to Malaysia via an illegal route. Based on police investigation, there is a suspect who has been identified as someone who has been offering work in Malaysia without the necessary legal documents. Based on police, the potential victims have already been turned over to the Ministry of Social Services and Development in Bongao, where they have received the necessary assistance and protection from local authorities. Meanwhile, the PNPMG continues to encourage the public to remain vigilant and immediately report any suspicious activities related to human trafficking to the authorities. The PNPMG emphasizes that collective action is essential in preventing human trafficking and ensuring the safety of the country's maritime domain. (B. Garcia)

JosuÃ© and Paloma were found dead in Florencio Varela. They had been missing since last Thursday. Two teenagers who had been missing since last Thursday were found dead in the last hours in the Florencio Varela partido in Buenos Aires. Police sources reported that the victims are Paloma Gallardo, 16 years old, and JosuÃ© Salvatierra, 14, classmates from Secondary School 63 in the area. The two minors were found dead under a bridge, near the Champion batteries factory, near the town square in Bosques. Although some sources reported that the bodies were restrained, this detail was not confirmed by the Police. According to the information provided, it has not been confirmed whether this was a double homicide or a homicide followed by a suicide. The discovery occurred in a sector of the collector that passes under the Bosques bridge, a dark and desolate area. On one side, the train tracks and the Champion factory, on the other, an empty lot that connects to Patagones Street. A feared site by the neighbors, which usually serves as a refuge for some people, and the lack of lighting makes it a dangerous place. The initial indications point to an improvised attack with the intention of stealing from them. It was something without planning, they were left with their few belongings, indicated the investigators. Among the stolen items are JosuÃ©'s backpack, both of their cellphones, and some money. Last Thursday, the parents of Salvatierra, who attended second year of high school, alarmed by the prolonged absence of the young man, went to his home and, due to the concern, they filed a report with 911. On the other hand, Omar Gallardo, Paloma's father, who was in fifth year, stated that his daughter was last seen on that same day when she headed to the gym, located about seven blocks from the square, around 6:00 p.m. The girl did not return home and by 21:00 they started to worry and think that something bad might have happened. The man made a phone report through the 145 hotline. I am concerned that behind the disappearance of these young people there might be a case of human trafficking, he said at the time, although this hypothesis has not been confirmed by the authorities yet. After intense searches, their remains were found under the bridge. Officers from the local police station and forensic experts from the Buenos Aires police force worked for several hours at the crime scene and up to this point the most solid hypothesis speaks of a double homicide.

Investigations Underway for 40 People in Large-Scale Operation Against Marijuana Cultivation in CulleraThe operation began several weeks ago after detecting several power supply cuts due to an overload in a neighborhood's grid, which raised suspicions among agents that the cause could be a criminal activity. The Civil Guard of Valencia is investigating 40 people after conducting 9 searches and seizing 100 kilograms of marijuana in a large-scale operation against drug cultivation in the municipality of Cullera (Valencia). The operation confirmed on January 30 that there were several illegal power supply consumptions through an amperage measurement, which determined 31 illegal connections. In this first phase, the agents marked one by one the homes whose consumption or addiction pointed to an abnormally high activity. Subsequently, a security device was deployed around the neighborhood where the marked homes were located, to prevent the possible escape of their residents. In the next stage, four teams were formed that performed simultaneous entries, and the operation ended with 9 entries and records in which 95 kilograms of marijuana in plants and five kilograms more in buds were obtained, as well as the production and distribution systems of these substances. In total, 40 people are being investigated for these facts, Spanish men and women between the ages of 21 and 51, for public health crimes (drug trafficking) and electricity supply fraud (a total of 39 crimes related to this activity). The proceedings have been handed over to the First Instance and Instruction Court number 1 of Sueca.

A 17-year-old Venezuelan girl was recently rescued from a human trafficking ring in Moquegua, Peru. The young woman, who had been lured under the false promise of a job, was exploited by the notorious criminal organization known as Los Hijos de Dios del Tren de Aragua. Her father, upon receiving a distress message from his daughter, managed to coordinate with Peruvian police for her liberation. The minor was deceived with a job offer. This is a common tactic used by criminal networks to lure young women. Once she arrived in Moquegua, the victim was deprived of her freedom and subjected to constant threats that prevented her from escaping or seeking help. For several weeks, she lived in a state of terror, unable to communicate with her family. On January 24, the teenager managed to send a message to her father, in which she cried out: "I am being held captive" The father, in his desperation, initiated a search, trying to negotiate with the captors first and then appealing to Peruvian authorities. The Human Trafficking Division of the Peruvian National Police carried out an operation at the Dubai Club, a nightclub where it had been reported that several young women were being exploited. The intervention resulted in the liberation of six victims, including the young Venezuelan woman. The reunion between the adolescent and her father was emotionally charged after days of anguish and uncertainty. Authorities were able to apprehend several of the kidnappers and closed the establishment, marking a significant impact against this faction of the Aragua Train, which has expanded its operations throughout South America, involved in criminal activities such as kidnapping, extortion, and human trafficking. This case highlights the gravity of the problem of human trafficking in the region. The conditions of vulnerability, lack of opportunities, and misinformation are increasing the number of young people who fall into these networks. Peruvian authorities have called on the population to report any suspicious activity, emphasizing that prevention and a swift response can be crucial in saving lives.

A 23-year-old man has been sentenced to one year in prison for kissing a 14-year-old girl without her consent in SabiÃ±Ã¡nigo. The sentence, issued by the Provincial Court of Huesca, allows for the possibility of replacing the sentence with six months of community service. The incident occurred in September 2022, just before the "only yes is yes" law came into effect in October of the same year. Due to this, the procedure was carried out under the previous legislation, classifying the crime as sexual abuse rather than sexual assault, with the aggravating factor that the victim was a minor. The defendant and the minor were friends and resided in SabiÃ±Ã¡nigo. At the time of the incident, the young man was 23 years old, while the girl was about to turn 15. The kiss occurred when they were alone on the street. Initially, the Prosecution had requested a three-year prison sentence, but after negotiations with the defense, the sentence was reduced to one year, with the possibility of replacing it with six months of community service. Defense attorney JosÃ© Ãngel LÃ³pez has reported that his client will attempt to fulfill the alternative sentence within the Zuera prison facility, where he is currently serving a sentence for a different crime. This case coincides with the start of the trial against Luis Rubiales, former president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF), for the non-consensual kiss to footballer Jennifer Hermoso during the 2023 Women's World Cup celebration. This process has brought to the forefront the debate on consent in sex-related crimes. The judicial ruling reinforces the criterion that kisses without consent can be penalized, in a context in which the legislation continues to evolve to ensure greater protection of people's sexual freedom and integrity.

Through an extensive investigation, the Larimer County Sheriff's Office identified the suspect as Christopher Kyle Shaffar (born November 11, resident of Fort Collins. Investigators executed a search warrant at his home in November 2023 After months of processing digital forensic evidence, investigators found over 3,700 graphically explicit images and videos of babies, children, and adolescents. They determined that the suspect knew and had contact with two children who appeared in hundreds of exploitation photographs. A warrant was issued against Shaffer for the following charges:Child Sexual ExploitationManufacturing Child Abuse Materials (F3)Child Sexual ExploitationPossession of Child Abuse Materials (Videos) (F5)Child Sexual ExploitationPossession of Child Abuse Materials (Images) (F5)Unlawful Child Sex Contact (F4)Invasion of Privacy for Sexual Gratification (F6)Shaffer was arrested and incarcerated in Larimer County Jail at the end of January 2025. By Ara Morales. The story of human migration is a constant phenomenon that has taken place throughout its history. Migrations have been motivated by various factors such as the search for better living conditions, fleeing war and violence, or the need to access better-paid education or work. Some of the historical events that have marked the history of human migration include the Industrial Revolution, this process gave rise to rural exodus, which involved millions of peasants worldwide. The Great European Emigration, between 1800 and 1950, millions of poor Europeans emigrated to the Americas, such as the United States, Mexico, Argentina, and Australia. Migrations in the Third World, from 1950 onwards, millions of people from underdeveloped countries emigrated to the United States, Europe, Canada, Japan, and Australia. The wars, wars have been a cause of forced migration, such as in the case of World War II in Europe and Asia, and in the wars in Africa. During World War II in the United States, they needed hands to attend to the fields, so the Braceros program was created, many of them went for temporary periods and returned to their places of origin, many others settled in the United States and there formed their families, but they have great ties with their places of origin. The factors that motivate people to migrate are diverse, including economic, demographic, social, political, environmental, and now we can add criminal violence in several countries. Cullera Tuesday, February 4, 2025, 0937 The Civil Guard of Valencia is investigating 40 people after conducting nine searches and seizing 100 kilograms of marijuana in a large-scale operation against drug cultivation in Cullera. In addition, 31 cases of electricity theft (illegal connections to the grid) were also detected, which could have generated a grave risk situation for the area. For several weeks, a neighborhood in Cullera had been suffering from apparently unjustified power outages due to the overload of the network. Given the suspicion that a criminal activity might be behind these outages and the risk posed to some residents by the repeated and prolonged cutoff of the grid, the Civil Guard deemed it necessary to carry out an operation to put an end to these incidents. The operation took place on January 30th, when several members of various units of the Civil Guard verified several illegal uses of electrical current at dawn. Through an amperage measurement, 31 illegal connections were determined. Several neighbors in the neighborhood had suffered recurring power outages due to the extremely high consumption resulting from the criminal activity. In the first phase, the agents marked one by one the homes whose consumption or connections pointed to an abnormally high activity. Subsequently, a security device was deployed in the surroundings of the neighborhood where the marked homes were located to prevent the inhabitants from fleeing. In the next stage, four teams were formed that performed simultaneous entries, avoiding to the maximum that upon being surprised or having knowledge of the operation, they could get rid of the crime instruments. While the records were being taken, rapid disconnections were made to the network in areas where there was also a risk of electrocution for citizens. Finally, the operation ended with nine entries and searches in which 95 kilograms of marijuana plants and five kilograms more in buds were seized. In addition, the systems of production and distribution of these substances were apprehended. In total, 40 people are being investigated for these facts, Spanish men and women between 21 and 51 years old, for public health crimes (drug trafficking) and electricity fluid fraud (a total of 39 related crimes). The proceedings were handed over to the First Instance and Instruction Court number 1 of Sueca.

A group of five men whose identities remain anonymous, referred to as the "John Does" or "Ring Boys," who survived sexual abuse, have filed a lawsuit against WWE, Vince McMahon, Linda McMahon, and TKO, alleging that they were manipulated and sexually abused by the ring crew head and ring announcer, Mel Phillips. In December 2024, we reported in Super Luchas that the case could be paused until the Maryland Supreme Court decided on the constitutionality of the Maryland Child Victims Act, that is, if the law were considered unconstitutional, the claims here cannot proceed. Embed from Getty Images More information Finally, it is confirmed (via Fox News) that the Maryland Child Victims Act is constitutional, so the lawsuit will be reinstated. The Maryland Supreme Court on Monday upheld the constitutionality of the state's Child Victims Act, which took effect in 2023 and eliminates statutes of limitations for individuals who were sexually abused as children to file lawsuits. Approximately 3,500 claims have been submitted thus far, and Maryland's payments on settlements could exceed $3 billion at a time when the state faces a similarly sized budget deficit. The law was challenged by attorneys for the Archdiocese of Washington, the private Key School in Annapolis, and the Harford County Board of Education, which have been accused in lawsuits of facilitating or covering up cases of child sexual abuse in the past. During a hearing before the state's highest court in September, the lawyers argued that a 2017 law, a precursor to the Law for Child Victims, prevented lawsuits against individuals who were not directly the perpetrators of the abuse, granting them a kind of permanent immunity that, according to them, was constitutionally protected by what is known as a statute of limitations.

LOWER RIVERBED Forty suspects in a large-scale operation against drugs in Cullera The Civil Guard of Valencia is investigating 40 people in 9 searches and seized 100 kilograms of marijuana in a large-scale operation against drug cultivation in Cullera. In addition, 31 cases of electricity theft were carried out. For several weeks, a neighborhood in Cullera had been suffering, apparently unjustifiably, from several power outages due to the overload of the grid. In view of the suspicion that behind these power outages there might be a criminal activity and the risk it posed to some neighbors of the repeated and prolonged cuts in the network, the Civil Guards proposed the need to carry out an operation to put an end to these facts. The operation took place on January 30th, when several members of various units of the Civil Guard checked several illegal electricity consumers early in the morning. Through an amperage measurement, 31 illegal connections were determined. Various neighbors from the neighborhood had suffered recurring power outages due to the extremely high consumption resulting from the criminal activity. In the first phase, the agents marked one by one the homes whose consumption or connections pointed to an abnormally high activity. Subsequently, a security device was deployed in the surroundings of the neighborhood where the marked homes were located to prevent the residents of the homes from fleeing. In the next stage, four teams were formed that performed simultaneous entries, avoiding to the maximum that upon being surprised or having knowledge of the operation, they could get rid of the instruments of the crime. While the records were being made, disconnections were made quickly to the grid in the places where there was also a risk of electrocution for citizens. Finally, the operation ended with 9 entries and searches, resulting in 95 kilograms of marijuana plants and an additional 5 kilograms of buds. The systems for the production and distribution of these substances were also apprehended. In total, 40 people are being investigated for these incidents, Spanish men and women between the ages of 21 and 51, for public health crimes (drug trafficking) and electricity fluid fraud (a total of 39 crimes related to this activity). The proceedings were submitted to the First Instance and Instruction Court number 1 of Sueca.

Former Celta de Vigo captain, Hugo Mallo, has been sentenced for sexual abuse after deciding not to appeal the sentence that found him guilty. In this way, the sentence imposed by the Barcelona Penal Court No. 19 becomes definitive, later ratified by the Eighth Section of the Barcelona Provincial Court. The facts date back to April 24, 2019, during the moments leading up to the Liga match between Espanyol and Celta de Vigo at the RCDE Stadium. Mallo, who was captain of the Galician team at the time, sexually abused Carme Coma, the person who worked as a mascot for Espanyol, by touching her breasts without her consent. According to the judicial resolution, the footballer acted with the intention of satisfying his libidinous mood and undermining the sexual integrity of the same. Despite denying the facts at all times and assuring that he would fight to prove his innocence, Mallo finally dropped the appeal, which confirms the conviction in an irrefutable manner. The sentence handed down in September by Judge Salvador Roig Tejedor imposed on the former player a pecuniary penalty of 24 months, with payments of approximately 7,000 euros per month, in addition to assuming the procedural costs, including those of the victim. The court emphasized the lack of a restraining act or remorse from the accused towards the victim, which led to the dismissal of the minimum penalty. In December, the Provincial Court of Barcelona reaffirmed the sentence in its entirety, stating that full conviction has been reached that the events occurred as the victim reported them, and that Mallo's declaration was contradictory not only with the victim's testimony but also with the images presented. It is worth noting that the sentence was not harsher because, at the time of the events, the reform of the Penal Code that would classify this crime as sexual assault had not yet come into effect. Currently, Hugo Mallo plays for Aris Thessaloniki.

According to the Observatory of Femicides in Argentina, Adriana Marisel Zambrano, 28 women were victims of gender violence in the country between January 1 and 31, 2025, equivalent to one femicide every 26 hours. The data show an alarming situation: 27 children and girls were left without a mother, and 49% of them are minors. Moreover, in 60% of the cases, the aggressor was the victim's partner or ex-partner, confirming that the most dangerous place for a woman in a situation of violence remains her own home, as 70% of the femicides occurred at home. In terms of geographical distribution, Buenos Aires leads the statistics of femicides, followed by Santa Fe, Mendoza, and CABA. Since 2008, The Encounter House has been collecting these data, becoming one of the main observatories in the country, whose statistics have been crucial in the elaboration of public policies and laws of protection. Key data on gender-based violence in January 2025 Five victims had previously filed complaints. Two perpetrators with a history of violence against women had restraining orders in place. Four aggressors were or had been part of law enforcement. One victim presented signs of sexual abuse. Two victims were migrants. Four perpetrators took their own lives after committing the crime. Two victims were murdered in the context of narco-crime. A homicide linked to a male adult.

text: The High Court of Justice of Andalusia (TSJA) has confirmed the conviction of a man for deceiving five women to engage in prostitution through fake contracts and forcing them with threats to engage in such activity, although it has reduced the sentence imposed by the Court of MÃ¡laga from 19 years and a half to 16 years and three months in prison, after partially granting the appeal filed by the defense. The sentence of the Andalusian high court states that the MÃ¡laga Chamber considered proven that between 2013 and 2017, the defendant contacted various women through the internet, offering them jobs, either as a model, as a companion, or as a domestic worker in MÃ¡laga. He also provided them with accommodation in his own home. Although the resolution pointed out, the work did not turn out to be the one offered, but once these women were in MÃ¡laga, where they had moved from their respective places of residence, they discovered that what the defendant intended was for them to engage in prostitution in that residence in exchange for a percentage. The MÃ¡laga Court considered it proven that these women were forced to perform such activity because they had signed contracts with the defendant and threatened them with denouncing them if they did not comply, and they would not be able to regularize their situation in Spain. In one case, he even managed to make one of the underage girls maintain complete sexual relations with him. Due to these incidents, they were convicted of several crimes of coercive prostitution, exploitation of prostitution, inducing prostitution, corruption of minors, and a aggravated sexual abuse crime with carnal access, imposing a global sentence of 19 and a half years in prison. In response to the conviction, the defense presented an appeal. Now, the TSJA rejects the majority of the arguments in which the defense requested acquittal, considering that the MÃ¡laga Court evaluated as determinant evidence the testimony of the victims, appreciating in them the absence of possible spurious motives, verisimilitude, coherence, and persistence, which is reinforced by the fact that we are not dealing with an isolated or punctual denunciation. At this point, it is clarified that five women are pointing to the accused as the person who, in some cases, forced them into prostitution, in others, profited from their sexual exploitation, and in some, obtained carnal access by bending their will to that effect, making it unimaginable that all of them would join in a kind of conspiracy or plot to falsely incriminate him. However, it is estimated that the argument that it is a single crime of corruption of minors and not two, and the one that urged to appreciate the undue delay, since the lack of notification to some accusations made it necessary to backtrack the proceedings to the state they were in three and a half years ago, causing a delay in the case. This implies the application of the circumstance that attenuates the penalty of undue delays, which involves the reduction of some of the imposed sentences. In the last few hours, the young man who had been detained after being accused of sexual abuse against a seven-year-old child regained his freedom due to a court decision based on lack of evidence and merit. To clarify, prosecutor Rodolfo Moure provided details of the case that is still shocking the community. The young man's freedom was requested by the prosecution. In cases of sexual abuse, we detain the person in two situations: one when there is flagrancy, that is, in the moment, which never happens in sexual abuse cases, and another when there is a risk that the person may escape. In this particular case, it was mentioned that this person was going to leave Balcarce for their profession as a truck driver, and their whereabouts would become uncertain. This motivated us to order immediate detention, which is what happened, without first hearing the victim. The victim had to testify three days after the arrest and did so, not confirming what we had been maintaining regarding a possible abuse. That is why the person was released by order of the Prosecutor's Office and will remain in liberty until the conclusion of the process, unless incriminating evidence is gathered that allows for their re-arrest. In this case, the young person is not acquitted, nor is it the case; they were granted liberty due to lack of merit, but the case continues. The person is not severed from the process; they are imputed in the case but in liberty due to lack of evidence. The young person can work and can leave the city to do their normal job. The judge imposed three conditions: one is to abstain from having contact with the victim, the second is to abstain from having contact with the victim's relatives, and the third is to establish a domicile; if they move or are absent for more than 24 hours, they must inform the judge. The prosecutor qualified the defendant's actions as imprudent for appearing in the media to give their testimony on the case. They are providing information from the case where a minor is involved, and we cannot reveal the victim's identity or anything that could lead to their identification. That is why we are cautious with the information we provide. This obligation weighs on the prosecution and the parties involved in the process, not on the defendant, if they prefer to speak publicly, that's their choice, but they can also face the consequences of possible harm and damage to the minor's family. As for the continuation of the case, the prosecutor stated that a medical expert report from the forensic doctors of Mar del Plata is required to determine certain issues related to the existence of the fact. Once we have this report, we will see if we can take the victim's testimony again. In the event that he may declare in a different way than he already has, because at first the minor was very distressed and he was able to say very little, we will see how to proceed. Regarding how this type of case is particularly lived in the Fiscalia, Moure stated that it is a situation that outrages and we try to be as prudent as possible and act in the fastest way possible.

Bangkok, 5 Feb (EFE). Thai authorities cut off electricity at five border points with Myanmar on Wednesday in an attempt to hit cyber-scam centers operating from the other side of the border, which have created a regional security problem with thousands of victims over the years. Pursuant to an order announced by the government on Tuesday, the Thai Electricity Generating Authority applied the cut in areas where they have identified telephone and online scam centers, where it is also presumed that victims of human trafficking were lured under deceptive job offers. The measure, which includes cutting off internet and fuel, will have restrictive effects on the supply of potable water in these areas, although the public Thai PBS chain assures that several of these centers have electric generators, so it is currently unknown how much this decision will affect the criminal gangs. Bangkok has reiterated that this action is a security measure against transnational crime and is only the beginning of a policy aimed at eradicating this scourge, now with the help of China, one of the points on the agenda of Thai Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra, on her official visit to Beijing, which begins today. The cybercrime centers, including those located in the Burmese populations of Shwe Kokko and KK Park adjacent to the border with Thailand, have taken center stage following the kidnapping of Chinese actor Wang Xing, which sparked concerns over security in the country that received nearly 36 million foreign tourists in 2024. The actor traveled to Bangkok in early January lured by a false job offer and was taken by a criminal gang to the Burmese side of the border, where he was rescued after several days missing. Following the commotion caused by this episode, the Thai government toughened its rhetoric and actions in an attempt to alleviate concerns and protect tourism, one of its main sources of income. The 20, 37 megawatt cut also comes after an unusual request from Myanmar's military junta, which has held power since the February 2021 coup, through an editorial published in state-controlled media, to ask neighboring countries for assistance in fighting these mafias. According to the figures provided in the article, the Burmese regime deported more than 53,000 Chinese nationals involved in online scams from October 2023 and the end of January. The rapid growth of illegal mining in Peru is severely affecting the economy. The surge in gold and copper prices has sparked illegal mining, generating multimillion-dollar losses for the country and financing criminal networks. The lack of state control and high international demand have enabled its expansion. The price of gold and copper has increased significantly in recent years, making illegal mining an even more lucrative activity. According to the Central Reserve Bank of Peru (BCRP), gold reached USD 2,650 per troy ounce, while copper reached USD 4.12 per pound. This phenomenon represents a severe resource drain, as illegal miners do not pay taxes or royalties to the State. According to economist Elmer Cuba of Macroconsult, illegal mining generates illicit exports worth up to USD 4 billion annually, depriving the country of key revenue for its development. The report "Integral Approach to Informal and Illegal Mining in Peru" from the Ministry of Energy and Mines (MINEM) indicates that 44% of Peru's gold exports come from illegal mining. This figure reflects the magnitude of the problem and the difficulty of eradicating this illicit activity. In addition to the economic impact, illegal mining has caused an environmental and social crisis. Deforestation, mercury and cyanide pollution, and community displacement are just a few of its consequences. The lack of regulation has also generated precarious working conditions and an increase in child labor. The Peruvian Institute of Economics (IPE) emphasizes that this activity is one of the main sources of funding for criminal networks. Human trafficking, money laundering, and chemical substance trafficking are directly linked to illegal mining in the country. In rural areas, where poverty and informal employment are high, many people see illegal mining as a quick way to earn a living. However, the lack of investment in education and formal employment perpetuates this cycle of illegality and environmental damage. Combating illegal mining requires a comprehensive approach that includes increased oversight, incentives for formal mining, and the development of sustainable economic alternatives. Without effective measures, this activity will continue to erode the economy and the country's future.

Today, the International Summit on Religious Freedom begins in Washington, D.C. Human rights defenders from around the world will gather to discuss how to combat the growing threat of religious and ethnic persecution. Samuel and Harut's families returned home and celebrated Christmas with a mix of joy and fear, aware of the uncertainty. As of February 2025, international passenger transportation companies will no longer be required to verify travel permits for minors. The measure, formalized through Directive 166 of the National Directorate of Migrations, was published in the Official Gazette and sparked controversy over its potential implications for the safety of children, girls, and adolescents. According to the regulation, long-distance bus companies, airlines, and maritime-flood transportation services will no longer need to request or control the documentation that authorizes the departure of minors from the country or the residency documents of foreign nationals residing in Argentina. The responsibility for these controls will exclusively fall on Migrations personnel at points of entry and exit to the national territory. The change, according to authorities, responds to the need to adapt procedures to new digital contracting and pre-flight check-in modalities that make it difficult for private companies to verify documentation in person. Nonetheless, the legal requirement to have corresponding documentation for minors remains in force. Families must present a travel permit authorized by a judge or competent authority, as well as a document proving the link between the minor and the responsible adult, to Migrations. In the case of foreign residents in the country, companies will no longer be required to verify precarious, temporary, or permanent residence certificates, or authorized stay documents, leaving this task to Migrations personnel. The measure generated criticism from sectors that warn of a possible increase in the risks related to human trafficking and the international abduction of minors, by eliminating a first preventive filter that was in charge of transportation companies. However, from the Government they assure that state control at borders will remain with the same rigor.

In a unprecedented move, the UK government has announced the penalization of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools designed to generate child sexual abuse material. This measure is part of an offensive against AI-generated abuse images, following warnings that such content was being produced at an alarming rate. The new legislation not only targets the possession of this type of AI-generated images but also pursues the means of production of this material. Among the measures are the penalization of possession, creation, or distribution of AI tools intended to generate child sexual abuse, punishable by up to 5 years in prison, as well as the prohibition of AI pedophile manuals that teach how to use this technology to sexually abuse children, with a penalty of up to 3 years in prison. Jess Phillips, Minister for Women and Girls' Protection and Violence, stated that the UK is the world's first country to legislate on AI abuse images and emphasized the need for global solutions to combat this crime. In an interview, Home Secretary Yvette Cooper described the phenomenon as truly disturbing and warned of the increasing and accelerating abuse, which is becoming more extreme and sadistic. The Home Office revealed that AI tools are being used to generate abuse images in several ways, including stripping real images of children naked or combining children's faces with existing child sexual abuse images. Additionally, the National Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Children (NSPCC, for its acronym in English) reported that its Childline service has received calls from distressed children who have found images of themselves generated by AI, using examples of victims who have been blackmailed and manipulated to continue suffering abuse. The government will also introduce a specific crime for those who operate websites sharing child sexual abuse content, with penalties of up to 10 years in prison. The UK Border Force will receive new powers to inspect digital devices of suspects at risk of child sex offenses. The measures will be presented as part of the Crime and Police Bill in Parliament. We know that the online activities of these sick predators often lead them to commit the most heinous abuses in person. This government will not hesitate to take action to protect the safety of children online, ensuring that our laws stay up to date with the latest threats, said Yvette Cooper.

text: Behind the cameras, the abuses against Colombian webcam models in BogotÃ¡ (AFP) Unhygienic rooms, shared sex toys, excessive shifts, denigrating clients' requests, harassment. For years silenced, webcam models denounce the abuses they suffered in Colombia, the hub of this multi-million dollar business. First modification Last modification The online sex industry showed its dark side behind cameras and thousands of kilometers away from their most frequent clients in the United States and Europe. In a luxurious webcam studio in BogotÃ¡, Paula Osorio recalls her beginnings in the industry five years ago under the yoke of unfair labor conditions in a country where sex work is legal. They set rules to do 12 hours of transmission a day, if they didn't deduct a percentage of the money I earned, says the 25-year-old model with piercings on her cheek and belly button. Similar reports were made in a Human Rights Watch (HRW) report in December that documented multiple psychological, physical abuses, and lack of hygiene in some webcam studios in Colombia, where the lack of opportunities heavily affects young women. According to the international NGO, there are thousands of studios and tens of thousands of women and trans individuals involved in this activity in the country, coming from poor sectors, single mothers, and without education. I thought that (economic fines) was normal within the industry, that all studios were like that, I started working there to eat and they abused me (...) because I had nowhere else to go, adds Osorio, who now works with better conditions. The devaluation of the local currency relative to the dollar makes Colombia one of the world's major centers for webcam activities, alongside Romania, according to experts. Garage StudiesBased on 55 interviews with webcam models, HRW found that most have been coerced, threatened, or forced into degrading, traumatic, or physically painful activities. In some cases, the lack of hygiene has led to skin rashes and other health problems related to the presence of fluids such as blood, vomit, and feces. The report also highlights the lack of transparency in contracts and the unequal distribution of profits. Almost all the women interviewed by AFP agreed that this last aspect has been traumatic, considering that most arrived in the webcam world seeking good and quick income, in a country with a low minimum wage (320 dollars) and a high informality rate (55%). The companions (...) are victims of violence within the studies, not all, reports Carolina Calle, a sex worker and human rights defender who heads the NGO CorporaciÃ³n Calle 7 A 40-year-old woman left her webcam modeling job a decade ago after experiencing harsh experiences, including having to share sex toys with other women. Cited press sources by HRW indicate that this business generated $40 million in 2021 in Colombia and that in 2020 there were 40,000 models. Webcammers' salaries depend on their popularity, but most earn more than the minimum wage. Since 2024, the government has been working on regulating this activity to ensure labor rights and combat tax evasion. The studies are not legally established as webcam companies, due to the lack of a norm. Although the report raised concerns in the industry, the demand for male workers also continues to grow. HRW's report put pressure on webcam entrepreneurs who only considered one side of the coin, according to Sergio Rueda, owner of the GoldLine studio. Rueda acknowledges that there are indeed garage-style shoots, that is, low-budget ones, but emphasizes that they do not represent the entire industry. Tired of the abuses, Darling LeÃ³n created a training center to instruct models on how to face them. It prevents them from getting involved in a scandal of rights violations, recounts the 28-year-old former model. But not all of them receive this type of training before entering this heavy industry, as defined by Tania RÃ­os, a 27-year-old mother of two young children and without a secondary education. The model remembers being forced to perform humiliating sexual acts, which she prefers not to delve into. If it's not the studio (the one that abuses), it's the client. One of the two sees the need and takes advantage of it, and sometimes one does many things out of need, asserts RÃ­os, who is now with a better agency. The interviewees report that they suffered or witnessed suggestive and even sexual abuse by their bosses. The abuses have led to depression, anxiety, and eating disorders, HRW affirms. According to Katherine Arroyave, GoldLine's psychologist, seven out of every ten women who arrive at her study have had bad experiences in the past.

In two separate operations, U.S. authorities arrested two Ecuadorian migrants, who could face prison time before deportation. Kail C., 27 years old, was detained in Jamaica, New York, by federal agents, less than a month after being released from a case of rape and sexual abuse in 2023. According to the U.S. Department of Justice, the Ecuadorian had pleaded guilty to a rape case in Queens, but was then arrested for his immigration status. The New York Post published an exclusive on the case of the Ecuadorian, with the headline "Migrant cut loose in plea deal after raping sleeping woman but then the feds stepped in." The Ecuadorian entered the U.S. in September 2016 on a visitor's visa, but remained in the country after his status expired in July 2021. He was accused of abusing a woman who fainted at a party in Jamaica on January 29, 2023. The victim reported the incident to the authorities. In his Instagram account, the Ecuadorian posted photos wearing the orange uniform of a detainee, after his arrest in the rape case. He could have faced between five and 25 years in prison if found guilty, but he pleaded guilty to another charge and was sentenced to reduced punishment. Stabbing in Marion In another case, 25-year-old Jordy T. was arrested in Indiana, sought for a stabbing that occurred in September in Marion, Massachusetts, which left one person seriously injured. The Ecuadorian is accused of intentional assault, armed assault, and using a weapon in the commission of a crime. Additionally, he is in the US illegally. He entered the US irregularly in 2022. He has a history of arrests for gun-related crimes in New York, according to federal sources. The stabbing incident in Marion occurred in September 2024. Investigators determined the Ecuadorian fled the state after committing the crime. Federal agents located the migrant in the 4300 block of Calumet Avenue, Valparaiso, Indiana, where he surrendered without resistance and no incidents occurred. Both Ecuadorians now await their court appearance, where their future will be decided, as they face serious charges and possible prison sentences before deportation.

In the last week of January, blockades were carried out in Madre de Dios, Amazonas, HuÃ¡nuco, Piura, La Libertad, Lima, Tumbes, ApurÃ­mac, and Lambayeque. From January 25 to 31, the Peruvian National Police and the Peruvian Navy, through the General Directorate of Captaincies and Coast Guard (Dicapi), in permanent coordination with the Specialized Environmental Prosecution Office, of the Public Ministry, carried out 24 blockades in nine departments of the country, in which they seized goods and materials valued at a total of 41,502,418 soles. All actions were carried out under the framework of Legislative Decree 1100, which regulates the blockade of illegal mining throughout the national territory. The largest number of interventions took place in Madre de Dios, where the PNP carried out eight operations and Dicapi, three. There were also operations in Amazonas (3), HuÃ¡nuco (2), Piura (2), La Libertad (2), Lima (1), Tumbes (1), ApurÃ­mac (1), and Lambayeque (1). The fight against the scourge of illegal mining continues unabated. The Executive is committed to eradicating this illicit activity that exploits natural resources, contaminates the environment, endangers the health of the population, creates holes in the Peruvian economy, and generates related crimes such as human trafficking. To this end, we are deploying a coordinated work between the Armed Forces, the Police, and the prosecutor's office, said Prime Minister Gustavo AdrianzÃ©n. The Dicapi focused its operations in Madre de Dios, specifically in the Malinowski, Pariamanu, and Madre de Dios rivers. Meanwhile, in that department, the Police acted in the Tambopata province, mainly in the districts of Inambari, Laberinto, and Las Piedras. Similarly, in Amazonas, the PNP intervened on two occasions in the El Cenepa district, in the Condorcanqui province, and in the Magdalena district, in Chachapoyas. At least five criminal gangs involved in this illicit activity were dismantled during the interdictions. In the interdiction operations, mining carts, suction bombs, detonators, drag boats, suction bombs, motorcycles, fuel containers, hoppers, metal cylinders, front loaders, a minivan, emulsion cartridges, safety fuses, carranchera boats, and compressor motors, among other goods and materials, were seized and destroyed.The Executive, through the Multisectoral Commission for the fight against illegal mining, led by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers (PCM), has planned to apply this year a strategy to combat illegal mining that will go beyond the interdiction operations, which will continue, and will cover an integral perspective that will give relevance to formal mining, the traceability of materials and explosives, and the promotion of alternative economies.

We reject the criminalization of migration and demand the removal of obstacles to the free flow of migrants' remittances to their countries of origin, which constitutes a grave violation of human and economic rights of the families affected by migration. We condemn the criminal organizations that promote and profit from migration, many of which are based or receive funding from the territory of the United States, violating human rights, taking advantage of the vulnerability of migrants, and subjecting them to risks, exploitation, and abuse. We commit to promoting coordination among the competent bodies of the ALBATCP member states and other bodies in Our America to dismantle and hinder the operations of human trafficking organizations known as Coyotes and demand that the government of the United States confront these organizations in their territory. We demand the lifting of unilateral and extortionate coercive measures that severely impact the functioning of economies, limit job and employment opportunities, and hinder the development of robust social security systems and the generation of productive capacities. We firmly express our unwavering support and absolute solidarity with Cuba in its confrontation of that Latin American and Caribbean sister nation to the new hostile and coercive economic actions imposed by the government of the United States. We also alert about the danger that poses to the peace and security of Cuba and the region, the establishment of a migrant detention center at the United States Naval Base in Guantanamo. We reject the use of this military enclave for these purposes, which usurps a portion of Cuban territory and has a long history of blatant human rights abuses. We express our strongest repudiation of the expressions of hate, racism, classism, and fascism that aim to plague Latin America and the Caribbean, with the sole purpose of dividing us and creating instability among our peoples. We reaffirm our commitment to the validity of the Proclamation of Latin America and the Caribbean as a Zone of Peace, convinced today more than ever to raise our voices in defense of the rights of the sovereign peoples of the countries of Latin America and the Caribbean, through dialogue, respect, and under the norms of International Law. A new report from the Observatory of Femicides in Argentina, led by Adriana Marisel Zambrano and directed by La Casa del Encuentro, revealed that during the month of January 2025, 28 victims of gender violence were registered in the country. The report details that 27 daughters and sons were left without a mother, of which 49% are minors. Additionally, 60% of the aggressors were partners or ex-partners of the victims. As previous records demonstrate, the most insecure place for a woman in a situation of violence remains her home, with 70% of the crimes occurring in the victim's residence or one shared with the aggressor. Regarding geographical distribution, Buenos Aires province leads the list with the highest number of cases, followed by Santa Fe, Mendoza, and the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires. Key data from the report Five victims had made previous complaints. Two female perpetrators were under preventive measures. Four female perpetrators were members or former members of security forces. A victim showed signs of sexual abuse. Two victims were migrants. Four perpetrators committed suicide after committing the crime. Two cases were linked to narco-crime. A case of a male adult was linked to a femicide. Since 2008, Casa del Encuentro has documented femicide cases in Argentina, providing essential data for the development of public policies and laws for prevention and protection of women and diversity. Pope Francis Urges Protection for Undocumented Children at US Border and Calls for an End to Nationalist Interests that Kill Children. At the opening of the International Summit on the Rights of the Child, held in the Apostolic Palace at the Vatican, the Pontiff called out against nationalist interests that kill children under bombs and condemned many of them to die as migrants at sea or due to violence between criminal gangs. He also attacked practices that are equivalent to murder, such as abortion, and denounced that many minors worldwide succumb to lack of care or various forms of exploitation. Abortion suppresses the life of children and cuts off the source of hope for all society, he claimed. The Holy Father also lamented that many more die in the desert or on the multiple routes of desperate travel. Killing the little ones is to deny the future. In some cases, the children themselves are forced to fight under the effects of drugs. Even in countries where there is no war, violence between criminal gangs is equally deadly for children and often leaves them orphaned and marginalized, he insisted. He also made it clear that not even the richest world is immune to injustice and noted the existence of other problems related to mental health. Pope Francis delivered his speech in the Clementine Hall of the Vatican. Credit: Vatican Media To a greater extent than in the past, schools and healthcare services have to deal with children who are already experiencing many difficulties, with young people with anxiety or depression, with adolescents who take the path of aggression or self-harm, he assured. In this way, he denounced the excessive individualism of developed countries and said that children in these contexts are also abused or even repressed by those who should protect and raise them. And he added: They are victims of parental fights, social or mental anguish, and addictions. Then, Pope Francis urged the present to ask themselves how a child's life can end like this. The Pontiff expressed himself in this way to different personalities such as Queen Rania of Jordan, Italian Senator for Life Liliana Segre, Holocaust survivor from the Nazi concentration camp of Auschwitz, Indian activist Kailash Satyarthi, Nobel Peace Prize winner in 2014, or Al Gore, former Vice President of the United States. It is not acceptable and we must resist habituation. Denied childhood is a silent cry that denounces the injustice of the economic system, the criminality of wars, the lack of medical attention and schooling, he indicated. In this way, he criticized certain media dynamics that tend to make humanity insensitive, provoking a hardening of general mentalities. We risk losing the most noble part of the human heart: pity, mercy, he lamented as he opened this event organized in the Clementine Hall of the Vatican by the Pontifical Committee for the World Day of the Child. Pope Francis denounces dramatic situations of childhood in the world The Holy Father used his address to give an overview of the grave situations that children face in many parts of the world. Pope Francis meets with children before the international gathering. Credit: Vatican Media In this way, he pointed out that over forty million children are displaced due to conflicts and that nearly one hundred million have no home. He also mentioned the drama of child slavery. One hundred sixty million children are victims of forced labor, trafficking, abuse, and all types of exploitation, including forced marriages, he stated. On the other hand, he cited the serious phenomenon of millions of migrant children traveling alone as well as the problem of not having legal documents. Many other minors live in limbo because they were not registered at birth. It is estimated that one hundred fifty million invisible children do not have legal existence, he noted after highlighting the practical consequences such as lack of access to education or healthcare. Additionally, he indicated that without legal protection, they can easily become victims of abuse or be sold as slaves. He also added: We remember the young Rohingya, who often struggle to be registered, the undocumented children at the border with the United States, the first victims of that exodus of desperation and hope of thousands who climb up from the South to the United States, and many others. In the same way, he criticized the logic of disposal in which human beings become omnipotent, and unborn life is sacrificed through the murderous practice of abortion. The Vatican hopes that this quote will help build a platform capable of addressing the most pressing issues related to the rights of children, while promoting international cooperation for a safer and more equitable world for children everywhere.

The method of attracting this vulnerable group to the facilities that have since been dismantled was by offering them false job offers to relocate to the border city The perpetrators used incentives such as clothing, jewelry, and cell phones to persuade them to join in the illicit activities, the commander of the institution stated, while indicating that five cell phones and other items used were confiscated.
